watchpoints: Heal week — hold loads, cut a set. Squat 3 sets, leg press 3, leg curl / incline RDL / calf raise 2 each. If a lift feels easy, that's the design — don't add reps or weight.
Squat holds at 75/side, run as a pyramid (8/6/8). The 6-rep middle set is the deepest, cleanest one — treat it as the quality set.
The Bulgarian split squat is new — introduce it, don't load it. Bodyweight or light DBs, 2 sets of 8-10 each leg, form-only. Smith machine if free; otherwise a bench and light DBs.
Leg press holds 3 plates — chase depth, not load. Full ROM is the work; the deep bottom position trains the core and QL.
QL/psoas watch. The cross-leg lateral lean is in the warmup for this. If anything in the QL talks during the warmup, modify the day — stop any lift that twinges.
Cool-down stays — 5-min block, hip/QL-biased on legs day.

sets.name: Warmup (incl. Cross-Leg Lateral Lean — QL/Psoas Release)

exercises.notes: Full depth, slow. Find where the hips are tight and breathe into it. Depth check before loading.

30s each side. Scissor one foot over the other, reach the same-side arm overhead, lean away from the back leg — the stretch runs down the side of the waist into the QL and lateral hip. Do this before loading the squat, especially if the QL feels tight.
Big slow circles. Wake up the hip stabilizers.
Spine mobility — slow, full ROM each direction.
Bodyweight. Use it as a QL check — if anything talks here, modify the day. Also previews the Bulgarian split squat pattern.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — the wrist dials a stretch up the back chain from forearm to lats to low back. A quick posterior-chain and low-back opener before loading the squat.
Set 1: 45/side x8. Set 2: 65/side x8. Same depth as the working sets.

**LOAD:** 75/side. Run as a pyramid — 8, then 6, then 8.

The 6-rep middle set is the quality set — make it the deepest and cleanest. Sets 1 and 3 at 8 bookend it.

**Cues:**
- Bar high on the upper traps (NOT the neck), upper-back shelf squeezed
- **Brace like prepping for a punch** — deep belly breath at the top, HOLD through the descent, exhale on the drive up
- **Hips back AND down**, not just down
- 'Spread the floor' — screw the feet into the ground
- Knees track over the toes
- Sit into the bottom
- Drive through the WHOLE foot

**Reflection:** does the 6-rep middle set feel like the cleanest, deepest one?

sets.name: Leg Press (3 Sets, 3 Plates, Full ROM)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 3 plates/side. 3 sets. Chase DEPTH, not load.

Full ROM at 3 plates is the work — the deep knee-to-chest position trains the core and QL at the bottom, not the leg muscles.

- **Foot position:** shoulder-width, mid-foot on the platform, slight toe-out — set before loading
- **Press through the WHOLE foot** — heels grounded
- **Full ROM** — knee toward the chest, actively pressing to keep the lower back from lifting off the pad
- Slow descent (3s), no bounce at the bottom
- Don't lock out hard at the top — leave a hair of bend
- If the hips lift off the pad at depth, that's too deep — back off
- **Breath:** in on the descent, out on the drive

sets.name: 🔆 Bulgarian Split Squat (Spotlight)

exercises.equipment: bench + light DBs — Smith machine if free (use smith-machine-bulgarian-split-squat)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** Bodyweight or light DBs (10-15lb at the sides max). 2 sets of 8-10 each leg. This is an introduction — the load is not the point.

The Bulgarian split squat is the program's unilateral leg lift. Rear foot fixed means no travel — more controlled, a better single-leg builder, gentler on the QL. Smith machine if it's free (`smith-machine-bulgarian-split-squat`); otherwise a flat bench for the rear foot and light DBs at the sides.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — drill the pattern every rep:**
- **Rear foot up on the bench** behind you, laces down or toes tucked
- **Step out far enough that the front shin stays roughly VERTICAL at the bottom** — too short a stance and the knee crashes past the toes
- **Front knee tracks over the front foot** — not caving in
- **Lower until the rear knee nearly touches the floor** — controlled, no dropping
- **Drive up through the FRONT HEEL** — the front leg does the work, the rear leg is a kickstand for balance
- **Torso stays TALL** — slight forward lean is fine, no folding over
- **2s descent**, own the bottom

**Reflection:** which is the limiter today — balance or strength? If it's balance, stay at bodyweight and groove the pattern. If the pattern is stable, light DBs are fine. Note any side-to-side asymmetry.

**QL watch:** still unilateral hip work — if anything in the QL/psoas talks, drop to bodyweight or cut to 1 set.

sets.notes: 2 sets, bodyweight or light DBs, form-only. The spotlight is the movement pattern.

sets.name: Calf Raise (2 Sets, Deep Heel-Drop + Slow Eccentric)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 3 plates/side, double-leg, on the incline leg press machine. 2 sets.

**Setup:**
- **Balls of both feet on the BOTTOM EDGE of the platform, heels hanging off the edge.** No plate under the foot — the platform edge gives the heel drop. This is a bottom-half-ROM movement.
- **Both feet on the platform** — double-leg

**Cues:**
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the heels drop as far below the edge as they'll go
- **Drive to FULL plantarflexion at the top**
- **3-4s eccentric** — the slow descent is the stimulus, not more weight
- **1s squeeze at the peak**, no bouncing
- **Breath:** continuous, don't hold

**LOAD:** 90. 2 sets.

**Cues:**
- **Ankles UNDER the pad** — the ankle bone is the contact point, NOT the mid-calf
- **Settings: 5/m/0/1** (verify before loading)
- **Lap pad locked DOWN firmly** — a loose pad lets the torso lift and turns it into lower-back work
- **Curl the heels toward the glutes** — full ROM, full squeeze
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze**
- Torso stays anchored to the seat, no lifting forward
- No bouncing out of the bottom

**LOAD:** 45lb plate. 2 sets. Dead slow with a 2s pause at the bottom.

**Cues:**
- Pad just below the hip crease (NOT the upper thigh, NOT the stomach)
- **Hip hinge** — a Romanian deadlift on the 45° bench, NOT a lumbar extension
- Lower back NEUTRAL throughout
- At the bottom, feel the stretch in the **hamstrings and glutes**, NOT the lower back
- Drive up by squeezing the glutes and hamstrings
- At the top, stop at neutral — past neutral loads the lumbar
- Tempo: 3s eccentric, 2s pause, 1s drive
- Take extra rest between sets if you need it

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Recovery Block (Hip/QL-Biased for Legs Day)

exercises.notes: 30s each side. Scissor the legs, reach overhead, lean away from the back leg — bookend the session with the same QL/psoas release as the warmup.
45s each side. Deep hip-flexor and glute release — the long hold is what lets the QL and psoas let go.
30s each side. Gentle twist for the QL — draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
45s each side. Front leg + back leg at 90°. Sink the hips toward the floor — hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Knees wide, arms extended forward. Parasympathetic shift before leaving the gym.

sets.notes: 5-min recovery block, hip/QL-biased on legs day — the chains that take the most load from squats, leg press, and the Bulgarian split squat. The cross-leg lateral lean opens it, child's pose closes it.

Three-part: spine primer → bodyweight work → deep stretch arc. Day-specific therapeutic add-on at the end (push = pec-minor protocol; pull = dead hang + scap pull; legs = pigeon + supine twist + the new cross-leg lateral lean; KB days skip — banded prep covers it).

sets.name: Primer — Wake the Spine (~3 min)

exercises.notes: Slow, full ROM each direction. Spine wave wakes the segment-by-segment articulation.
30s each side. Thoracic rotation + shoulder opener — reach a little further each week.
Gentle spinal extension — counters the all-day desk flexion. **Replaces W12's puppy-pose** in the primer; the extension wakes the back line.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Make tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and **hold the tension**. The wrist is the dial — a small internal rotation pulls a stretch up the whole back chain, forearm → shoulder → lats → low back. Slow, breathe.

sets.name: Work Block — Bodyweight Activation (~5 min)

exercises.notes: Slow walkouts — hamstring load on the way out, plank on the way in. **Rotates back in** (W11 had it) — full-body warm in one shape.
45s alternating. Plank with opposite arm + leg extension — anti-rotation. **Rotates back in** — different anti-rotation pattern than W12's shoulder taps.
45s alternating. From down-dog, draw one knee toward the forehead, hold a beat, switch. **Stays** — the core+hip+shoulder integration earns its place.
45s slow. **Stays** — durable hip opener under plank load.
30s each side. **Stays** — the windmill on the floor, the lateral-hinge cue translation.

sets.notes: Inchworm + bird-dog rotate back in for variety. Anti-rotation gets a different shape than W12.

exercises.notes: 30s each side. **Stays every week** — signature spine move.
30s each direction. Quadruped hip abduction — slow, full ROM.
30s each side. Hip flexor + adductor + back-leg quad. Drop to elbows if accessible. **Stays** — durable hip opener.
Bodyweight, slow. **Stays every week** — mirrors the Tuesday loaded cossack.
30s each side. Flowing entry into pigeon. **Replaces W12's static pigeon** — the flowing version for variety; the hip release still lands.
60s slow pulses. Adductor + hip opener. **Rotates back in** (W11 had it) — gentle pulsing release.

sets.notes: Continuous arc — flow between shapes, breathe deeply. Anchors stay (scorpion, cossack, lizard); pigeon + adductor work rotate for variety.

sets.name: 📍 Day-Specific Add-On — Pick by Today's Training (~3-5 min)

exercises.notes: **📍 PUSH DAYS — KEY PROTOCOL MOVE.** 30s each at LOW / MID / HIGH elbow positions. Arm bent 90°, forearm on the door frame, step through and rotate the torso AWAY. Desk work continuously re-tightens pec minor — daily.
**📍 PUSH DAYS** — active side of the pec-minor fix. Lower trap + rotator cuff.
**📍 PUSH DAYS** — serratus activation, helps unstick a tight pec minor.
**📍 PUSH DAYS (optional)** — slow rotator cuff work. Add if the shoulder feels off — worth doing this week with the right-shoulder cluster active.
**📍 PUSH DAYS (optional)** — pins the shoulder blades in the corrected position.
**📍 PULL DAYS** — 25s. Decompress the shoulders, warm the grip.
**📍 PULL DAYS** — scapulae retracting only, no elbow bend. Crisp scap engagement before loaded pulls.

**📍 LEGS DAYS — 🆕 NEW (W12D5 user discovery).** 30s each side. Scissor one foot over the other, reach the same-side arm overhead, lean away from the back leg — QL/psoas release. Do this before heading to the gym; it's also in the legs-workout warmup.
**📍 LEGS DAYS — W8 QL-SPASM PROTOCOL.** 90s each side. The long hold is what lets the QL/psoas release. **Non-negotiable on legs day.**
**📍 LEGS DAYS** — 60s each side. Gentle twist for the QL. Lacrosse-ball QL roll above the iliac crest beforehand if available.

name: Week 13 Pull — Heal Week (Spotlight: Bicep Curl + High Cable Curl + Cable Crunch)
description: **Heal week.** Same lighter week as W13 push — a symptom-driven back-off for the long-running right-shoulder cluster and accumulated soft-tissue tightness (one of several heal weeks this program, not a one-off). Not a 'deload' (the form-first cycle held loads) and not a calendar cadence. **HOLD all loads, CUT volume ~60-70%.** Spotlights rotate to the **curl + crunch finishers** (bicep curl, high cable curl, cable crunch) — the lightest lifts of the day, ideal heal week spotlights. **Trap-3 raise replaces the behind-back shrug block** this week (planned rotation) — the shrugs gave a strong first signal W12D3 ('crackly pop, then everything aligned'); trap-3 raises isolate the lower trap even more directly at a lighter load. **W12D3 takeaways baked in:** pull-ups all-slow on straight bar 8/6/6/5 ('felt great for the first time in a long time'); chest-supported row 35 'good and easy'; DB row held form at 80; reverse fly 30° reverse-incline variant clicked; face pull cue change was transformative ('like another exercise, neck feels less engaged'); high cable curl ramped to 170.

dayOverview.theme: Heal week — hold every load, cut every exercise a set. The curl + crunch finishers are the spotlight because they're the lightest work of the day; a heal week is the right week to drill cues with nothing heavy competing. Trap-3 raise replaces the behind-back shrug block on the planned rotation — same trap-chain intent, lower-trap isolation, even lighter load. Watch the right-shoulder cluster: if it's worse than W13D1 push, that's the structural signal — PT eval.

spotlights.why: The bicep curl is the W13 spotlight (tracker says 'preacher curl' — incline curl is the de-facto lift here, preacher bench is always taken). W12D3 had BOTH sides weak with 8+2 assisted on set 3 — but the user flagged they skipped the left-first protocol and there was cumulative fatigue before it. A heal week puts the curl on fresher legs: drill left-first, strict reps, full stretch + 2s pause. The reflection question: do the numbers recover when the fatigue ahead of them is cut?

W12D3 ramped to 170 ('approaching working weight; 180 would be hard but doable'). Heal week HOLDS 170 — drill the upper-arm-parallel-and-fixed setup instead of chasing 180. The pec-stabilizes-the-arm sensation the user noted is positional and fine.

Held at 130 (W12D3 done without comment). Heal week drills the cue that makes it an ab lift and not a hip-flexor lift: hips LOCKED, spine flexes, crunch from the abs only. Light, controlled, full attention.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W11 chest-supported row + lat pulldown · W12 face pull + reverse fly · W13 bicep curl + high cable curl + cable crunch (current, Heal Week) · W14 cycle back to pull-up + DB row.
watchpoints: **This is a heal week — hold loads, cut sets, resist pushing.** Pull-ups stay 6-8 but 3 sets not 4. DB row drops to 2 sets at 70 only (skip the 60 and 80). Lat pulldown, face pull → 2 sets. If a lift feels easy, that's the heal week working.

**Right shoulder symptom cluster — cross-check against W13D1 push.** If the line-of-sensation / grip-triggered pain is WORSE than it was on push day, that flips the working hypothesis from functional to structural — **book a PT eval, don't wait.** If it's the same or better, the heal week + trap-chain work is doing its job.

**Trap-3 raise replaces the behind-back shrug block** (planned rotation). The shrugs got a strong W12D3 signal; trap-3 raises hit the lower trap even more directly. Start VERY light — 5-10lb. The lower trap is small and fatigues fast. Same report-back: does it relieve or aggravate the shoulder cluster?

**Left bicep weaker than right** (W10D3 + W11D3). W12D3 both sides were weak but the user skipped the left-first protocol. This week: **left first, every set.** Strict reps only — no assist past asymmetry.
**DB row holds the MIDDLE of the pyramid (70), not the top (80).** Skipping the heavy 80 set IS the heal week for this lift — don't substitute it back in.
Cool-down stays — 5-min block, permanent every gym day.

exercises.notes: Scap activation. Squeeze shoulder blades together, soft elbow.
Spine warm — slow, full ROM each direction.
Active hang, not collapsed — engage lats, pull shoulders DOWN away from the ears even at full extension.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — the wrist dials a stretch up the back chain from forearm to lats to low back. Primes grip and the pulling chain before the bar work.

**LOAD:** Bodyweight. **This week: 3 sets, NOT 4.** Reps stay 6-8 (W12D3's all-slow straight-bar 8/6/6/5 was clean — 'felt great for the first time in a long time').

**Straight bar is fine** — W12D3 the user chose it deliberately ('wanted to get basics working') and it worked well. Stick with straight bar, or mix grips if preferred; either way:
- Active hang start, not collapsed
- Pull elbows DOWN to ribs, NOT chin to bar
- Chest leads to the bar at the top
- Eyes ahead, head neutral — no chin tucking
- **Slow eccentric, ~2-3s**, return to an active hang — the all-slow tempo was the W12D3 win
- Stop the set when the rep stops being clean — never kip

**Right shoulder watch:** W11D3 the front of the right shoulder lit up on a wide grip. If it talks, drop to a close or neutral grip set.

sets.name: 🔆 Station 2: DB Rack / Bench Block (Bicep Curl Spotlight + Chest-Supported Row + DB Row + Reverse Fly — Heal Week)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 35lb (HOLD — W12D3 had 35 available and 'good and easy'). **This week: 2 sets.** Hold 35 — do not push to 40 even though W12 said it had headroom; that's a W14 decision.
- **Chest stays GLUED to the bench** — if it lifts off, too heavy
- Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit
- Both elbows pull together — asymmetric = slow down
- 2s eccentric, 1s squeeze, no DB slam at the bottom

**LOAD:** 70lb (HOLD — the MIDDLE of the W12 pyramid). **This week: 2 sets at 70 only — skip the 60 warmup set AND the 80 top set.** Dropping the heavy 80 is the heal week for this lift; do not add it back.
- Chest-supported on the incline bench
- Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit
- Don't rotate the torso
- Slow 2s descent, 1s squeeze
- 70 should feel controlled and clean — W12D3 held form even at 80, so 70 on a heal week is honest practice reps, not a grind

**LOAD:** 25lb (HOLD). **This week: 2 sets.**

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — drill these every rep:**
- **Sit on the incline bench (~45-60°)**, back against the bench, DBs hanging at the sides — this is the de-facto curl (preacher bench is always taken; preacher at 12.5/side is the swap if it's somehow free)
- **Left arm first, every set** — W10D3 + W11D3 showed the left weaker; W12D3 the user skipped left-first and both sides went weak. The weak side gets the freshest reps. This week, no excuse — the heal week cut the fatigue ahead of this lift.
- **Full stretch at the bottom — pause 2s** (the user's own cue from W11D3)
- **Curl smoothly to a peak squeeze**, no swing
- **2-3s eccentric** — fight the long-head stretch
- **Stop each arm at strict failure** — do NOT assist past the asymmetry. A clean 8 beats 8+2 assisted.

**Reflection — the heal week question:** W12D3 both sides struggled (8+2 assisted), possibly from cumulative fatigue. This week the volume ahead of the curl is cut. Do the numbers recover? If left hits a clean 8-10 today, fatigue-ordering was the W12 explanation. If it's still weak fresh, the curl placement may need to move earlier in W14.

**LOAD:** 20lb (HOLD — 22.5 'doesn't exist at this gym,' confirmed). **This week: 2 sets.**
- **30° reverse-incline (chest-down on the incline bench)** — W12D3 locked this as the default form ('WAY better than the hunched-over version'). Set the bench to ~30°.
- DBs hanging fully extended at start, **soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED throughout**
- **Lead with the elbow, hand passive** — same pattern as the lateral raise
- **Wings out and slightly UP to shoulder height** — sweep, don't lift
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze** — no swing, no momentum

sets.notes: **One trip to the DB rack covers all 4 lifts.** Circuit or straight sets — your call. Bench at incline ~30° for the rows + incline curl AND the reverse fly (30° reverse-incline). 2 rounds, not 3 — this is the heal week.

exercises.equipment: regular lat pulldown (default, 140) — dual pulley fallback 70/side ≈ 140 if the machine is occupied
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 140 (HOLD — W12D3 confirmed clean on the regular machine). **This week: 2 sets, NOT 3.**
- **Wide grip near the bend** — more lat isolation, less bicep
- **Slight backward lean ~15°, NO further** — more = it becomes a row
- **Pull the bar to the UPPER CHEST — NEVER behind the neck**
- 'Lats squeezing oranges into the back pockets' at the bottom
- 1s pause at the contraction, 2s controlled return to a full overhead stretch
- Knees pinned firmly under the pad

sets.name: Station 4: Cable Column — Face Pull (Heal Week — 2 Sets)

exercises.equipment: cable column (mid/upper-chest height + rope)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** cable column 42.5 (HOLD). **This week: 2 sets, NOT 3.** Keep the W12D3 cue protocol — that's the lift now, the user said it 'felt like another exercise' and 'neck feels less engaged.'
- **Pull the rope to face level** — not to the chest
- **ELBOWS HIGH (above the shoulders)** — the make-or-break cue; if they drop, the rear delt offloads
- **External rotate at the top — knuckles point UP, like a double-biceps pose.** This is why the lift exists.
- **1s peak hold** at the contracted position — count it
- **Slow controlled return, 2s** — let the cable pull the arms back

**Setup: pick the cable column you'll finish the workout on** — the curl + crunch finisher lives at the same column. Slide the rope to the high attachment after this.

sets.name: 🔆 Station 5: Cable Column Finisher — High Cable Curl + Cable Crunch (Spotlight, Heal Week)

exercises.equipment: cable column (high attachment) — same column as face pull
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** cable column 170 (HOLD — W12D3 actual working weight). **This week: 1 working set per arm is the prescription** — treat the 2nd round as optional, stop at 1/arm if it feels complete. Do NOT push to 180; that's a post-heal week decision.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — drill the setup every rep:**
- **Single D-handle, one arm at a time** (the W12D3 setup that 'felt nice')
- **Stand sideways, arm out at shoulder level**
- **Upper arm parallel to the floor, FIXED** — if the elbow drops, it becomes an ordinary curl. The fixed upper arm is the entire point of the high-cable variant.
- **Curl the hand to the ear**, peak squeeze
- **Slow eccentric, no bounce at the start**
- The pec-stabilizes-the-arm sensation the user noted W12D3 is positional and normal — the upper arm parallel at shoulder level recruits the pec to hold position. Not a sign anything's wrong.

**Reflection:** with the upper arm truly fixed, does 170 feel like honest bicep work, or is the shoulder/pec doing the holding job? On a heal week, get this dialed at 170 before W14 considers 180.

exercises.equipment: cable column (high attachment + rope)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** cable column 130 (HOLD — W12D3 done without comment). **This week: 2 sets.**

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — drill the cue that makes this an ab lift:**
- **High attachment + rope** (swap from the D-handle — same column)
- **Kneel under the high cable**
- **HIPS LOCKED** — the single most important cue. The hips do not move.
- **Crunch from the abs ONLY** — the spine flexes, the hips stay put. Hips moving = hip-flexor work, not abs. If you feel it in the hip flexors, you've lost the cue.
- **Chest toward the thighs**, hold the crunch 1 second
- **Slow eccentric**

**Reflection:** at the bottom of each rep, is it the abs that flexed the spine, or did the hips fold? Locking the hips is the whole lift.

sets.notes: **The spotlight block — lightest work of the day, drilled deep.** High cable curl: 1 working set per arm (heal week). Cable crunch: 2 sets. Same cable column as the face pull.

sets.name: 🆕 Station 6: Trap-3 Raise (Replaces Behind-Back Shrug Block — Planned Rotation)

exercises.equipment: incline bench + light DBs
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 5-10lb DBs — start at 5. The lower trap is small and fatigues fast; 5-10lb is genuinely plenty. 3 sets.

**Why this lift, this week** (continues the W12D1 shoulder-shrugs discussion — see `docs/notes/functional-bulk/shoulder-shrugs-discussion.md`):
- Behind-back shrugs got a strong signal W12D3 ('crackly pop, then everything aligned'). **Trap-3 raise rotates in as planned** — it isolates the lower trap ('trap 3') even more directly than the shrug, at a much lighter load. The lower trap is the underused side of the upper-trap-dominant pattern.
- The shrugs and trap-3 raises alternate across pull days — don't do both the same day.

**Cues (drill every rep):**
- **Lie face-down on an incline bench (~30-45°)**, a light DB in each hand
- **Arms hang toward the floor, thumbs pointing UP** (external rotation) — the thumbs-up is non-negotiable, it sets the lower-trap line
- **Lift the arms into a Y — at ~135° from the torso**, NOT straight overhead. Raise until the arms are in line with the ears or slightly above.
- **Lift from the SHOULDER BLADES, not the hands** — the cue is the scapula sliding down-and-in, the arms just go along for the ride
- **1-2s hold at the top**, slow eccentric back to neutral
- No momentum, no bouncing off the bottom

**What to watch (REPORT BACK):** does this relieve the right-shoulder cluster the way the W12D3 shrugs did? Same hypothesis test — relief = functional pattern (keep going), aggravation = structural (PT eval). sets.notes: Closing trap-chain block at the incline bench. 3 sets, very light load, the cue is the whole lift. ~4 min including rest. Alternates with behind-back shrugs across pull days — trap-3 this week, shrugs return W14.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow position. Pec minor lengthen — the antagonist to the upper-trap chain loaded all session.
Passive hang from the pull-up bar. **Don't engage** — let the shoulders unpack and the spine decompress.
30s each side on the mat. Draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended. Breathe into the rotated rib cage.

sets.notes: **5 minutes of recovery work, non-negotiable closing block (permanent since W12D3).** On a heal week this is the connective-tissue catch-up window — give it the full 5 minutes.

Rest 2.5 min pull-ups, 90s DB block, 2 min lat pulldown, 90s face pull, 60s finisher, 60s trap-3 block.

name: Week 13 Push — Heal Week (Spotlight: Cable Column Block — Lat Raise + Tri Ext + Straight-Arm Pulldown)
description: **Heal week.** W13 is a deliberate lighter week — the latest of several across this program, since the right shoulder is a long-running issue — prompted by the W12D1 right-shoulder symptom cluster ('line from hand to shoulder,' grip-triggered shoulder pain) and the accumulated soft-tissue tightness of the first sustained training cycle. Spotlights rotate to the **cable column block** (cable lat raise + incline overhead tri ext + straight-arm pulldown) — the lightest lifts of the day, perfect for a heal week where the cue is the only thing being trained. **NEW: farmer carry** joins as a closing block (W12D1 shoulder-shrugs discussion outcome — loaded carry trains the same packed-shoulder pattern as the shrugs). **W12D1 takeaways baked in:** chest press 165 x 10 x 3 ran clean at the 3rd-station placement ('way easier when this is third'); incline DB went to 45 cleanly ('weirdly good no pain'); Kinesis fly 8 'stretching and relaxing everything.'

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W11 chest press machine · W12 lateral raise + Kinesis cable fly · W13 cable column block — lat raise + tri ext + straight-arm pulldown (current, Heal Week) · W14 cycle back to push press + incline DB to refresh.
watchpoints: **This is a heal week — resist the urge to push.** Loads HOLD at W12 numbers; every exercise drops a set. If a set feels easy, that is the heal week working as designed — do NOT add reps or weight. The point is to let connective tissue catch up to muscle (it lags 6-8 weeks).

**Right shoulder symptom cluster (W12D1) is the headline watchpoint.** 'Line from hand to shoulder' at 90°, raising the arm to 90° getting hard, squeezing the right hand triggering shoulder weakness/pain. The heal week + cool-down + shrug/carry work is the intervention. **If the cluster is WORSE by W13D3 pull day, that flips the hypothesis from functional to structural — book a PT eval.** Don't escalate push press load until it settles.
**Chest press cut to 2 sets at 165** — W12D1 confirmed 165 x 10 x 3 ran clean at the 3rd-station slot; heal week trims to 2. Hold 165, do NOT chase a 3rd set.
**Incline DB holds 45** — W12D1 went to 45 'weirdly good no pain.' Heal week: 2 sets, hold 45. Drop to 40 only if the right shoulder is loud on set 1.

**NEW: farmer carry closing block** — extends the W12D1 shoulder-shrugs discussion. The packed-shoulder loaded carry trains the same down-and-back trap pattern as the behind-back shrugs. Introduce light: 2 walks, 40-50lb DBs. Cue is 'pack DOWN not up.'
Yuri band red warmup non-negotiable. Doorframe pec stretch in the morning flow add-on.

exercises.notes: Slow, big circles. Wake up scap glide before loading.
Full sequence with red band. Non-negotiable on push day — extra important this week with the right-shoulder symptom cluster active.
Ribs down, glutes tight, body in one line. Slow eccentric, 1s pause with chest 1-2" off the floor. (Heal week: 10, not 12.)

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — the wrist dials a stretch up the back chain from forearm to shoulder to lats. Wakes the grip and shoulder line before loading.

sets.name: Station 1: DB Rack — Push Press + Lateral Raise (Heal Week — 2 Sets Each)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40/side (HOLD — W12D1 hit 40 x 10/10/8). **This week: 2 sets, NOT 3.**
- **Feet parallel, hip-width** — locked since W7
- **Ribs DOWN before the dip** — W12D1 flagged rib flare creeping in on set 2; on a 2-set day there is no excuse for it, catch it on set 1
- **Pack DOWN, not up** — shoulder blades into the back pockets, neck long. If you have to shrug up to lock out, the load is too heavy *for the cue* — that check matters more than ever with the shoulder cluster active.
- Shallow dip ~3-4", vertical DB path, head pokes through at the top
- Stop the set the moment rib position or the packed shoulder breaks

**LOAD:** 15lb (HOLD — W12D1 hit 15 x 20 x 2, slow eccentric 'super hard'). **This week: 2 sets, ~18 reps** (slightly trimmed from 20).
- **Lead with elbow, hand passive** — wrist follows, no wrist break
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED** through the rep
- **Stop at shoulder height — never higher** (past = traps eat the rep)
- **2s eccentric** — slow descent is the stimulus
- **Scap-reset between sets** — roll shoulders, engage/disengage scapula
- Massage the right pec between sets if the shoulder talks

sets.name: Station 2: DB Rack — Incline Bench (Heal Week — 2 Sets)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 45lb pair (HOLD — W12D1 hit 45 x 10 x 3, 'felt weirdly good no pain'). **This week: 2 sets.** Drop to 40 only if the right shoulder is loud on set 1.
- **Bench at 30°**, NOT 45° — forearm stack is automatic at 30°
- **Shoulders packed back AND down** — pin scaps into the bench
- Elbows ~45° from torso
- 1s pause at the bottom, no DB clack at the top
- This is a heal week — 45 should feel controlled, not a grind. If it grinds, the right shoulder is telling you something — drop to 40.

sets.name: Station 3: Chest Press Machine (Heal Week — 2 Sets at 165)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 165 (HOLD — W12D1 ran 165 x 10 x 3 clean at this 3rd-station placement, 'way easier when this is third'). **This week: 2 sets, NOT 3.** Do not chase a 3rd set just because 165 felt good last week — the heal week is the cut.
- **Seat height: handles align with mid-chest / nipple line**, set BEFORE sitting
- **Shoulders pinned BACK against the back pad** — the foundation cue
- **3s eccentric** — count it
- **Press to almost extension** — leave a hair of bend
- Massage out the right pec between sets — pre-empt the referral

sets.name: Station 4: Kinesis Cable Fly (Heal Week — 2 Sets)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** Kinesis 8 (HOLD — W12D1 'felt great, stretching and relaxing everything'). **This week: 2 sets.** This is the lift that loosens the right shoulder — protect it even on a heal week.
- **Slight forward hinge at hips** — chest leads, not head
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED throughout** — not a press, not a curl
- **"Hug a tree"** — squeeze from the chest, not the arms
- **Slow eccentric (~3s)** — let the cables pull the arms back for the deep pec stretch
- **Stretch is the stimulus** — W12D1 said the shoulder felt good at the stretch; that's the cue

sets.name: 🔆 Station 5: Cable Column Block — Lat Raise → Tri Ext → Straight-Arm Pulldown (Spotlight, Heal Week — 2 Rounds)

exercises.equipment: cable column (default — W12D1 setup) — Kinesis 3 fallback if column is occupied
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** cable column ~30-40lb (HOLD — form-first range). **This week: 2 rounds, one arm at a time.**

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — drill the W12D1 cue interaction every rep:**
- W12D1 observation: **'if I lead with elbow and focus on back, I feel it in the elbow even tho not using it at all.'** That sensation means the elbow is becoming a load path it shouldn't be.
- **Lead with the elbow as a DIRECTION, not a lever** — the elbow points the way the arm travels; it does not bend, extend, or grip. If you feel the elbow *working*, you've turned a direction cue into a joint action. Reset: soft elbow, fixed angle, let the medial delt lift the whole arm as one unit.
- **Soft elbow ~10°, FIXED throughout** — the angle never changes from start to top
- **Stand sideways to the column**, working arm farther from the stack
- **Stop at shoulder height — higher = traps**
- **Fight the cable on the way down**, no snap-back, 2s eccentric
- **Massage the right pec between sets** — kills the crackle
- **Skip 'run line behind body' cue** — doesn't apply at this gym's geometry

**Reflection:** by round 2, is the elbow quiet (just pointing) or is it still 'feeling' the rep? If it's still feeling it, slow down and lighten — the heal week is the week to get this clean.

exercises.equipment: cable column kneeling (default — W12D1 working number) — Kinesis 5 fallback if column is occupied
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** cable column 70 (HOLD — W12D1 locked 70 as the working number; 50 was too easy). **This week: 2 rounds.**

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — drill the setup every rep:**
- **Kneel facing AWAY from the high pulley**, rope overhead
- **Torso slightly forward — that's the 'incline.'** It biases the long head; without the forward lean it's an ordinary pressdown.
- **Elbows PINNED** — only the forearms move. The elbow is the hinge and nothing else. If the elbows drift forward or flare, the long head offloads.
- **Hands shoulder-width on the rope** (long-head emphasis)
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the rope pull the hands behind the head
- **Stop just shy of lockout**, slow eccentric

**Reflection:** at round 2, are the elbows still pinned in the same spot they started, or have they crept forward? The pin is the lift.

exercises.equipment: cable column (default — W12D1 setup) — Kinesis 6 ≈ cable column 100 fallback
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** cable column 100 (HOLD — W12D1 working number, done clean 'no specifics needed'). **This week: 2 rounds.**

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — drill the cues that keep this from becoming a lat pulldown:**
- **Stand a step back, hinge ~15° at the hips** — fixed hinge, the torso doesn't pump
- **Slight elbow bend (~5°), FIXED throughout** — perfectly straight arms = elbow risk; bending arms = it becomes a pulldown. The elbow holds ONE angle the whole set.
- **Pull the bar to the thighs, NOT past** — past the thighs the shoulders roll forward and the lats switch off
- **Squeeze the lats hard at the bottom** — 'oranges into the back pockets'
- **Slow controlled return to a full overhead stretch** — the stretch at the top is half the lift

**Reflection:** does it feel like a straight-arm lat movement, or has the elbow started bending to help? If the elbow is bending, that's the lat tapping out — stop the set.

sets.notes: **The spotlight block — and the lightest work of the day, which is exactly why it's the heal week spotlight.** Nothing here is heavy; the entire training effect this week is the quality of the cue. One trip to the cable column covers all three (slide the attachment between exercises). 2 rounds, not 3.

sets.name: 🆕 Station 6: Farmer Carry (NEW — W12D1 shoulder-shrugs discussion outcome)

exercises.equipment: DB rack
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40-50lb DBs — start at 40, this is an introduction. **2 walks of ~30-45s.**

**Why this lift, now** (W12D1 shoulder-shrugs discussion — see `docs/notes/functional-bulk/shoulder-shrugs-discussion.md`):
- The behind-back shrugs gave a strong first signal W12D3 ('crackly pop, then everything aligned'). Farmer carry trains the **same packed-shoulder pattern** under a different stimulus — the traps engage tonically to hold the shoulder packed while you walk.
- It directly drills the **'pack DOWN, not up'** correction the user flagged W12D1.

**Cues (drill every step):**
- **Stand TALL** — ribs down, crown of the head reaching up
- **Shoulders pulled DOWN and BACK** — into the back pockets, NEVER shrugged toward the ears. This is the whole point of the lift. The DBs will try to pull the shoulders up; resist that the entire walk.
- **Neck long, eyes forward** — no chin poke
- **Walk a straight line at a deliberate pace**, breathing steadily — don't rush
- **Grip firm but not death-clenched** — note whether a hard right-hand squeeze provokes the shoulder (W12D1 grip→shoulder coupling watch)

**What to watch (REPORT BACK):** does keeping the shoulder packed under the carry feel like it RELIEVES the right-shoulder cluster (like the shrugs did), or aggravate it? Same hypothesis test as the shrugs — relief = functional pattern, aggravation = structural, escalate to PT.

**heal week note:** keep this genuinely light — 2 walks, 40lb. It's a new lift in a heal week; build the cue, the load comes later.

sets.notes: Quick closing block at the DB rack on the way to the cool-down. 2 walks, ~30-45s each, light load. Focus is the packed-shoulder posture, not the weight. Total ~3 min including rest.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow position. Arm bent 90°, forearm on the door frame, step through + rotate the torso AWAY. Pec minor lengthen — the antagonist to the upper-trap chain that's been loaded all session.
Passive hang from the pull-up bar. **Don't engage** — let the shoulders unpack and the spine decompress. Especially valuable this week for the right-shoulder cluster.
30s each side on the mat. Lie back, draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended. Breathe into the rib cage on the rotated side.
45s each side. Front leg + back leg at 90°. Sink hips toward the floor — hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Knees wide, big toes touching, arms extended forward. Breathe into the back ribs — parasympathetic shift before leaving the gym.

sets.notes: **5 minutes of recovery work, non-negotiable closing block (permanent since W12D3).** On a heal week this block matters even more — it's the connective-tissue-catch-up window. Goes after the last lift, before walking out.

tips: **Heal week — hold every load, cut every exercise a set.** Not the first — the right shoulder has prompted lighter stretches before; this is routine maintenance, not a setback. If something feels easy, that's the design. Do not add reps or weight.

**Spotlight: the cable column block** (cable lat raise + incline overhead tri ext + straight-arm pulldown) — the lightest work of the day, drilled deep because a heal week has nothing else competing for attention.
**Cable lat raise: 'lead with elbow' is a DIRECTION, not a joint action.** If you feel the elbow working, you've corrupted the cue (W12D1 observation). Reset to a fixed soft elbow.
**Right shoulder symptom cluster is the headline watchpoint.** If it's worse by W13D3 pull day, the hypothesis flips to structural — book a PT eval.
**Chest press 2 sets at 165, incline DB 2 sets at 45** — both held from W12D1's clean numbers. Heal week trims the volume, not the load.
**Pack DOWN, not up** — push press, incline DB, chest press, lateral raise, farmer carry all carry the cue. If you must shrug up to finish a rep, the load is too heavy for the cue — drop it.

**NEW: farmer carry closing block** — 2 walks, 40-50lb DBs, 'tall posture, packed shoulders, breathe.' Extends the trap-chain work the shrugs started. Report whether it relieves or aggravates the right shoulder.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, permanent every gym day.** On a heal week it's the connective-tissue catch-up window.
Yuri band red warmup non-negotiable. Doorframe pec stretch in the morning flow add-on.
Rotation plan: W14 cycles back to push press + incline DB to refresh those cues.
Rest 2 min DB rack work, 2.5 min chest press, 75s cables + carry.
formPhilosophy: Heal week — a deliberate lighter week for the shoulder and soft tissue, not a deload and not a calendar ritual. The training effect this week is NOT load; it's letting connective tissue catch up to muscle (it lags 6-8 weeks) and drilling cues with the volume turned down. The cable column spotlight, the cool-down, and the new farmer carry all serve recovery and pattern quality. Building decades, not weeks.

Control on the way down — bell to the floor as cleanly as it came up. Closes the flow before switching sides.

sets.name: 🔆 Figure-8 → Tactical Clean Flow (Spotlight)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 25lb. 3 rounds of 60s continuous flow.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the exit-into-clean cue:**
- **START in the hike position** (bell between the legs, hinged at the hips)
- **Figure-8 → exit into a tactical clean to rack** — pass between the legs, hand catches BEHIND, the pull becomes the clean
- **The figure-8 EXITS into the clean** — the bell does not return to a hand mid-pass; the catch becomes the clean. This is the skill.
- Lower the bell back through the hike position; the next pass switches sides
- Continue alternating for the full 60s

**Cues:**
- **Tactical clean = controlled, threaded into the rack** — no yank, no forearm slam
- **Hike is home base** — every transition resets through hike
- **Right shoulder watch on the rack catch** — if it talks, drop to figure-8 passes only and finish the round

**Reflection:** does the pass→clean feel like one motion, or two? The skill is the seamless transition — if there's a hand catch between the pass and the clean, the cue's broken.

**Dose: 3 rounds at 25lb.** Volume restored from W13's 2 rounds — this is the spotlight, deeper drill at slightly more volume.

sets.name: Asgooch Overhead Flow — Alternating Sides (Flow, NOT Reps)

exercises.notes: Single hand. Controlled pull, full extension, hips hinged, back flat.

Bell locked overhead. **Hardest move in the flow.** Full depth IF mobility allows; reduce depth before load if it limits.

Bell overhead. **Lock elbow, bell over shoulder, torso TALL.** Drive through the front HEEL. **Right shoulder watchpoint** — most likely place for the crackle; modify to a front-rack lunge on this move only if it talks.

- Set 2 at 7: same depth, one more rep. The 'build courage' step.

**Cues:**
- Bar high on the upper traps (NOT the neck), upper-back shelf squeezed

- **Hips back AND down**, not just down
- 'Spread the floor' — screw the feet into the ground
- Knees track over the toes
- Sit into the bottom
- Drive through the WHOLE foot

sets.name: Leg Press + Calf Raise Station (Same Machine — W13D5 Station-Grouping Rule)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 3 plates/side (HELD). 4 sets of 12. Chase DEPTH, not load.

Full ROM at 3 plates is the work — the deep knee-to-chest position trains the abs/QL (W12D5 + W13D5 confirmed the soreness pattern).

- **Foot position:** shoulder-width, mid-foot on the platform, slight toe-out — set before loading
- **Press through the WHOLE foot** — heels grounded
- **Full ROM** — knee toward the chest, actively pressing to keep the lower back from lifting off the pad
- Slow descent (3s), no bounce at the bottom
- Don't lock out hard at the top — leave a hair of bend
- If the hips lift off the pad at depth, that's too deep — back off
- **Breath:** in on the descent, out on the drive

sets.name: Leg-Press Calf Raise (Same Machine — Stays Right Here)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 3 plates/side (HELD). 3 sets of 15. Stay on the leg press — this is why station-grouping matters.

**Setup:**
- **Balls of both feet on the BOTTOM EDGE of the platform, heels hanging off the edge.** No plate under the foot — the platform edge gives the heel drop on its own.
- **Both feet on the platform** — double-leg

**Cues:**
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the heels drop as far below the edge as they'll go
- **Drive to FULL plantarflexion at the top**
- **3-4s eccentric** — the slow descent is the stimulus, not added load
- **1s squeeze at the peak**, no bouncing
- **Breath:** continuous, don't hold

W13D5 'felt easy this time even with slow eccentrics, feel great.' If it still feels easy at slow tempo, the W15 conversation is moving to single-leg + slow (W10D5 trap caveat — only when the eccentric is dialed in).

sets.name: Bulgarian Split Squat (Bench Station — Step Up to Light DBs)

exercises.equipment: bench + light DBs at the sides — Smith machine if free (use smith-machine-bulgarian-split-squat)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** Light DBs **15-20lb pair at the sides**, step up from W13D5's bodyweight intro. 3 sets of 8-10 each leg (volume restored from W13's 2 sets). W13D5: 'felt fine no twitching or spawning... happy to go up after this.'

**Cues (carry from W13D5 intro):**
- **Rear foot up on the bench** behind you, laces down or toes tucked
- **Step out far enough that the front shin stays roughly VERTICAL at the bottom** — too short a stance = knee crashes past the toes
- **Front knee tracks over the front foot** — not caving in
- **Lower until the rear knee nearly touches the floor** — controlled, no dropping
- **Drive up through the FRONT HEEL** — the front leg does the work, the rear leg is a kickstand for balance
- **Torso stays TALL** — slight forward lean is fine, no folding over
- **2s descent**, own the bottom

**Watch:** if anything twitches/spasms (W13D5 prior-attempt lesson — going too heavy too fast triggered spasms before), drop to bodyweight for the remaining sets and finish. The DB step-up is conservative for a reason.

**LOAD:** 90 (HELD). 3 sets of 12. Slow tempo — W13D5 'feel these deeply when doing it slowly' is the cue.

**Cues:**
- **Ankles UNDER the pad** — the ankle bone is the contact point, NOT the mid-calf
- **Settings: 5/m/0/1** (verify before loading)
- **Lap pad locked DOWN firmly** — loose pad lets the torso lift and turns it into lower-back work
- **Curl the heels toward the glutes** — full ROM, full squeeze
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze**
- Torso stays anchored to the seat, no lifting forward
- No bouncing out of the bottom

**LOAD:** 45lb plate (HELD). 3 sets of 15. Dead slow with a 2s pause at the bottom.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — drill the hip-hinge cues, the tempo is the progression:**
- **Pad just below the hip crease** — NOT on the upper thigh, NOT on the stomach
- **Hip hinge** — Romanian deadlift on the 45° bench, NOT a lumbar extension
- Lower back NEUTRAL throughout
- **At the bottom:** stretch in the **hamstrings and glutes**, NOT the lower back. If the lumbar rounds, you're going too deep for current mobility.
- Drive up by squeezing the glutes and hamstrings
- **At the top:** stop at neutral. Past neutral = lumbar load = QL irritation.
- **Tempo: 3s eccentric, 2s pause at the bottom, 1s drive up.** The slow eccentric is the entire reason this lift works.
- Take extra rest between sets if you need it

**Reflection:** at 45lb dead slow for 3 sets restored, where is the stretch landing — hamstrings/glutes (correct) or lower back (too deep / pad placement off)? If lower back, slow down further and check pad position before set 2.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Recovery Block (Hip/QL-Biased for Legs Day)

exercises.notes: 30s each side. Scissor the legs, reach overhead, lean away from the back leg — bookend the session with the same QL/psoas release as the warmup.

- **DBs racked on front delts**, elbows up just enough to keep them pinned

- **Vertical DB path** — DBs travel parallel up next to the ears, head pokes through at the top
- **Drive fast, lockout solid, descent controlled**
- **Breath:** in at the dip, out on the drive

sets.name: Station 7: Farmer Carry (3 Walks)

exercises.equipment: DB rack
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40-50lb DBs. 3 walks of ~30-45s each.
- **Stand TALL** — ribs down, crown of the head reaching up
- **Shoulders pulled DOWN and BACK** — into the back pockets, never shrugged toward the ears. The DBs will try to pull the shoulders up; resist the entire walk.
- **Neck long, eyes forward** — no chin poke
- **Walk a straight line at a deliberate pace**, breathing steadily — don't rush
- **Grip firm but not death-clenched** — W13D1 found a hard right-hand squeeze provokes the shoulder; firm-but-relaxed grip is the cue

**Watch:** does the carry continue to feel neutral on the right shoulder (like W13D1's 'grip is the hardest part'), or has it shifted? Log if the shoulder talks at any specific load.

sets.notes: Closing trap-chain block. 3 walks at 40-50lb, light load, packed-shoulder posture is the lift.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow position. Pec minor lengthen — the antagonist to the upper-trap chain loaded all session.
Passive hang from the pull-up bar. **Don't engage** — let the shoulders unpack and the spine decompress.
30s each side on the mat. Draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
45s each side. Front leg + back leg at 90°. Sink hips toward the floor — hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Knees wide, arms extended forward. Parasympathetic shift before leaving the gym.

sets.notes: 5 minutes of recovery work, non-negotiable closing block.

sets.name: OTD Flow (Light Groove — Skill Practice)

exercises.notes: Bell starts on the floor between the feet, hips drive the lift, catch in the rack with the knees slightly bent.
Goblet/rack position. **LIGHT** — Thursday before Friday legs, keep depth without grinding. Sit tall, full depth, no bouncing.
Stride out wide, sit into the working leg, keep the other leg long. Mobility, not strength.

The deliberate leverage move inside the flow — **the body goes DOWN, the bell barely moves.** From the rack, hinge and rotate AWAY from the bell side, eyes tracking the bell, until the arm locks out overhead — you lower your body under the bell, you don't press it up. Slow and smooth; it's leverage, not a press.
Control on the way down — bell to the floor as cleanly as it came up. Closes the flow before switching sides.

sets.notes: **This is a continuous FLOW, not separate stations.** Move through the full chain on ONE side — dead clean → front squat → lateral lunge → bent press → tactical clean — letting each move feed the next, then repeat the whole flow on the other side. sets.name: 🔆 Windmill (Spotlight — Lateral-Hinge Mobility)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 18-20lb. 3 rounds, 5 each side. Light — this is mobility under load, not a strength lift.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the lateral hinge, clean:**
- **Bell locked overhead, arm vertical, eyes track the bell** the entire rep — the bell never leaves your sight
- **Hip hinge AWAY from the bell side** — push the hip out toward the bell-arm side, fold over the front leg
- **The stretch lives in the back leg's hip flexor / hamstring and the side of the waist — NOT the lower back.** If you feel it in the lumbar, you're bending the spine instead of hinging the hip
- **Long spine throughout** — the bend is at the hip, the spine stays long (no crunching down)
- **Free hand reaches down the inside of the front leg** toward the floor as the torso lowers
- **Slow descent, brief pause at the bottom, controlled return** — own every inch

**Reflection:** can you keep the stretch in the hip/waist and OUT of the lower back for all 3 rounds? This is the same lateral-hinge pattern as the bent press in the OTD flow — drilling it clean here should make the bent press feel more like leverage and less like a press.

sets.notes: Spotlight mobility flow. 3 rounds at 18-20lb, ~5 min including rest. Light bell — range and clean hinge mechanics are the work.

**LOAD:** 45. 3 rounds, 5 each side.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — drill the clean-catch and the press:**
- **Catch the clean with the knees slightly bent** — absorb the bell, zero impact at the rack
- **Hips drive the clean**, NOT the arm — the arm just guides the bell into the rack

sets.name: Asgooch Overhead Flow — Alternating Sides (Flow, NOT Reps)

Bell locked overhead. **Hardest move in the flow.** Full depth IF mobility allows; reduce depth before load if it limits.

Bell overhead. **Lock the elbow, bell over the shoulder, torso TALL.** Drive through the front HEEL. **Right shoulder watchpoint** — most likely place for the crackle; sub a front-rack lunge on this move only if it talks.
**Dip and drive** — legs do the work, the arm guides. Smooth descent to the rack. End of one pass.

sets.notes: **This is a FLOW, not a reps circuit.** One PASS = move through all five moves once — **row → snatch → squat → lunge → push press** — on ONE arm, continuous, no rest between moves. **Alternate arms every pass:** left pass, right pass, left pass... **5 passes per side = 1 set.** Do **4 sets (5th optional)**, resting 60-90s between sets. Weak side starts each set. Right shoulder watch on the overhead stack — modify rather than grind.

sets.name: Mobility Block — Cossack + Windmill + Single-Leg Around-the-World (Maintenance)

- Slow descent, hard stop at end-range

**LOAD:** 25lb. Maintenance (spotlighted on Thursday this week).

- 5 reps clockwise, 5 counter-clockwise, then switch legs
- **Torso quiet** — the bell tries to pull you into rotation; resist

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 35-40lb (heavier bell for the swing). Hip drive, not a squat.

Bodyweight. Hands at the bell or close together — triceps emphasis.
