Skip when the workout has already taken 55+ min or you're cooked** (especially since the strength block added a round this week). 3 rounds, continuous within a round. The mandatory workout finishes at the cooldown without this block.

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 25lb. Light row, 2s pull / 2s lower. Skip if the shoulders are cooked from the flow.
60s each side. Hip flexor release.
60s. Adductors get tight on KB days from the cossacks.

tips: **Full template** — banded prep → strength block (3 rounds) → Asgooch flow → mobility → cooldown.
**Spotlight: clean & press + the strength block.** The block steps up to 3 rounds — volume is the lever, loads hold.
**KB row prescribed at 45** (10 each) — it ran easy there last week.
**Asgooch flow = a FLOW, not reps.** One pass through all 5 moves on one arm, then alternate arms. 5 passes/side = 1 set. 4 sets mandatory, 5th optional. Pace it.
**Brutal Complex finisher stays OPTIONAL/EXTRA** — skip it on packed days; the strength-block extra round already added time.
**Pull-up greasing in the strength block** — 1-2 light bodyweight sets, NOT to failure.
**Right shoulder watch through the Asgooch overhead stack** — sub a front-rack lunge rather than grind.
**Leg-heavy flow bias = Tuesday** — Thursday will be lighter on the loaded squatting (Friday legs is the day after).
Cooldown mandatory — pigeon + butterfly.
Rotation plan: W16 cycles forward — TGU or windmill refresh.
formPhilosophy: The KB Tuesday template is settled; W15 exercises its built-in step-up lever — the strength block adds a round rather than the bells adding weight, which is exactly how the template was designed to progress without bloating or chasing load. Clean & press anchors the spotlight because it's where real strength is showing at held weight. The Asgooch flow stays a flow. Building decades, not weeks.

name: Week 15 Legs — Steady State, Station-Grouped (Spotlight: Leg Press + Bulgarian)
description: Volume steady, station-grouped. Squat holds 75 with the 6/7/8/8 ascending pyramid that produced good depth (depth built UP across the ramp last week, so it stays). Spotlights cycle forward to leg press (drill the full-ROM knees-to-chest depth — it's been training the abs/QL more than the legs three weeks running) and Bulgarian split squat (step the load up — the single-40 last week had headroom). Leg curl stays before incline RDL so the two hamstring lifts don't stack.

dayOverview.theme: Steady state, station-grouped. Squat holds 75 / 6/7/8/8 (depth builds across the ramp). Leg press + Bulgarian get the spotlight — leg press for the full-ROM core/QL depth, Bulgarian for the load step-up. Leg curl before incline RDL so the hamstring work doesn't stack.

spotlights.why: The full-ROM knees-to-chest position has trained the abs/QL/core more than the legs three weeks running — the user feels it there, not in the quads. Spotlight drills the depth + the active brace that keeps the lower back from lifting off the pad. Depth is the work; the load holds at 3 plates.

Stepped from bodyweight (W13) to a single 40lb DB (W14) clean, no twitching, 'could go heavier.' The step-up is earned — spotlight drills the front-heel drive + vertical-torso pattern at the new load so the form leads the weight.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W12 seated leg curl + calf raise · W13 Bulgarian split squat (NEW) · W14 squat + incline RDL · W15 leg press + Bulgarian (current) · W16 cycle forward — squat depth or calf-raise single-leg.
watchpoints: **Loads hold** — squat 75/side, leg press 3 plates, calf raise 3 plates, leg curl 90, incline RDL 45lb plate. The Bulgarian steps up (see its notes).
**Squat holds 6/7/8/8 at 75.** Depth built UP across the ascending ramp last week (the later sets were the deepest) — keep working the depth here, don't add load.
**Station-grouped sequence:** warmup → squat → leg press → leg-press-calf-raise (SAME machine, stay there) → Bulgarian (bench station) → leg curl → incline RDL → cool-down. No backtracking.
**Keep leg curl BEFORE incline RDL.** Running them reversed (incline RDL first) stacked two hamstring lifts back-to-back and smoked the second — keep the prescribed order.
**Bulgarian step-up** — single 45-50lb DB or a 25lb pair (your call on the carry). If anything twitches/spasms, drop to bodyweight and finish — that's the standing rule on this lift.
**QL/psoas watch** — cross-leg lateral lean in the warmup AND cool-down. If anything talks in the warmup, modify the day; mid-session, drop a set.

sets.name: Warmup (incl. Cross-Leg Lateral Lean — QL/Psoas Release)

exercises.notes: Full depth, slow. Find where the hips are tight and breathe into it. Depth check before loading.

30s each side. Scissor one foot over the other, reach the same-side arm overhead, lean away from the back leg — the stretch runs down the side of the waist into the QL and lateral hip. Do this before loading the squat.
Big slow circles. Wake up the hip stabilizers.
Spine mobility — slow, full ROM each direction.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension. Quick posterior-chain and low-back opener before loading the squat.
Bodyweight. QL check — if anything talks here, modify the day. Also previews the Bulgarian pattern.
Set 1: 45/side x8. Set 2: 65/side x8. Same depth as the working sets.

**LOAD:** 75/side. 4 sets: **6 / 7 / 8 / 8**. The depth built up across the ramp last week — keep working it at 75, that's the win.
- Bar high on the upper traps (NOT the neck), upper-back shelf squeezed
- **Brace like prepping for a punch** — deep belly breath at the top, HOLD through the descent, exhale on the drive up
- **Hips back AND down**, not just down
- 'Spread the floor' — screw the feet into the ground
- Knees track over the toes
- **Sit into the bottom** — the later sets were the deepest last week; keep chasing that depth, set by set
- Drive through the WHOLE foot

**Reflection:** the deepest reps last week came on the 7- and 8-rep sets, not the opening 6. Does that hold again — does depth keep building across the ramp? If it does, 6/7/8/8 at 75 is the durable pattern.

sets.name: 🔆 Leg Press + Calf Raise Station (Same Machine — Spotlight: Leg Press Depth)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 3 plates/side. 4 sets of 12. Chase DEPTH, not load.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the full-ROM core/QL position:**
- **Foot position:** shoulder-width, mid-foot on the platform, slight toe-out — set this before loading
- **Full ROM — knees toward the chest** ('knees hitting chest'). This deep position is what's been training the abs/QL/core more than the quads — that's the intent, not a bug
- **Actively press to keep the lower back from lifting off the pad** at the bottom — the brace is the spotlight; if the hips roll off the pad, you've gone past your current control, back off a hair
- **Press through the WHOLE foot** — heels grounded
- **Slow descent (3s), no bounce at the bottom**
- **Don't lock out hard at the top** — leave a hair of bend. Breath: in on the descent, out on the drive

**Reflection:** where does the work land — abs/QL/core (the pattern of the last three weeks) or the legs? If it's still core-dominant at full depth, that's the lift doing its job; hold 3 plates and keep the depth.

sets.name: Leg-Press Calf Raise (Same Machine — Stays Right Here)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 3 plates/side. 3 sets of 15. Stay on the leg press — same machine, no walking off.
- **Balls of both feet on the BOTTOM EDGE of the platform, heels hanging off** — no plate under the foot, the platform edge gives the heel drop
- **Both feet on the platform** — double-leg
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the heels drop as far below the edge as they'll go
- **Drive to FULL plantarflexion at the top**
- **3-4s eccentric** — the slow descent is the stimulus, not added load
- **1s squeeze at the peak**, no bouncing. Breath continuous, don't hold.

The slow tempo bit hard at this load last week — hold 3 plates; the single-leg conversation waits until the eccentric is dialed at double-leg.

sets.name: 🔆 Bulgarian Split Squat (Bench Station — Spotlight: Load Step-Up)

exercises.equipment: bench + DBs — Smith machine if free (use smith-machine-bulgarian-split-squat)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** step up — **single 45-50lb DB (goblet/suitcase) or a 25lb pair at the sides**, your call on the carry. The single-40 last week was 'decently hard... could go heavier.' 3 sets of 8-10 each leg.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — let the form lead the load:**
- **Rear foot up on the bench** behind you, laces down or toes tucked
- **Step out far enough that the front shin stays roughly VERTICAL at the bottom** — too short a stance = the knee crashes past the toes
- **Front knee tracks over the front foot** — not caving in
- **Lower until the rear knee nearly touches the floor** — controlled, no dropping
- **Drive up through the FRONT HEEL** — the front leg does the work, the rear leg is a kickstand for balance
- **Torso TALL** — a slight forward lean is fine, no folding over
- **2s descent**, own the bottom

**Watch:** if anything twitches/spasms, drop to bodyweight for the remaining sets and finish — going too heavy too fast is what triggered spasms on prior unprogrammed attempts. The step-up is deliberate, not a jump.

**Reflection:** does the front-heel drive + vertical torso hold at the heavier load, or does the form start leaning/cheating? If it holds clean, this is the new working load; if it cheats, the single-40 was the right number.

sets.name: Seated Leg Curl (3 Sets at 90 — Before Incline RDL)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 90. 3 sets of 12, slow tempo — you feel these deeply when you go slow.
- **Ankles UNDER the pad** — the ankle bone is the contact point, NOT the mid-calf
- **Settings: 5/m/0/1** (verify before loading)
- **Lap pad locked DOWN firmly** — a loose pad lets the torso lift and turns it into lower-back work
- **Curl the heels toward the glutes** — full ROM, full squeeze
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze**
- Torso anchored to the seat, no lifting forward; no bouncing out of the bottom

This comes BEFORE incline RDL on purpose — running it after smoked it last week. Take the leg curl fresh.

**LOAD:** 45lb plate. 3 sets of 15, dead slow with a 2s pause at the bottom.
- **Pad just below the hip crease** — NOT on the upper thigh, NOT on the stomach
- **Hip hinge** — a Romanian deadlift on the 45° bench, NOT a lumbar extension. Lower back NEUTRAL throughout
- **At the bottom:** the stretch is in the **hamstrings and glutes**, NOT the lower back. If the lumbar rounds, you're going too deep for current mobility
- **Drive up by squeezing the glutes and hamstrings**
- **At the top:** stop at neutral. Past neutral = lumbar load = QL irritation
- **Tempo: 3s eccentric, 2s pause at the bottom, 1s drive up.** The slow eccentric is the entire reason this lift works
- Take extra rest between sets if you need it

**Reflection:** where's the stretch landing — hamstrings/glutes (correct) or lower back (too deep / pad placement off)? If lower back, slow down further and check the pad before set 2.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Recovery Block (Hip/QL-Biased for Legs Day)

exercises.notes: 30s each side. Scissor the legs, reach overhead, lean away from the back leg — bookend the session with the same QL/psoas release as the warmup.
45s each side. Deep hip-flexor and glute release — the long hold lets the QL and psoas let go.
30s each side. Gentle twist for the QL — draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
45s each side. Hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Knees wide, arms extended forward. Parasympathetic shift.

sets.notes: 5-min recovery block, hip/QL-biased on legs day.

tips: **Steady state, station-grouped.** Squat 4 sets, leg press 4, calf raise 3, Bulgarian 3, leg curl 3, incline RDL 3.
**Squat holds 6/7/8/8 at 75** — depth builds across the ramp; keep working it, don't add load.
**Spotlight: leg press + Bulgarian.** Leg press drills the full-ROM core/QL depth; Bulgarian steps the load up.
**Station-grouped:** warmup → squat → leg press → leg-press-calf-raise (same machine — stay there) → Bulgarian → leg curl → incline RDL → cool-down. No backtracking.
**Leg curl BEFORE incline RDL** — don't reverse them; running incline RDL first stacked the hamstring work and smoked the leg curl.
**Bulgarian steps up** — single 45-50lb DB or a 25lb pair. Drop to bodyweight if anything twitches.
**Incline RDL is a 45lb plate, dead slow** — the tempo is the progression, not the number.
**Cross-leg lateral lean in the warmup AND cool-down** — QL/psoas release.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, hip/QL-biased on legs day.**
Rest: 3 min squats, 2 min leg press, 90s calf raise + Bulgarian + isolations.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state legs week. The squat pattern is settled (75 / 6/7/8/8, depth builds across the ramp), so the spotlight moves to the two lifts with something to drill: leg press, where full depth has quietly become core/QL work, and the Bulgarian, where a clean step-up is earned. The sequence keeps the two hamstring lifts from stacking. Form leads load on every lift — building decades, not weeks.

name: W15 Morning Flow — Bodyweight Spine + Hip (All Days, Rotated Variety)
description: 15 min bodyweight floor flow — universal W15 morning flow, used every training day (Mon push / Tue KB / Wed pull / Thu KB / Fri legs). Same three-part shape as W11-W14 with rotated moves for variety. Three-part: spine primer → bodyweight work → deep stretch arc. Day-specific therapeutic add-on at the end (push = pec-minor protocol; pull = dead hang + scap pull; legs = cross-leg lateral lean + pigeon + supine twist; KB days skip — banded prep covers it).

exercises.notes: Slow, full ROM each direction. Spine wave wakes the segment-by-segment articulation.
30s each side. Rotates in for W15 — from quadruped, thread one arm under the body and rotate the thoracic spine, then reach it back open. Wakes the mid-back rotation.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — the wrist dials a stretch up the back chain. Stays in the primer.

sets.name: Work Block — Bodyweight Activation (~5 min)

exercises.notes: Rotates in for W15. Feet flat, drive through the heels, squeeze the glutes to a tall bridge, ribs down — no arching the lower back. Posterior-chain wake-up.
30s each side. Anti-rotation — opposite arm + leg extend, hold a beat, hips stay square (no swinging). Different shape than W14's shoulder taps.
45s alternating. From down-dog, draw one knee toward the forehead, hold a beat, switch. Core + hip + shoulder integration.
45s slow. Durable hip opener under plank load.
30s each side. The windmill on the floor — lateral-hinge cue translation.

sets.notes: Glute bridge + bird-dog rotate in for variety. Anti-rotation gets a different shape than W14.

sets.name: Yoga Flow — Deep Stretch Arc (~7 min)

exercises.notes: 30s each side. Stays every week — signature spine move.
30s each direction. Quadruped hip abduction — slow, full ROM.
30s each side. Hip flexor + adductor + back-leg quad. Drop to elbows if accessible. Stays — durable hip opener.
Bodyweight, slow. Stays every week — mirrors the Tuesday loaded cossack.
Rotates in for W15 — knees wide on the mat, sink the hips back, deep adductor opener. Ease in slowly; the adductors take a beating on KB days.
30s each side. Long hold on the hip release to close the arc.

sets.notes: Continuous arc — flow between shapes, breathe deeply. Anchors stay (scorpion, cossack, lizard); frog stretch joins and pigeon closes for W15.

sets.name: 📍 Day-Specific Add-On — Pick by Today's Training (~3-5 min)

exercises.notes: **📍 PUSH DAYS — KEY PROTOCOL MOVE.** 30s each at LOW / MID / HIGH elbow positions. Arm bent 90°, forearm on the door frame, step through and rotate the torso AWAY. Desk work continuously re-tightens pec minor — daily.
**📍 PUSH DAYS** — active side of the pec-minor fix. Lower trap + rotator cuff.
**📍 PUSH DAYS** — serratus activation, helps unstick a tight pec minor.
**📍 PUSH DAYS (optional)** — slow rotator cuff work. Add if the shoulder feels off.
**📍 PUSH DAYS (optional)** — pins the shoulder blades in the corrected position.
**📍 PULL DAYS** — 25s. Decompress the shoulders, warm the grip.
**📍 PULL DAYS** — scapulae retracting only, no elbow bend. Crisp scap engagement before loaded pulls.
**📍 LEGS DAYS** — 30s each side. Scissor one foot over the other, reach the same-side arm overhead, lean away from the back leg — QL/psoas release. Also in the legs-workout warmup.
**📍 LEGS DAYS — W8 QL-SPASM PROTOCOL.** 90s each side. Long hold lets the QL/psoas release. Non-negotiable on legs day.
**📍 LEGS DAYS** — 60s each side. Gentle twist for the QL. Lacrosse-ball QL roll above the iliac crest beforehand if available.

sets.notes: **Pick today's day-specific protocol — push / pull / legs.** ~3-5 min total. KB days (Tue/Thu) skip this block — the in-workout banded prep covers the equivalent.

tips: Same shape as W11-W14, rotated moves. Morning flows stay low-fatigue; variety keeps them fresh.
**15 min main flow + 3-5 min day-specific add-on** — universal across W15 (Mon push / Tue KB / Wed pull / Thu KB / Fri legs).
**Scorpion + cossack BW + lizard pose stay every week** — durable anchors.
**Thread-the-needle, glute bridge, bird-dog, frog stretch rotate in for W15** variety.
**Day-specific add-on at the end** — push days do the pec-minor protocol, pull days do dead hang + scap pull, legs days do cross-leg lean + 90s pigeon + supine twist. KB days skip the add-on.
If short on time: scorpion + lizard + cossack BW + pigeon, plus today's day-specific add-on.
formPhilosophy: Same as W11-W14 — variety means different shapes hitting the same patterns. Scorpion-family spine work + hip openers + adductor stretches. Morning flows stay structured around the in-workout banded prep's logic on KB days, and the day-specific protocols on PPL days.

name: Week 15 Pull — Steady State (Spotlight: Chest-Supported Row + Face Pull)
description: Volume steady. The behind-back shrug moves to an early activation slot — it's protective 'opposite movement' work for the right shoulder, and burying it as the closing station last week meant a rushed session dropped it (the shoulder flared). Chest-supported row steps up to 40 (35 was too easy two weeks running). Face pull gets the spotlight refresh now that the elbows-high / external-rotate cue is landing. Cable lifts list a number per equipment option, including the new dual-pulley variant.

dayOverview.theme: Steady state. Behind-back shrug moves to the FRONT of the session as protective activation. Chest-supported row steps to 40. Face pull gets the spotlight. DB row holds the 60/70/80 pyramid, pull-ups hold 4 sets. Cable lifts list per-equipment numbers.

spotlights.why: 35 came in 'too easy without a sweat' two weeks running, so the weight-up is earned — steps to 40. Spotlight drills the chest-glued-to-bench / elbow-to-hip cue at the new load so the form holds through the jump, not just the number.

Cycles back — last spotlighted W12. The reposted form (elbows high above the shoulders, external-rotate at the top) just started landing — 'very different, feeling it in the back.' Spotlight locks that cue in at 42.5 before any load change.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W12 face pull + reverse fly · W13 bicep + high cable curl + cable crunch · W14 pull-up + DB row · W15 chest-supported row + face pull (current) · W16 cycle forward — lat pulldown or bicep refresh.
watchpoints: **Behind-back shrug is now FIRST (activation slot), not the closing station.** It's protective decompression work — the counter-movement to all the pulling — and it's the one piece that can't be allowed to drop. Do it right after the warmup. (The shrug/trap-3 alternation pauses this week; the shrug specifically is the protective piece, so it stays.) A light 1-set version is now also greased into the push + KB-day warmups.
**Chest-supported row steps to 40.** Confirm the form holds through the jump — chest glued, elbow to the hip, no torso twist. If 40 grinds the form, drop back to 35 and we hold.

**Shoulder management:** last week's flare was VOLUME-driven (more sets, all slow-eccentric, high time-under-tension), not weight. Don't make every set all-slow-eccentric at once — ramp the tempo. Lean on the early shrug, the cable fly, morning stretches, and external rotations. The flare is management-tractable as long as the shrug actually gets done.
**Loads hold** — DB row 60/70/80, pull-up bodyweight, face pull 42.5, high cable curl 170, reverse fly 20. Cable crunch steps up (see its notes).
**Cable lifts have per-equipment numbers** — pick whichever station's free, log equipment + number. Lat pulldown now has four known variants (machine / cable column / cable pulley / dual pulley).
**Left bicep first, every set** — the weak-left pattern resurfaces when the curl comes late in the session.
**Pull-up frequency holds** — 4 sets here + 1 in push warmup + 1-2 in KB Tuesday. Slow tempo, not to failure.

exercises.notes: Scap activation. Squeeze the shoulder blades together, soft elbow.
Spine warm — slow, full ROM each direction.
Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — primes grip and the pulling chain before bar work.
Active hang, not collapsed — engage the lats, pull the shoulders DOWN away from the ears even at full extension.

sets.name: Behind-Back DB Shrug — Protective Activation (DO THIS FIRST)

exercises.equipment: DB pair, held behind the body
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40-50lb pair. 3 sets — moved to the FRONT this week.

**Why it's here, first:** this is the 'opposite movement' to all the pulling — a counter/decompression for the right shoulder. Burying it at the end meant it got skipped, and the shoulder flared. It reads more like a stretch than a lift; that's the point. Do it before the loaded pulling so it's locked in.
- **DBs held BEHIND the body** at the sides of the hips/glutes — palms facing back
- **Shoulders pull DOWN and BACK** at the start — packed, not relaxed
- **Shrug UP and slightly BACK** — pinch the shoulder blades together at the top
- **Hold 1s at the top**, slow descent
- **Pack DOWN, NOT up** as the resting position — the lower position IS the work
- Chest open, not slouched

**Reflection:** does doing the shrug first change how the right shoulder feels through the rest of the pull session vs. the weeks it was last or skipped?

sets.notes: Protective trap-chain activation, moved to the front of the session. ~4 min. Light-to-moderate, peak-squeeze — treat it as a decompression, not a max effort. This is the full 3-set version; a light 1-set greasing version now also lives in the push + KB-day warmups.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** Bodyweight. 4 sets of 6-8.
- **Straight bar** — the variant that's been feeling best
- **Active hang start**, not collapsed
- **Pull elbows DOWN to ribs**, NOT chin to bar
- **Chest leads to the bar at the top**, eyes ahead, head neutral
- **Slow eccentric ~2-3s**, active hang at the bottom of every rep — no dropping
- **Stop the set when the rep stops being clean** — never kip. Don't grind to failure with the shoulder freshly out of last week's flare; quality reps, frequency over max effort.

sets.name: 🔆 DB Rack / Bench Block — Chest-Supported Row (Spotlight) + DB Row + Incline Curl + Reverse Fly (3 Rounds)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40 (step up from 35 — it was too easy two weeks running). 3 sets of 10-12.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — drill the form holds at the new load:**
- **Chest stays GLUED to the incline bench** — if the chest peels off to heave the DBs up, the weight's ahead of the form
- **Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit** — elbow-to-hip keeps it in the lats, not the rear delt
- **Don't rotate the torso** — no twisting up to throw the DB; both sides of the chest stay on the pad
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze** at the top, no DB slam at the bottom
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the shoulder blade protract, then re-pull

**Reflection:** does 40 still hold the chest-glued, elbow-to-hip form for all 3 clean sets, or does the form start cheating (chest peels, torso twists) on set 3? If the form cheats, that's the ceiling — drop to 35 and we hold there.

**LOAD:** 60/70/80 ascending pyramid — one set per round (60, then 70, then 80). 80 holds clean now, so the pyramid stays.
- **Chest-supported on the incline bench** — same setup as the chest-supported row
- **Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit**
- **Don't rotate the torso** — chest glued, no twisting up
- **Slow 2s descent, 1s squeeze**
- **At 80:** if the torso starts twisting or the elbow drifts to the armpit, stop the set — that's the form tapping out.

**LOAD:** 25lb. 3 sets of 8-10. Preacher-style chest-supported curl (the preacher-bench replacement).
- **Set the incline bench to ~45°, lean in chest-first** — armpit and the back of the upper arm flat on the pad
- **Arm hangs down the face of the pad**, underhand grip; the upper arm stays flat on the pad the ENTIRE rep (don't lift the elbow off)
- **Left arm first, every set** — the weak-left pattern returns when the curl comes late
- **Full stretch at the bottom — pause 2s**
- **Curl smoothly to the peak squeeze**, no swing; 2-3s eccentric

**LOAD:** 20lb. 3 sets of 12 — strict tempo, cap at 12 with a slower eccentric rather than chasing extra reps.
- **30° reverse-incline** (chest-down on the incline bench)
- DBs hanging fully extended at the start, **soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED throughout**
- **Lead with the elbow, hand passive**
- **Wings out and slightly UP to shoulder height** — sweep, don't lift
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze** — no swing

sets.notes: One trip to the DB rack covers all 4 lifts. Incline bench at ~30° for the rows + reverse fly (30° reverse-incline), set to ~45° for the incline curl. 3 rounds.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD (pick whichever station's free, log which one):**
- **Regular lat pulldown machine: 140**
- **Dual pulley: 70** ('surprisingly strong' here)
- **Cable column: 52.5-57.5**
- **Cable pulley: 47.5**

3 sets.
- **Wide grip near the bend** — more lat isolation, less bicep
- **Slight backward lean ~15°, NO further** — more = becomes a row
- **Pull the bar to the UPPER CHEST — NEVER behind the neck**
- 'Lats squeezing oranges into the back pockets' at the bottom
- 1s pause at the contraction, 2s controlled return to a full overhead stretch
- Knees pinned firmly under the pad

exercises.equipment: cable column (mid/upper-chest height + rope)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** cable column 42.5. 3 sets of 20.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — lock in the cue that just started landing:**
- **Pull the rope to face level** — not to the chest
- **ELBOWS HIGH (above the shoulders)** — the make-or-break cue; this is what moved the work into the back
- **External-rotate at the top** — knuckles point UP, like the top of a double-biceps pose
- **1s peak hold** at the contracted position
- **Slow controlled return, 2s** — let the cable pull the arms back, don't drop
- This is rear-delt + mid-trap + external-rotator health work — the right-shoulder-protective end of the pull day

**Reflection:** can you keep 'feeling it in the back' (not the front of the shoulder / the biceps) for all 3 sets at 42.5? If the front of the shoulder takes over, the elbows have dropped — re-set them high. Hold 42.5 while the cue is the focus.

sets.name: Cable Column Finisher — High Cable Curl + Cable Crunch (2-3 Sets)

exercises.equipment: cable column (low pulley, single D-handle, one arm at a time)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD (single arm — scales differ, log which station):**
- Cable column (single D-handle): 170
- Pulley / weight-stack station: ~120
2 working sets per arm.
- **Single arm at a time, one D-handle** — stand sideways, arm out at shoulder level
- **Upper arm parallel to the floor, FIXED** — the whole point of the high-cable variant
- **Curl the hand toward the ear**, peak squeeze
- **Left arm first**; slow eccentric, no bounce at the start

**LOAD (pick whichever station's free, log which one):**
- **Cable pulley (rope): 75-77.5** (step up — 72.5 came in 'fairly easy')
- **Cable column (rope): 135**

3 sets.
- **Kneel under the high cable**
- **HIPS LOCKED** — the most important cue. The hips do not move.
- **Crunch from the abs ONLY** — the spine flexes, the hips stay put. Hips moving = hip-flexor work, not abs.
- **Chest toward the thighs**, hold the crunch 1 second
- **Slow eccentric.** If the step-up still feels easy, note it for another bump.

sets.notes: Same cable column as the face pull. 2 rounds = 2 sets each; round the cable crunch to 3 if there's time and the abs aren't fried.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow position. Pec minor lengthen.
Passive hang. Don't engage — let the shoulders unpack and the spine decompress.
30s each side. Draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
45s each side. Hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Parasympathetic shift.

sets.notes: 5 minutes of recovery work, non-negotiable closing block.

tips: **Behind-back shrug moves to FIRST** — protective decompression for the right shoulder. It can't be the piece a rushed session drops anymore.
**Chest-supported row steps to 40** — 35 was too easy two weeks running. Spotlight: confirm the form holds through the jump.
**Face pull spotlight** — elbows high, external-rotate, feel it in the back. Hold 42.5 and lock the cue.
**Shoulder management: ramp the tempo** — don't make every set all-slow-eccentric at once. Last week's flare was volume/TUT, not weight.
**Loads hold** — DB row 60/70/80 pyramid, pull-up bodyweight, high cable curl 170, reverse fly 20.
**Cable crunch steps up to pulley 75-77.5** (72.5 was fairly easy).
**Cable lifts list per-equipment numbers** — lat pulldown (140 machine / 70 dual pulley / 52.5-57.5 column / 47.5 pulley). Pick what's free, log it.
**Left bicep first, every set** — weak-left pattern.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, permanent every gym day.**
Rest: shrug 60s, 2.5 min pull-ups, 90s DB block, 2 min lat pulldown, 90s face pull, 60s finisher.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state pull week with one structural change: the protective shrug leads instead of trails, because the shoulder needs the decompression work front-loaded and reliably done. Chest-supported row earns its weight-up after two easy weeks; face pull earns the spotlight now that its cue finally landed. Loads otherwise hold — last week's flare was volume, not weight, so the lever is sequencing and tempo, not backing off the numbers. Building decades, not weeks.

name: Week 15 Push — Steady State (Spotlight: Chest Press + Farmer Carry)
description: Volume steady, loads steady. Spotlights cycle forward to chest press machine + farmer carry — the two trap/press lifts that haven't had a deep-cue drill recently. Chest press gets the cross-body arm stretch baked in between sets (it cleared the right-pec referral last session). Order is availability-driven: take whichever station is free, but keep each station's work grouped so you don't lose the machine. Cable lifts list a number per equipment option.

dayOverview.theme: Steady state — sets and loads hold. Spotlight cycles forward to chest press + farmer carry. Push press, incline DB, lateral raise, cable block all run maintenance cues at their working numbers. Pull-up greasing set stays in the warmup.

spotlights.why: Cycles forward — last spotlighted W11. The right pec refers on set 1 here; the cross-body arm stretch between sets clears it. Spotlight drills the seat height + scap-pinned setup AND bakes the cross-body stretch in as a between-set cue (direct user request).

First time in the spotlight. It got skipped last session, and it's the cleanest packed-shoulder posture drill on push day — tall ribs, shoulders down and back, firm-but-not-clenched grip (the grip-clench / right-shoulder coupling is the thing to watch). Make the carry the lift, not a walk.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W12 lateral raise + Kinesis fly · W13 cable column block · W14 push press + incline DB · W15 chest press + farmer carry (current) · W16 cycle forward — lateral raise + Kinesis fly refresh.
watchpoints: **Order is availability-driven — take whichever station is free.** Keep each station's full set of work together (don't bounce between two stations mid-block, or you lose the machine). If push press ends up second after a long warmup, expect ~7/6/6 at 45 rather than 8-10 — that's the accepted trade-off for getting the session in.
**Cable lateral raise holds at cable column 30** while the pain-free shoulder streak is new — last session was the first pain-free lateral raise in ~6 weeks. Don't chase load here yet.
**Pack DOWN, not up** — push press, incline DB, lateral raise, chest press, farmer carry all carry the cue. If a lockout needs a shrug, the load is too heavy for the cue — pause the set.
**Pull-up greasing set stays in the warmup** — 1 fresh set of 6-8, slow, not to failure. Part of the weekly pull-up frequency (this + 4 on pull day + 1-2 on KB Tuesday).

**Protective shrug greasing set in the warmup (NEW)** — the pull-day behind-back shrug, scattered here + onto KB days because it's cheap and you keep forgetting it. 1 light set; it decompresses the right shoulder.

**Right shoulder watch** — last push day was the cleanest in 6 weeks. The pull-day flare later in W14 was volume-driven, not push. If the line-of-sensation / grip-triggered cluster shows on any press here, drop volume on the day.
**Cable block lists a number per machine** — pick the one that's free and log the equipment + number you used.

sets.name: Warmup + Shoulder Rehab (Non-Negotiable) + Pull-Up Greasing + Protective Shrug

exercises.notes: Slow, big circles. Wake up scap glide before loading.
Full sequence with red band. Non-negotiable on push day.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — the wrist dials a stretch up the back chain from forearm to shoulder to lats. Wakes the grip and shoulder line before loading.
Ribs down, glutes tight, body in one line. Slow eccentric, 1s pause with chest 1-2" off the floor.

**Pull-up greasing set.** 1 fresh set, slow tempo, NOT to failure. Active hang start, pull elbows down to ribs, chest leads. Frequency, not max effort — if the shoulder talks, drop to scapular-pulls only and finish the count.

**Protective shrug (greasing set) — the pull-day shrug, now scattered to more days.** 1 light set, DBs held behind the body, palms back. Pack the shoulders DOWN and BACK, shrug UP and slightly back, 1s peak squeeze, slow down. It's the 'opposite movement' that decompresses the right shoulder — costs no time or energy, easy to forget. Light activation, not a working set.

**LOAD:** 45lb DBs per side. 3 sets of 8-10 (7/6/6 is fine if these run second — see the order watchpoint).
- **Feet parallel, hip-width** — not duck stance
- **Ribs DOWN before the dip** — catch any rib flare on set 1
- **Pack DOWN, not up** — shoulder blades into the back pockets, neck long
- **Shallow dip ~3-4"**, straight down through the heels
- **Vertical DB path** — DBs travel up next to the ears, head pokes through at the top
- **Drive fast, lockout solid, descent controlled.** Breath: in at the dip, out on the drive

**LOAD:** 15lb DBs. 3 sets of 15-18.
- **Lead with elbow, hand passive** — wrist follows
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED** through the rep
- **Stop at shoulder height — never higher**
- **2s eccentric** — slow descent is the stimulus
- Scap-reset between sets if the shoulder gets noisy

sets.name: Incline DB Press (3 Sets at 45 pair)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 45lb pair. 3 sets of 8-10 (or run the slow-eccentric higher-rep version that felt right last week — 10-12 with a 3s descent).
- **Bench at 30°**, not 45° — steeper biases front delt over upper chest
- **Shoulders packed back AND down** — pin the back of the shoulder into the bench
- **Forearm stacked vertically over the elbow at the bottom** — the cue that makes 45 feel honest
- **Elbows ~45° from torso**, not flared to 90°
- **Press to a fingerwidth apart at the top**, 1s pause at the bottom. Breath: in on descent, out on press

**LOAD:** 165. 3 sets of 8-10.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — drill the setup, and stretch the pec between sets:**
- **Seat height: handles align with the mid-chest / nipple line** — set this BEFORE sitting; the wrong height is what loads the front of the shoulder
- **Shoulders pinned BACK against the pad** — the foundation cue, hold it the entire set
- **3s eccentric** — count it; the slow lower is the stimulus
- **Press to almost extension** — leave a hair of bend, don't lock and dump
- **Ribs down** — no arching off the pad to push more weight
- **🔁 BETWEEN EVERY SET: cross-body arm stretch on the right side** — pull the arm across the chest, 20-30s. It cleared the right-pec referral last session; do it proactively, not just when the pec talks.

**Reflection:** does the cross-body stretch between sets keep the right pec quiet across all 3 sets, or does the referral build anyway by set 3? If it builds, that's a sign to drop a set or pull the load slightly — note it.

**LOAD:** Kinesis 8 (bump to 9 from set 2 if set 1 feels light — both run clean).
- **Slight forward hinge at the hips** — chest leads, not head
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED throughout**
- **'Hug a tree'** — squeeze from the chest, not the arms
- **Slow eccentric (~3s)** — let the cables pull the arms back for the deep pec stretch
- The shoulder feels good here — the stretch is the stimulus, protect that

sets.name: Cable Column Block — Lat Raise → Tri Ext → Straight-Arm Pulldown (3 Rounds)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:**
- **Cable column: 30** (hold — the pain-free streak is new)
- **Kinesis: 5-6** (the W9-swap default, if the column's taken)

3 rounds, one arm at a time.
- **Lead with the elbow as a DIRECTION** — the elbow points, doesn't bend
- **Soft elbow ~10°, FIXED** throughout
- **Stand sideways** to the stack, working arm farther from it
- **Stop at shoulder height — higher = traps**
- **2s eccentric**, fight the cable down

**LOAD:**
- **Cable column: 70** (default)
- **Kinesis: 5** (fallback)

3 rounds. **Always kneeling — there's no bench at this station; the forward torso lean IS the 'incline.'**
- **Kneel facing AWAY from the high pulley**, rope overhead
- **Elbows PINNED** — only the forearms move
- **Hands shoulder-width on the rope**
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the rope pull the hands behind the head
- **Stop just shy of lockout**, slow eccentric. Set 1 feels easy, set 3 is brutal — that's the lift working.

**LOAD:**
- **Cable column: 120** (the working number — really hard at 10 here)
- **Kinesis: 6** (fallback)

3 rounds.
- **Stand a step back, hinge ~15° at the hips** — fixed hinge, the torso doesn't pump
- **Slight elbow bend (~5°), FIXED throughout**
- **Pull the bar to the thighs, NOT past** — past = shoulders roll forward, lats switch off
- **Squeeze the lats hard at the bottom** — 'oranges into the back pockets'
- **Slow controlled return to a full overhead stretch.** Hold 120; only step to 125 if set 3 stays clean two sessions running.

sets.notes: Cable block — sharp cues, 3 rounds. One trip to the chosen station covers all three. Pick what's free (cable column is the default for all three this week) and log what you used.

sets.name: 🔆 Farmer Carry (Spotlight — 3 Walks)

exercises.equipment: DB rack
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40-50lb DBs. 3 walks of ~30-45s each.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the carry IS the lift, make the posture the work:**
- **Stand TALL** — ribs down, crown of the head reaching up, no leaning back to counterbalance
- **Shoulders pulled DOWN and BACK** — into the back pockets, never shrugged toward the ears. The DBs pull the shoulders up the whole walk; resist it the whole walk. This is the 'pack DOWN, not up' cue under load.
- **Neck long, eyes forward** — no chin poke
- **Walk a straight line at a deliberate pace**, breathing steadily — don't rush to put them down
- **Grip firm but NOT death-clenched** — a hard right-hand squeeze provokes the right shoulder; firm-but-relaxed is the cue

**Reflection:** does the right shoulder stay neutral when the grip stays relaxed, and does a harder clench change that? Log whether grip pressure is the variable that touches the shoulder.

sets.notes: Spotlight trap-chain block. 3 walks at 40-50lb — light load, packed-shoulder posture is the entire point. Do this; it got skipped last session.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow position. Pec minor lengthen — the antagonist to the upper-trap chain loaded all session.
Passive hang from the pull-up bar. **Don't engage** — let the shoulders unpack and the spine decompress.
30s each side on the mat. Draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
45s each side. Front leg + back leg at 90°. Sink the hips toward the floor — hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Knees wide, arms extended forward. Parasympathetic shift before leaving the gym.

sets.notes: 5 minutes of recovery work, non-negotiable closing block. It got skipped last week — don't skip it.

tips: **Steady state — sets and loads hold.** The work this week is depth of execution, not new numbers.
**Spotlight: chest press + farmer carry.** Chest press drills the setup + the cross-body stretch between sets; farmer carry drills packed-shoulder posture under load.
**Cross-body arm stretch between every chest-press set** — proactively, not just when the pec refers. It cleared the right pec last session.
**Order is availability-driven** — take whatever station is free, keep each station's work grouped. Push press going second costs a couple reps; that's fine.
**Cable lateral raise holds at cable column 30** — the pain-free streak is new, don't chase load.
**Pack DOWN, not up** — every press + the carry carries the cue.
**Pull-up greasing set in the warmup** — 1 slow set, not to failure.
**Farmer carry — do it** (it got skipped last session). 3 walks at 40-50lb.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, permanent every gym day.**
Rest: 2 min push press + chest press, 90s lateral raise + Kinesis fly + farmer carry, 75s cable block.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state push week — the gains come from sharper execution at the established loads, not from chasing weight. Chest press and farmer carry get the deep-cue treatment because they touch the right-shoulder/pec pattern most directly: the cross-body stretch and the relaxed-grip carry are both shoulder-management tools as much as they're lifts. Building decades, not weeks.

name: Week 16 KB Saturday Cardio — Conditioning (Spotlight: Snatch; 100-Rep Block Finisher)
description: Saturday KB OPTION — pure conditioning, distinct from Tue (strength) and Thu (lighter skill template). Light bell throughout (16-20lb) — breathing rate and sustainability are the targets, not load. The Asgooch cardio complex carries over; the flow combos rotate to halo→reverse-lunge + around-the-body-pass-to-squat; and the finisher rotates this week to high-rep 100-rep blocks (from the @gymfiesta daily challenge) — light bell, posture-and-volume focused. Spotlight on the snatch (the technical, shoulder-relevant move in the cardio complex). Choice-of-the-day on D6 alongside stairmaster, easy run, or rest.

dayOverview.theme: Saturday conditioning — light bell, breathing-rate target. Asgooch cardio complex + rotated flow combos. Finisher rotates to 100-rep blocks. Day after Friday legs — squatting stays LIGHT on purpose. Spotlight: the snatch punch-through.

spotlights.why: The technical centerpiece of the Asgooch cardio complex and the most right-shoulder-relevant move on a light-bell day. Spotlight the hip-drive + punch-through + soft catch so the bell doesn't bang the wrist or crash the shoulder at the top — the move that most rewards clean mechanics on a conditioning day.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W14 controlled-power finisher · W15 brutal-complex-variant finisher · W16 100-rep block finisher (current) · W17 cycle forward — controlled-power or a fresh complex. The Asgooch cardio complex stays; the flow combos + finisher rotate so Saturday stays fresh.
watchpoints: **Day after Friday legs.** Squatting (front squat × 6 in the complex) stays LIGHT — 16-20lb. The 100-rep finisher is upper/core/hinge biased on purpose; skip the squat reps if the QL/quads are talking.
**Light bell is the whole point** — 16-20lb working. Conditioning means breathing rate, not bell weight.
**Asgooch CARDIO complex ≠ Tuesday's OVERHEAD complex** — same author, different chain. Cardio = row/clean/squat/snatch (low-and-explosive).
**Snatch spotlight** — hips drive the bell, punch the hand THROUGH at the top for a soft catch, no bang on the wrist. Sub high pulls if the right shoulder crackles on the catch.
**Finisher rotated to 100-rep blocks** — light bell, 4×25 each. Break to 5×20 if needed. It's posture + volume conditioning, not strength; keep moving.
**Choice-of-the-day on D6** — not mandatory. Skip if Friday legs cooked you; swap for stairmaster / easy run if cardio-only is the call. No pull-up greasing here — Saturday is the conditioning flank.

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 16-20lb. Loosen the shoulders fast — the cardio complex is its own warmup.
Easy two-handed swings. Prime the hinge.
Light, open the hips. Skip if Friday legs left the quads sore.
Standing, torso hinged slightly forward. Wakes the grip + forearm + posterior chain — primes the snatch catch.

sets.name: Quick Banded Prep (~2 min — abbreviated)

exercises.notes: Mini-band overhead.
Scaps depress.
Rear delts fire.
Sternum height, ribs down.

sets.notes: **Abbreviated prep** — 4 moves instead of the full 7. Saturday is conditioning; the full 7-move prep is overkill for a light-bell day.

sets.name: 🔆 Asgooch Cardio Complex — LEFT (Spotlight: Snatch)

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 16-20lb. Left hand. Hips back, back flat, pull the elbow past the ribs. 2s pull, 2s lower.
Left hand. **Hip drive into the rack** — thumb to collarbone. Smooth catch — knees absorb.
Left rack. **LIGHT** — Friday legs is yesterday. Sit tall, full depth IF the legs are fresh; reduce depth before load if they're cooked.

Left hand. 🔆 **SPOTLIGHT — the punch-through:**
- **Hips drive the bell**, not the arm — the hinge throws it overhead
- **Punch the hand THROUGH at the top** — the bell rotates around the wrist and you punch up to meet it, so it settles soft with no bang
- **Soft catch, ribs down at lockout** — the bell stacks over the shoulder
- **Right shoulder watch on the catch** — sub high pulls for the last 2 rounds if it crackles

sets.notes: 5 rounds LEFT. Continuous within a round — row → clean → squat → snatch with no rest. Rest 30-45s between rounds. **Weak side first.** Different from Tuesday's overhead Asgooch — same author, different chain.

sets.name: Asgooch Cardio Complex — RIGHT

exercises.notes: Right hand. Same form — hips back, full extension.
Right hand. Smooth clean to the rack.
Right rack. Same depth/load discipline as the left.
Right hand. **Spotlight punch-through + right shoulder watchpoint on the catch** — same modify-to-high-pull rule.

sets.notes: 5 rounds RIGHT. Continuous within a round. **If the workout is running long after the left side, drop to 3-4 rounds right — don't grind a quality session into a sloppy one.**

sets.name: Flow Combos — Halo to Reverse Lunge + Around-the-Body Pass to Squat

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 16-20lb. Halo one direction → reverse lunge → halo the other direction → reverse lunge the other leg. Continuous, fluid. The halo loosens the shoulder while the lunge keeps the legs honest.

Pass the bell around the body once → squat → next pass, alternating pass direction. Torso tall and still during the pass; full depth on the squat (LIGHT — Friday legs is yesterday). Coordination + conditioning hybrid.

sets.notes: Coordination-conditioning hybrids — the upper-body skill challenge slows the leg work down enough that the squats don't dump the quads. 3 rounds, 30-45s rest between rounds.

sets.name: 🌀 100-Rep Block Finisher — Light & High-Volume (Rotated In for W16)

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 16-20lb. Pass the bell around the hips/body, alternate direction each set. Core tight, torso quiet. 4×25 = 100 total.
Side-to-side swings across the body — use core rotation, hips drive. 4×25 = 100 total.
Explosive hip snap, pull the bell to chin height, elbows high. 4×25 = 100 total. **Right shoulder watch** — keep it light; the hip snap does the work, not the arm.
Standard two-handed swings — squeeze the glutes hard at the top, keep the hinge honest as the reps climb. 4×25 = 100 total.

sets.notes: **100-rep block finisher — light bell, high volume.** Four blocks of 100 (4×25 each = 400 reps). Break each 100 into 4×25 or 5×20 as needed; rest 20-30s between blocks. **If short on time or pre-fatigued, do the first 2-3 blocks** — don't grind the volume into sloppy reps. Posture + conditioning, not strength; keep moving and keep the breathing rate up.

exercises.notes: Slow spine wave. Decompress after the high-rep finisher.
60s each side. Hip flexor release — counters the lunge flow + cardio-complex squat reps.
60s. Adductors take a hit from the lateral shapes.

tips: **Saturday conditioning option — choice-of-the-day on D6.** Alternates with stairmaster, easy run, or rest. Skip if Friday legs cooked you.
**LIGHT bell throughout: 16-20lb working.** This is the whole point. Conditioning = breathing rate, not load.
**Core blocks carry over:** Asgooch CARDIO complex (row/clean/squat/snatch × 6 × 5 rounds per side) + rotated flow combos (halo→reverse-lunge + around-body-pass→squat).
**Finisher rotated to 100-rep blocks** — around-body pass / side swing / high pull / swing, 4×25 each, light bell. Do 2-3 blocks if short on time.
**Spotlight: the snatch punch-through** — hips drive, punch the hand through, soft catch. Sub high pulls if the catch crackles.
**Squatting stays LIGHT** — Friday legs is yesterday. Skip the squat reps if the quads are tight.
**Right shoulder watch on the snatch + high pull** — light bell, smooth catch; high pulls if it crackles.
**No pull-up greasing here** — Saturday is the conditioning flank.
Cooldown mandatory — cat-cow + pigeon + butterfly.
Rotation plan: W17 rotates the finisher again so Saturday stays fresh.
formPhilosophy: Saturday is conditioning, distinct from the Tue and Thu KB days. Light bell, more reps, more variety. The cave-pull strategy rotates the finisher block week to week — controlled-power, brutal-complex, now 100-rep blocks — so Saturday builds breadth without going stale or heavy. The day stays explicitly optional: it's the KB flavor of the D6 cardio choice, for days when a treadmill isn't the right call.

name: Week 16 KB Conditioning — Thursday, New Flow + Coordination Block (Spotlight: Figure-8 → Reverse Lunge)
description: KB Thursday, full template — now with a permanent Flow + Coordination block dropped in right after the banded shoulder prep. This is base KB skill-building: light-bell, flowing coordination drills to widen the movement vocabulary while the bell is still new. The block rotates content week to week; this week it spotlights the figure-8 → reverse lunge (new to the program). The rest of the day holds — lighter strength block, the canonical OTD flow, TGU + windmill as mobility maintenance, a balance closer, cooldown. Lighter on loaded squatting (Friday legs is the day after).

dayOverview.theme: Thursday KB day, full template, lighter on loaded squatting. NEW permanent Flow + Coordination block right after the banded prep — base KB skill-building, rotating content. This week it spotlights the figure-8 → reverse lunge. TGU + windmill drop to mobility maintenance. Day closes on a light balance closer — conditioning + skill + balance, never a metabolic finisher.

spotlights.why: The first content of the new permanent Flow + Coordination block, and new to the program. You're still building base KB skills — this drills the figure-8 weave (hip rotation + grip + coordination) flowing into a reverse lunge. Skill novelty over intensity: the win is a new movement in the bank, learned clean, at a light bell.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: Flow + Coordination block (permanent): W16 figure-8 → reverse lunge · W17 figure-8 weave or split-stance pass-through · W18 halo → reverse lunge · then the GymFiesta-trio + swing variants. Mobility maintenance rotates its cue focus: W15 windmill spotlight → W16 TGU + windmill maintenance → W17 bent-press refresh.
watchpoints: **NEW permanent Flow + Coordination block — right after the banded prep.** Light-bell base-skill work: a familiar pass to warm up, then the week's new skill. It runs every Thursday now and won't get dropped. Skill + coordination is the point, NOT cardio burn — keep it light and clean.

**Thursday = day before Friday legs.** Loaded squatting (OTD-flow front squat, goblet) stays LIGHT — no PR attempts. The figure-8 → reverse lunge adds light leg work; keep the bell light so it's coordination, not load.
**OTD flow is the canonical 5-move flow** — dead clean → front squat → lateral lunge → bent press → tactical clean. Bent press is move #4, in the flow, not a separate block. Light groove, 2 rounds.
**TGU + windmill are maintenance this week** — sharp cues, light load. The deep-cue focus is on the new Flow + Coordination skill.
**Right shoulder watch on the overhead work** (TGU lockout, windmill, OTD-flow bent press) — if it talks, lighten and slow down; back off range before grinding.
**Protective shrug greasing set in the warmup** — 1 light set, DBs or a bell behind the body. Cheap, easy to forget.
**Balance closer, not a metabolic finisher** — single-leg RDL → bird-dog → standing side-to-side twist, light bell. Thursday is conditioning + skills + balance, and Friday legs is tomorrow.

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 15-20lb. Slow circles, both directions. Shoulder loosener.
Standing, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — wakes the grip and forearms for the flow + clean catches.

exercises.equipment: light DB pair or a kettlebell held behind the body
exercises.notes: **Protective shrug (greasing set).** 1 light set held behind the body, palms back. Pack the shoulders DOWN and BACK, shrug UP and slightly back, 1s peak squeeze, slow down. The 'opposite movement' that decompresses the right shoulder — costs nothing, easy to forget.

sets.name: Banded Shoulder Prep (~3 min)

exercises.notes: Mini-band overhead OR blue rope band gripped in hands.
Elbows drive to the ribs, scaps depress.
Press out to a T — fires rear delts and mid-traps.
Pull apart at the sternum, scaps retract, ribs down.
Sweep the arms back. Don't overarch.
15s each side. Primes the lateral hinge for the OTD-flow bent press + windmill.
Both arms in a V/Y overhead. Hold and breathe — lower traps fire.

sets.notes: 1 round of all 7 banded moves (~3 min). Sustained tension, no rest between positions.

sets.name: 🔆🌀 Flow + Coordination (NEW permanent block — Spotlight: Figure-8 → Reverse Lunge)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 15-20lb. Warm-up familiar — the base around-the-body pass.
- Hold the bell at waist height, **pass it around the body in a smooth circle** — hand to hand behind the back and in front
- **Core tight, torso quiet** — the bell tries to pull you into rotation; resist it
- 8 passes one direction, then 8 the other. Smooth and continuous — this primes the grip + coordination for the figure-8.

**LOAD:** 15-20lb (LIGHT — coordination, not load). 3 rounds, 5 each leg.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — learn the weave-to-lunge cleanly:**

- **Chest up, eyes forward** through the figure-8; don't round over the bell
- **The figure-8 cues hip rotation; the lunge anchors it** — coordination drill first, conditioning second

**Reflection:** does the hand-off in the figure-8 stay smooth (no fumble, bell close to the body) and flow straight into the lunge — or do the two halves feel like separate moves you stop between? The skill is making it one continuous weave-to-lunge. New move; clean reps over fast reps.

name: Week 16 Legs — Steady State, Station-Grouped (Spotlight: Seated Leg Curl + Calf Raise)
description: Volume steady, station-grouped. Squat steps to 80/side, keeping the 6/7/8/8 rep volume — reps stay the progression lever, not heavier load. dayOverview.theme: Steady state, station-grouped. Squat steps to 80 / 6-7-8-8 (reps stay the lever); leg press steps to 4 plates, deep ROM held. Leg curl + calf raise get the spotlight refresh — leg curl for the slow-tempo feel, calf raise for the deep heel-drop eccentric. Leg curl before incline RDL so the hamstring work doesn't stack.

Cycles forward — last spotlighted W12. The slow eccentric started biting hard at 3 plates. Spotlight drills the deep heel-drop off the platform edge + the 3-4s eccentric at double-leg — the single-leg conversation waits until the double-leg eccentric is fully dialed.

watchpoints: **Loads** — squat steps to 80/side, leg press 4 plates (ROM first), calf raise 3 plates, leg curl 90, incline RDL 45lb plate, Bulgarian 50lb (optional 60 if easy).

**Keep leg curl BEFORE incline RDL.** Reversed, the two hamstring lifts stack and smoke the second — keep the prescribed order.
**Bulgarian holds 50lb** — single DB (suitcase); optional bump to 60 if 50 feels easy. If anything twitches/spasms, drop to bodyweight and finish — the standing rule on this lift.
**QL/psoas watch** — cross-leg lateral lean in the warmup AND cool-down. If anything talks in the warmup, modify the day; mid-session, drop a set.

sets.name: Warmup (incl. Cross-Leg Lateral Lean — QL/Psoas Release)

Big slow circles. Wake up the hip stabilizers.
Spine mobility — slow, full ROM each direction.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension. Quick posterior-chain and low-back opener before loading the squat.

- Bar high on the upper traps (NOT the neck), upper-back shelf squeezed
- **Brace like prepping for a punch** — deep belly breath at the top, HOLD through the descent, exhale on the drive up
- **Hips back AND down**, not just down
- 'Spread the floor' — screw the feet into the ground
- Knees track over the toes
- **Sit into the bottom** — keep chasing the depth set by set, even as the load steps up
- Drive through the WHOLE foot

**Reflection:** the reps may land a little short of 8/8 on the first session at 80 — that's fine, build them back up over the coming weeks at this weight. Does the depth hold at 80 the way it did at 75? If the bottom shortens to make the number, ease back. Depth + reps, not heavier load.

sets.name: Leg Press + Calf Raise Station (Same Machine)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 4 plates/side — the new go-to. The deep knees-to-chest ROM still comes first: if 4 plates shortens the ROM or lets the lower back lift off the pad, drop back to 3 plates. ROM is the work; the load follows it.
- **Foot position:** shoulder-width, mid-foot on the platform, slight toe-out
- **Full ROM — knees toward the chest.** This deep position trains the abs/QL/core more than the quads — that's the intent
- **It feels harder cold** — the deep ROM opens up once the hips are warm (the warmup + squat before it prime this), so don't judge the load on set 1
- **Actively press to keep the lower back from lifting off the pad** at the bottom; if the hips roll off the pad, back off a hair
- **Press through the WHOLE foot** — heels grounded
- **Slow descent (3s), no bounce at the bottom**

sets.name: 🔆 Leg-Press Calf Raise (Spotlight — Same Machine, Stays Right Here)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 3 plates/side. 3 sets of 15. Stay on the leg press — same machine, no walking off.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the deep heel-drop + slow eccentric, drilled:**
- **Balls of both feet on the BOTTOM EDGE of the platform, heels hanging off** — no plate under the foot; the platform edge gives the heel drop
- **Both feet on the platform** — double-leg
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the heels drop as far below the edge as they'll go. That deep stretch is the growth signal
- **Drive to FULL plantarflexion at the top**
- **3-4s eccentric** — the slow descent is the stimulus, not added load; it started biting hard at 3 plates
- **1s squeeze at the peak**, no bouncing. Breath continuous, don't hold

**Reflection:** does the 3-4s eccentric stay honest (no rushing) at the deep heel-drop for all 3 sets at 3 plates? When the slow double-leg eccentric is fully dialed and starts feeling easy, that's the cue to open the single-leg conversation — not before.

exercises.equipment: bench + DBs — Smith machine if free (use smith-machine-bulgarian-split-squat)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** single 50lb DB (suitcase) — hold the stepped-up load; optional bump to 60 if 50 feels easy. 3 sets of 8-10 each leg.
- **Rear foot up on the bench** behind you, laces down or toes tucked
- **Step out far enough that the front shin stays roughly VERTICAL at the bottom** — too short a stance = the knee crashes past the toes
- **Front knee tracks over the front foot** — not caving in
- **Lower until the rear knee nearly touches the floor** — controlled, no dropping
- **Drive up through the FRONT HEEL** — the front leg does the work, the rear leg is a kickstand
- **Torso TALL** — a slight forward lean is fine, no folding over
- **2s descent**, own the bottom

**Watch:** if anything twitches/spasms, drop to bodyweight for the remaining sets and finish.

sets.name: 🔆 Seated Leg Curl (Spotlight — 3 Sets at 90, Before Incline RDL)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 90. 3 sets of 12, slow tempo.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the slow-tempo feel you get here, drilled clean:**
- **Ankles UNDER the pad** — the ankle bone is the contact point, NOT the mid-calf
- **Settings: 5/m/0/1** (verify before loading)
- **Lap pad locked DOWN firmly** — a loose pad lets the torso lift and turns it into lower-back work
- **Curl the heels toward the glutes** — full ROM, full squeeze
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze** — the slow eccentric is the whole stimulus; you feel these deeply when you go slow
- Torso anchored to the seat, no lifting forward; no bouncing out of the bottom

**Reflection:** with the ankle-under-pad contact and the pad locked tight, does the squeeze stay in the hamstring (not the lower back) on the slow eccentric for all 3 sets? This comes BEFORE incline RDL on purpose — take the leg curl fresh.

**LOAD:** 45lb plate. 3 sets of 15, dead slow with a 2s pause at the bottom.
- **Pad just below the hip crease** — NOT on the upper thigh, NOT on the stomach
- **Hip hinge** — a Romanian deadlift on the 45° bench, NOT a lumbar extension. Lower back NEUTRAL throughout
- **At the bottom:** the stretch is in the **hamstrings and glutes**, NOT the lower back. If the lumbar rounds, you're going too deep for current mobility
- **Drive up by squeezing the glutes and hamstrings**
- **At the top:** stop at neutral. Past neutral = lumbar load = QL irritation
- **Tempo: 3s eccentric, 2s pause at the bottom, 1s drive up.** The slow eccentric is the entire reason this lift works
- Take extra rest between sets if you need it

**Reflection:** where's the stretch landing — hamstrings/glutes (correct) or lower back (too deep / pad placement off)? If lower back, slow down further and check the pad before set 2.

**📍 PUSH DAYS** — serratus activation, helps unstick a tight pec minor.

**📍 PUSH DAYS (optional)** — pins the shoulder blades in the corrected position.

watchpoints: **Behind-back shrug stays FIRST (activation slot).** Front-loading it kept the last pull day flare-free — it's the protective counter-movement to all the pulling and can't be the piece a rushed session drops. Do it right after the warmup.

**DB row → 70/80/90, no straps.** Drop the 60 opener; the new top set is 90 for ~5-6 reps. Grip is the limiter (left hand taps out first) — that's deliberate, train the grip rather than bypass it. Set the DB down when grip gives.

**Grip is the new ceiling on the pulling lifts, not the shoulder** — DB row, lat pulldown, and the push-day farmer carry all tap out at grip now. The shoulder has recovered enough that grip is the honest limiter; no straps.
**Face pull steps to 45** — the elbows-high / external-rotate cue is locked ('feeling it in the back'), so the load can move now.
**Loads otherwise hold** — chest-supported row 40, pull-up bodyweight, high cable curl 170, reverse fly 20, cable crunch pulley 77.5.
**Shoulder management: ramp the tempo** — don't make every set all-slow-eccentric at once. The one flare this cluster was volume/time-under-tension, not weight.

exercises.notes: Scap activation. Squeeze the shoulder blades together, soft elbow.
Spine warm — slow, full ROM each direction.
Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — primes grip and the pulling chain before bar work.
Active hang, not collapsed — engage the lats, pull the shoulders DOWN away from the ears even at full extension.

sets.name: Behind-Back DB Shrug — Protective Activation (DO THIS FIRST)

exercises.equipment: DB pair, held behind the body
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40-50lb pair. 3 sets — first in the session.

**Why it's here, first:** this is the 'opposite movement' to all the pulling — a counter/decompression for the right shoulder. Front-loading it kept the last pull day flare-free. It reads more like a stretch than a lift; that's the point.
- **DBs held BEHIND the body** at the sides of the hips/glutes — palms facing back
- **Shoulders pull DOWN and BACK** at the start — packed, not relaxed
- **Shrug UP and slightly BACK** — pinch the shoulder blades at the top
- **Hold 1s at the top**, slow descent
- **Pack DOWN, NOT up** as the resting position — the lower position IS the work
- Chest open, not slouched

sets.notes: Protective trap-chain activation, front of the session. ~4 min. Light-to-moderate, peak-squeeze — a decompression, not a max effort. A light 1-set greasing version also lives in the push + KB-day warmups.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** Bodyweight. 4 sets of 6-8.
- **Straight bar** — the variant that's been feeling best
- **Active hang start**, not collapsed
- **Pull elbows DOWN to ribs**, NOT chin to bar
- **Chest leads to the bar at the top**, eyes ahead, head neutral
- **Slow eccentric ~2-3s**, active hang at the bottom of every rep — no dropping
- **Stop the set when the rep stops being clean** — never kip. The limiter now is strength + clean form, not the shoulder; quality reps, frequency over max effort.

sets.name: 🔆 DB Rack / Bench Block — Chest-Supported Row + DB Row + Incline Curl (Spotlight) + Reverse Fly (3 Rounds)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40. 3 sets of 10-12.
- **Chest stays GLUED to the incline bench** — if the chest peels off to heave the DBs, the weight's ahead of the form
- **Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit** — keeps it in the lats
- **Don't rotate the torso** — both sides of the chest stay on the pad
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze** at the top, no DB slam at the bottom
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the shoulder blade protract, then re-pull

**LOAD:** 70/80/90 ascending pyramid — one set per round (70, then 80, then 90). No straps.
- **Chest-supported on the incline bench** — same setup as the chest-supported row
- **Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit**
- **Don't rotate the torso** — chest glued, no twisting up
- **Slow 2s descent, 1s squeeze** on the 70/80 sets; the 90 is the heavier top-end set — ~5-6 reps, drive the elbow, control the descent
- **Grip is the limiter** (left hand first) — set the DB down when grip gives, not when the back fails. The slower 70/80 sets double as grip work.

**LOAD:** 25lb. 3 sets of 8-10. Preacher-style chest-supported curl (the preacher-bench replacement).

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — lock in the both-arms-equal pattern that just cleared:**
- **Set the incline bench to ~45°, lean in chest-first** — armpit and the back of the upper arm flat on the pad
- **Arm hangs down the face of the pad**, underhand grip; the upper arm stays flat on the pad the ENTIRE rep (don't lift the elbow off)
- **Left arm first, every set** — keep the protocol as insurance
- **Full stretch at the bottom — pause 2s**
- **Curl smoothly to the peak squeeze**, no swing; 2-3s eccentric
- **Both arms unsupported, no spotting hand** — the left held this last time even late in the session; the work is keeping both sides equal in quality

**Reflection:** does the left hold the same clean slow-eccentric + bottom-pause as the right for all 3 sets, even at the end of the block? If it does, the weak-left chapter is closed — the floor has risen.

**LOAD:** 20lb. 3 sets of 12 — strict tempo, cap at 12 with a slower eccentric rather than chasing reps.
- **30° reverse-incline** (chest-down on the incline bench)
- DBs hanging fully extended at the start, **soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED throughout**
- **Lead with the elbow, hand passive**
- **Wings out and slightly UP to shoulder height** — sweep, don't lift
- **Hold the top a beat, then 2s eccentric** — keep building the slow drop you've been working

sets.notes: One trip to the DB rack covers all 4 lifts. Incline bench at ~30° for the rows + reverse fly (30° reverse-incline), set to ~45° for the incline curl. 3 rounds.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD (pick whichever station's free, log which one):**
- **Dual pulley: 70** ('very little pain' here lately — the current home)
- **Regular lat pulldown machine: 140**
- **Cable column: 52.5-57.5**
- **Cable pulley: 47.5**

3 sets.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — drill the cue while the shoulder's quiet:**
- **Wide grip near the bend** — more lat isolation, less bicep
- **Slight backward lean ~15°, NO further** — more = it becomes a row
- **Pull the bar to the UPPER CHEST — NEVER behind the neck**
- **'Lats squeezing oranges into the back pockets'** at the bottom
- **1s pause at the contraction, 2s controlled return** to a full overhead stretch
- Knees pinned firmly under the pad
- **Grip is the limiter at the end** — same as DB row; that's fine, it's the honest cap

**Reflection:** at dual-pulley 70 with the wide grip, does the work stay in the lats (back-pocket squeeze) with the shoulder quiet, or does grip end the set before the lats are done? If grip is consistently the ender, that confirms the shoulder's no longer the ceiling here — settle dual-pulley 70 as the home.

sets.name: Cable Column — Face Pull (3 Sets, Step to 45)

exercises.equipment: cable column (mid/upper-chest height + rope)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** cable column 45 (step up — the cue's locked, the load can move).
- **Pull the rope to face level** — not to the chest
- **ELBOWS HIGH (above the shoulders)** — the make-or-break cue; this is what moved the work into the back
- **External-rotate at the top** — knuckles point UP, like the top of a double-biceps pose
- **1s peak hold**, then a slow 2s return — let the cable pull the arms back, don't drop
- Rear-delt + mid-trap + external-rotator health work — the right-shoulder-protective end of pull day
- **If the front of the shoulder takes over, the elbows have dropped** — re-set them high. If 45 drops the elbows, go back to 42.5.

sets.name: Cable Column Finisher — High Cable Curl + Cable Crunch (2-3 Sets)

exercises.equipment: cable column (low pulley, single D-handle, one arm at a time)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD (single arm — scales differ, log which station):**
- Cable column (single D-handle): 170
- Pulley / weight-stack station: ~120
2 working sets per arm.
- **Single arm at a time, one D-handle** — stand sideways, arm out at shoulder level
- **Upper arm parallel to the floor, FIXED** — the whole point of the high-cable variant
- **Curl the hand toward the ear**, peak squeeze
- **Left arm first**; slow eccentric, no bounce at the start

**LOAD (pick whichever station's free, log which one):**
- **Cable pulley (rope): 77.5** (the working number — 'really hard,' slow eccentrics not available here yet)
- **Cable column (rope): ~120**

3 sets.
- **Kneel under the high cable**
- **HIPS LOCKED** — the most important cue. The hips do not move.
- **Crunch from the abs ONLY** — the spine flexes, the hips stay put. Hips moving = hip-flexor work, not abs.
- **Chest toward the thighs**, hold the crunch 1 second
- **Slow eccentric where you can** — 77.5 bites hard enough that the slow drop isn't fully available, which means it's the right load. Hold it.

sets.notes: Same cable column as the face pull. 2 rounds = 2 sets each; round the cable crunch to 3 if there's time and the abs aren't fried.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow position. Pec minor lengthen.
Passive hang. Don't engage — let the shoulders unpack and the spine decompress.
30s each side. Draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
45s each side. Hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Parasympathetic shift.

sets.notes: 5 minutes of recovery work, non-negotiable closing block.

tips: **Behind-back shrug stays FIRST** — protective decompression that kept the last pull day flare-free. It can't be the piece a rushed session drops.
**DB row → 70/80/90, no straps.** Drop the 60; new top set is 90 for ~5-6 reps. Grip is the limiter (left hand) and that's deliberate — train it, don't bypass it.
**Spotlight: lat pulldown + incline curl.** Lat pulldown drills the wide-grip / bar-to-chest cue at dual-pulley 70; incline curl drills the both-arms-equal pattern that finally cleared.
**Face pull steps to 45** — the elbows-high cue is locked, so the load can move.
**Grip is the new ceiling on pulling, not the shoulder** — DB row, lat pulldown, farmer carry all tap out at grip now. No straps.
**Loads otherwise hold** — chest-supported row 40, pull-up bodyweight, high cable curl 170, reverse fly 20, cable crunch pulley 77.5.
**Shoulder management: ramp the tempo** — don't make every set all-slow-eccentric at once.
**Left bicep first, every set** — keep the protocol as insurance.
