**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, permanent every gym day.**
Rest: shrug 60s, 2.5 min pull-ups, 90s DB block, 2 min lat pulldown, 90s face pull, 60s finisher.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state pull week with the protective shrug leading, which is the change that kept the shoulder quiet. The DB row earns a heavier top-end set with grip — not straps — as the honest cap, by the user's call. Face pull earns its load step now that the cue landed. The spotlights lock in two wins while the shoulder's clear: the lat pulldown cue and the both-arms-equal curl. Building decades, not weeks.

name: Week 16 Push — Steady State (Spotlight: Lateral Raise + Kinesis Fly)
description: Volume steady, loads steady. Spotlights cycle forward to the DB lateral raise + Kinesis cable fly — the two shoulder-isolation lifts due for a deep-cue refresh, and the two that feel best on the right shoulder right now. Push press runs early when the rack's free (it recovers reps there); tempo is your energy lever — fast-drive or slow-eccentric, your call by feel. Chest press keeps the cross-body arm stretch between sets. Cable lifts list a number per equipment option.

dayOverview.theme: Steady state — sets and loads hold. Spotlight cycles forward to DB lateral raise + Kinesis fly. Push press runs early when the rack's open; tempo (fast-drive vs slow-eccentric) is your energy lever. Chest press keeps the cross-body stretch between sets. Pull-up greasing + protective shrug stay in the warmup.

spotlights.why: Cycles forward — last spotlighted W12. The last set's final reps have been breaking form at 15lb. Spotlight drills lead-with-the-elbow + the 2s eccentric so all three sets hold clean at 15, and bakes in the scap-reset-between-sets habit that quiets the shoulder.

Cycles forward — last spotlighted W12. This is the lift the right shoulder/pec likes best — the slow-eccentric stretch reads as relief, not pain. Spotlight drills the fixed soft elbow + the deep loaded stretch, the most shoulder-friendly pec work on the day.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W13 cable column block · W14 push press + incline DB · W15 chest press + farmer carry · W16 lateral raise + Kinesis fly (current) · W17 cycle forward — push press + incline DB refresh.
watchpoints: **Run push press early when the rack's free** — it recovered to 8/10/8 there. If it ends up second after a long warmup trail, expect ~7/6/6 at 45 — that's the accepted trade-off for getting the session in.
**Tempo is your energy lever** — fast-drive (bank energy for later) or slow-eccentric (more stimulus). Pick by feel; neither is the 'right' one. Form holds either way.
**Cable lateral raise holds at cable column 30** — two straight pain-free weeks. Don't chase load while the streak is alive. (Distinct from the DB lateral raise spotlight — the day has both.)
**Pack DOWN, not up** — push press, both lateral raises, incline DB, chest press, farmer carry all carry the cue. If a lockout needs a shrug, the load's too heavy for the cue — pause the set.
**Chest press: cross-body arm stretch between every set** — proactively, it keeps the right pec quiet. The win on chest press is a quiet pec, not the rep count.
**Pull-up greasing set + protective behind-back shrug stay in the warmup** — both cheap, both easy to forget. Part of the weekly pull-up + shoulder-decompression frequency.
**Cable block lists a number per machine** — pick what's free, log the equipment + number you used.

sets.name: Warmup + Shoulder Rehab (Non-Negotiable) + Pull-Up Greasing + Protective Shrug

exercises.notes: Slow, big circles. Wake up scap glide before loading.
Full sequence with red band. Non-negotiable on push day.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — dials a stretch up the back chain from forearm to shoulder. Wakes the grip and shoulder line before loading.
Ribs down, glutes tight, body in one line. Slow eccentric, 1s pause with chest 1-2" off the floor.

**Pull-up greasing set.** 1 fresh set, slow tempo, NOT to failure. Active hang start, pull elbows down to ribs, chest leads. Frequency, not max effort — drop to scapular-pulls only if the shoulder talks, and finish the count.

**Protective shrug (greasing set).** 1 light set, DBs held behind the body, palms back. Pack the shoulders DOWN and BACK, shrug UP and slightly back, 1s peak squeeze, slow down. The 'opposite movement' that decompresses the right shoulder — costs no time, easy to forget.

**LOAD:** 45lb DBs per side. 3 sets of 8-10 (7/6/6 is fine if these run second — see the order watchpoint).
- **Feet parallel, hip-width** — not duck stance
- **Ribs DOWN before the dip** — catch any rib flare on set 1
- **Pack DOWN, not up** — shoulder blades into the back pockets, neck long
- **Shallow dip ~3-4"**, straight down through the heels
- **Vertical DB path** — DBs travel up next to the ears, head pokes through at the top
- **Tempo is your call** — fast-drive to bank energy, or slow eccentric for more stimulus. Drive fast, lockout solid; the descent matches the tempo you pick. Breath: in at the dip, out on the drive

**LOAD:** 15lb DBs. 3 sets of 15-18.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — make all three sets hold the form, not just the first two:**
- **Lead with the elbow, hand passive** — the wrist follows the elbow, the hand never lifts first
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED** through the whole rep — a locking/unlocking elbow recruits the traps
- **'Pour the water out of two cups'** at the top — a hair of internal rotation, pinky leads up
- **Stop at shoulder height — never higher.** Higher just shrugs the traps off the medial delt
- **2s eccentric** — the slow descent is the entire stimulus; fight the drop
- **Scap reset between sets** — roll the shoulders, actively engage/disengage the scapula a few times before the next set. This is what's kept the right shoulder quiet here.

**Reflection:** the last set's final reps have been breaking down at 15. Does the scap reset + a strict 2s eccentric hold the form clean to the end of set 3, or does it still break? If it breaks, that's the honest ceiling at 15 — hold, don't add load.

sets.name: Incline DB Press (3 Sets at 45 pair)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 45lb pair. 3 sets — run the controlled-descent version that landed best (10-12 with a pause at the bottom + a controlled, not-quite-slow descent).
- **Bench at 30°**, not 45° — steeper biases front delt over upper chest
- **Shoulders packed back AND down** — pin the back of the shoulder into the bench
- **Forearm stacked vertically over the elbow at the bottom** — the cue that makes 45 feel honest
- **Elbows ~45° from torso**, not flared to 90°
- **1s pause at the bottom** ('dead weight'), press to a fingerwidth apart at the top. Breath: in on descent, out on press

**LOAD:** 165. 3 sets.
- **Seat height: handles at the mid-chest / nipple line** — set it before sitting; the wrong height loads the front of the shoulder
- **Shoulders pinned BACK against the pad** — hold it the whole set
- **Tempo is the lever:** on a genuine 3s slow eccentric, 6 clean reps is the honest number here — don't force the rep count to match a fast-tempo week. The win is the right pec staying quiet, not the reps.
- **Press to almost extension** — leave a hair of bend
- **Ribs down** — no arching off the pad
- **🔁 BETWEEN EVERY SET: cross-body arm stretch on the right side** — pull the arm across the chest, 20-30s. Do it proactively; it's kept the right pec quiet.

If 165 craters below ~5 on a slow eccentric and the pec stays quiet, that's fine — you're strong-enough here and the management goal is met. Drop to 150-155 only if you want the higher rep count back at the slow tempo.

**LOAD:** Kinesis 9 (the working number now — drop to 8 only if 9 feels off on set 1).

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the shoulder-friendly pec stretch, drilled:**
- **Slight forward hinge at the hips** — chest leads, not the head
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED throughout** — these are NOT presses; the elbow angle never changes
- **'Hug a tree'** — the squeeze comes from the chest, not the arms pulling together
- **Stop a fistwidth apart at the top** — don't crash the handles; the last inches are arm work
- **Slow eccentric (~3s)** — let the cables pull the arms back into the deep pec stretch. The right shoulder/pec likes this stretch — it reads as relief, that loaded-lengthen 'everything stretching out' feeling. Protect that.

**Reflection:** does the slow loaded stretch keep the pec/shoulder feeling relieved (not pinched) across all 3 sets at 9? If it does, this is the template for shoulder-friendly chest work — note what the stretch feels like.

sets.name: Cable Column Block — Lat Raise → Tri Ext → Straight-Arm Pulldown (3 Rounds)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:**
- **Cable column: 30** (hold — two pain-free weeks running)
- **Kinesis: 5-6** (the W9-swap default, if the column's taken)

3 rounds, one arm at a time.
- **Lead with the elbow as a DIRECTION** — the elbow points, doesn't bend
- **Soft elbow ~10°, FIXED** throughout
- **Stand sideways** to the stack, working arm farther from it
- **Stop at shoulder height — higher = traps**
- **2s eccentric**, fight the cable down

**LOAD:**
- **Cable column: 70** (default)
- **Kinesis: 5** (fallback)

3 rounds. **Always kneeling — there's no bench at this station; the forward torso lean IS the 'incline.'**
- **Kneel facing AWAY from the high pulley**, rope overhead
- **Elbows PINNED** — only the forearms move
- **Hands shoulder-width on the rope**
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the rope pull the hands behind the head
- **Stop just shy of lockout**, slow eccentric. Set 1 feels easy, set 3 is brutal — that's the lift working.

**LOAD:**
- **Cable column: 120** (the working number — really hard here)
- **Kinesis: 6** (fallback)

3 rounds.
- **Stand a step back, hinge ~15° at the hips** — fixed hinge, the torso doesn't pump
- **Slight elbow bend (~5°), FIXED throughout**
- **Pull the bar to the thighs, NOT past** — past = shoulders roll forward, lats switch off
- **Squeeze the lats hard at the bottom** — 'oranges into the back pockets'
- **Slow controlled return to a full overhead stretch.** Hold 120 — reps may fall on the later sets; that's the load biting, not a problem.

sets.notes: Cable block — sharp cues, 3 rounds. One trip to the chosen station covers all three. Pick what's free (cable column is the default for all three) and log what you used.

sets.name: Farmer Carry (3 Walks)

exercises.equipment: DB rack
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 50lb DBs. 3 walks of ~45-60s each — chase hold-time now that 50 is the load and the shoulder stays neutral.
- **Stand TALL** — ribs down, crown reaching up, no leaning back
- **Shoulders pulled DOWN and BACK** — into the back pockets, never shrugged toward the ears. The DBs pull the shoulders up the whole walk; resist the whole walk
- **Neck long, eyes forward** — no chin poke
- **Grip firm but NOT death-clenched** — grip is the limiter here (it taps out before the shoulder), so let it be the trainable edge; set the bells down when grip fails rather than white-knuckling
- **Walk a straight line at a deliberate pace**, breathing steadily

sets.notes: Trap-chain + grip block. 3 walks at 50lb — packed-shoulder posture, and grip as the honest edge. Set them down when grip gives, not before.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow position. Pec minor lengthen — the antagonist to the upper-trap chain loaded all session.
Passive hang from the pull-up bar. **Don't engage** — let the shoulders unpack and the spine decompress.
30s each side on the mat. Draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
45s each side. Front leg + back leg at 90°. Sink the hips toward the floor — hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Knees wide, arms extended forward. Parasympathetic shift before leaving the gym.

sets.notes: 5 minutes of recovery work, non-negotiable closing block.

tips: **Steady state — sets and loads hold.** The work is depth of execution at the established numbers.
**Spotlight: DB lateral raise + Kinesis fly.** Lateral raise drills the elbow-lead + 2s eccentric so all 3 sets hold at 15; Kinesis fly drills the shoulder-friendly loaded stretch at 9.
**Run push press early when the rack's free.** Tempo (fast-drive vs slow-eccentric) is your energy lever — pick by feel.
**Cable lateral raise holds at cable column 30** — two pain-free weeks; don't chase load.
**Cross-body arm stretch between every chest-press set** — proactively. A quiet pec is the win, not the rep count; 6 clean slow-eccentric reps at 165 is honest.
**Pack DOWN, not up** — every press + the carry carries the cue.
**Pull-up greasing set + protective shrug in the warmup** — 1 slow set each, not to failure.
**Farmer carry: 50lb, chase hold-time** — grip is the edge; set them down when grip gives.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, permanent every gym day.**
Rest: 2 min push press + chest press, 90s lateral raise + Kinesis fly + farmer carry, 75s cable block.

sets.name: 🔆🌀 Flow + Coordination (permanent block — Spotlight: Figure-8 Weave)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 15-20lb. Warm-up familiar — the base around-the-body pass.
- Hold the bell at waist height, **pass it around the body in a smooth circle** — hand to hand behind the back and in front
- **Core tight, torso quiet** — the bell tries to pull you into rotation; resist it
- 8 passes one direction, then 8 the other. Smooth and continuous — primes the grip + coordination for the figure-8.

**LOAD:** 15-20lb (LIGHT — coordination, not load). 3 rounds, 8 each direction.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the smooth figure-8 weave:**
- **Feet wider than shoulder-width, slight squat** — stay low and tall-chested, but this is NOT a leg burner; the bend just clears the path for the bell
- **Pass the bell between the legs in a figure-8** — one hand hands it off to the other from front to back, weaving the 8 around the legs
- **Bell stays close to the body** — a tight orbit, not a wide loop
- **Core braced, torso quiet** — the weave tries to pull you into rotation; resist it
- **Eyes forward, chest up** — don't round over the bell to chase the hand-off
- **Smooth and continuous** — grip + coordination, not speed

**Reflection:** does the hand-off stay smooth and the bell stay close (no fumble, no wide loop) for all 3 rounds — or does it get sloppy as the grip tires? The skill is one continuous clean weave. New move; clean reps over fast reps.

sets.notes: **Permanent Flow + Coordination block.** Base KB skill-building — light bell, flowing coordination. A familiar pass to warm up, then this week's new skill. 3 rounds, ~5 min, short rest. Keep it light and clean; this precedes the strength + flow work and shouldn't fatigue you.

sets.name: OTD Flow (Light Groove — Skill Practice)

exercises.notes: Bell starts on the floor between the feet, hips drive the lift, catch in the rack with the knees slightly bent.
Goblet/rack position. **LIGHT** — Thursday before Friday legs, keep depth without grinding. Sit tall, full depth, no bouncing.
Stride out wide, sit into the working leg, keep the other leg long. Mobility, not strength.

The deliberate leverage move inside the flow — **the body goes DOWN, the bell barely moves.** From the rack, hinge and rotate AWAY from the bell side, eyes tracking the bell, until the arm locks out overhead — you lower your body under the bell, you don't press it up. Slow and smooth; it's leverage, not a press.
Control on the way down — bell to the floor as cleanly as it came up. Closes the flow before switching sides.

sets.notes: **This is a continuous FLOW, not separate stations.** Move through the full chain on ONE side — dead clean → front squat → lateral lunge → bent press → tactical clean — letting each move feed the next, then repeat the whole flow on the other side. About 2 reps' worth at each move, don't stop to count. **~20-25lb throughout, 2 rounds. Light groove** — it should feel effortless. If the 25lb bell is taken, the next bell up (35lb) is the fallback — but keep it light; Friday legs is tomorrow.

- **Hinge and rotate AWAY from the bell side** — push the hip out toward the bell side, fold at the hip
- **Eyes track the bell the WHOLE time** — the bell stays stacked over the shoulder
- **The stretch lives in the hip/hamstring of the bell side**, NOT the lower back — long spine, don't round to reach
- **Weak side gets the deliberate reps.** Slow up, slow down. Right shoulder watch — keep it stacked; drop the load before the bell drifts forward.

**LOAD:** 18-20lb. Maintenance.
- Bell locked overhead, eye tracks the bell
- **Hip hinge AWAY from the bell side**
- **Stretch lives in the back leg's hip flexor, NOT the lower back**
- Long spine throughout, slow descent and controlled return.

- Eyes ON the bell at every checkpoint; pause at every checkpoint — the reverse is half the lift

- **Ribs down, stand tall** — the twist comes from the core/obliques, NOT the lower back

formPhilosophy: Two sections on KB Tuesday — a flow and a workout. The flow is a single-bell leggy complex chained for continuity, the lower-body cousin of the OTD flow; skill comes from connecting the moves smoothly, not from a max load. The Strength + Conditioning block that follows is the workout section — pull, posterior, and core work the lateral flow doesn't cover, so the day lands as genuinely full-body, not flow-only. The shoulder scaffolding (banded prep, protective shrug, cooldown) stays because that's the part that protects the joint; the flow tops out at the rack and the strength block is all pulls / hinges / swings, so the whole day stays off the overhead — a genuinely easy-shoulder day. Loads stay moderate; the lateral squat clean spotlight drills leg-driven power, not the number. Building decades, not weeks.

name: Week 17 Legs — Steady State, Station-Grouped (Spotlight: Squat Depth + Incline RDL)
description: Volume steady, station-grouped. Squat holds at 80/side with the 6/7/8/8 rep volume — keep building the reps back toward 8/8 at this load; reps are the progression lever, not heavier weight. Leg press holds at 4 plates with the deep knees-to-chest ROM as the priority. Spotlights cycle forward to the squat (depth under the stepped-up load) and the incline RDL (the dead-slow hinge where tempo is the whole progression). Leg curl stays before incline RDL so the two hamstring lifts don't stack. Bulgarian holds its load.

dayOverview.theme: Steady state, station-grouped. Squat holds 80 / 6-7-8-8 (build the reps back, keep the depth); leg press holds 4 plates, deep ROM first. Squat depth + incline RDL get the spotlight refresh — squat for holding depth at 80, incline RDL for the dead-slow hinge. Leg curl before incline RDL so the hamstring work doesn't stack.

spotlights.why: Cycles forward — at the stepped-up 80 the job is holding the same depth that ran clean at 75 while the reps build back to 8/8. Spotlight drills the brace + hips-back-and-down + sit-into-the-bottom so depth leads and the load follows.

Cycles forward — the dead-slow hinge where tempo, not load, is the progression. Spotlight drills the pad-below-the-hip-crease placement + the hamstring/glute stretch (not lower back) + the 3s eccentric / 2s bottom pause at the 45lb plate.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W15 leg press + Bulgarian · W16 leg curl + calf raise · W17 squat depth + incline RDL (current) · W18 cycle forward — leg press ROM + Bulgarian refresh.
watchpoints: **Loads** — squat 80/side (6-7-8-8), leg press 4 plates (ROM first), calf raise 4 plates, leg curl 90, incline RDL 45lb plate, Bulgarian two 40lb DBs (one per hand).

**Squat holds 80 / 6-7-8-8.** Keep building the reps back toward 8/8 at this load — reps are the progression lever, not heavier weight. Keep the depth; if the bottom shortens to make the number, ease back.
**Station-grouped sequence:** warmup → squat → leg press → leg-press-calf-raise (SAME machine, stay there) → Bulgarian (bench station) → leg curl → incline RDL → cool-down. No backtracking.
**Keep leg curl BEFORE incline RDL.** Reversed, the two hamstring lifts stack and smoke the second — keep the prescribed order.
**Bulgarian holds two 40lb DBs** — one per hand. If anything twitches/spasms, drop to bodyweight and finish — the standing rule on this lift.
**QL/psoas watch** — cross-leg lateral lean in the warmup AND cool-down. If anything talks in the warmup, modify the day; mid-session, drop a set.

sets.name: Warmup (incl. Cross-Leg Lateral Lean — QL/Psoas Release)

exercises.notes: Full depth, slow. Find where the hips are tight and breathe into it. Depth check before loading.

30s each side. Scissor one foot over the other, reach the same-side arm overhead, lean away from the back leg — the stretch runs down the side of the waist into the QL and lateral hip. Do this before loading the squat.
Big slow circles. Wake up the hip stabilizers.

Back to a wall, heels a step out, weight on the heels. Pull the toes UP toward the shins as high as they'll go, lower slow. Wakes up the shins (the calf's antagonist), preps ankle dorsiflexion for squat depth, and it's shin insurance for the run-in. ~30s, bodyweight.
Spine mobility — slow, full ROM each direction.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension. Quick posterior-chain and low-back opener before loading the squat.
Bodyweight. QL check — if anything talks here, modify the day. Also previews the Bulgarian pattern.
Set 1: 45/side x8. Set 2: 70/side x6 — heavy-ish primer before 80. Same depth as the working sets — the slightly-lighter-but-still-heavy primer is what's been adding the reps.

**LOAD:** 80/side. 4 sets: **6 / 7 / 8 / 8** — keep building the reps back toward 8/8 at this load; reps are the progression lever, not heavier weight. **Drop the last set (the 4th 8) if it feels heavy or unsteady** — bank 6/7/8 clean rather than grind a shaky 8.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — hold the depth at the stepped-up load:**
- Bar high on the upper traps (NOT the neck), upper-back shelf squeezed
- **Brace like prepping for a punch** — deep belly breath at the top, HOLD through the descent, exhale on the drive up
- **Hips back AND down**, not just down
- **'Spread the floor'** — screw the feet into the ground, knees track over the toes
- **Sit into the bottom** — keep chasing the depth set by set, even as the reps climb
- Drive through the WHOLE foot

**Reflection:** does the bottom depth at 80 match what it was at 75, or does the bottom shorten to make the rep? Depth leads, the reps build back over the coming weeks at this load, the weight waits. If the depth shortens, ease back.

sets.name: Leg Press + Calf Raise Station (Same Machine)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 4 plates/side. The deep knees-to-chest ROM comes first: if 4 plates shortens the ROM or lets the lower back lift off the pad, drop back to 3 plates. ROM is the work; the load follows it.
- **Foot position:** shoulder-width, mid-foot on the platform, slight toe-out
- **Full ROM — knees toward the chest.** This deep position trains the abs/QL/core more than the quads — that's the intent
- **It feels harder cold** — the deep ROM opens up once the hips are warm, so don't judge the load on set 1
- **Actively press to keep the lower back from lifting off the pad** at the bottom; if the hips roll off, back off a hair
- **Press through the WHOLE foot** — heels grounded
- **Slow descent (3s), no bounce at the bottom**
- **Don't lock out hard at the top** — leave a hair of bend. Breath: in on the descent, out on the drive

sets.name: Leg-Press Calf Raise (Same Machine, Stays Right Here)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 4 plates/side. 3 sets of 15. Stay on the leg press — same machine, no walking off.
- **Balls of both feet on the BOTTOM EDGE of the platform, heels hanging off** — the platform edge gives the heel drop
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the heels drop as far below the edge as they'll go
- **Drive to FULL plantarflexion at the top**
- **Tempo by feel** — own the stretch at the bottom and the squeeze at the top, no bouncing. Breath continuous.

exercises.equipment: bench + DBs — Smith machine if free (use smith-machine-bulgarian-split-squat)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** two 40lb DBs, one per hand. 3 sets of 8-10 each leg.
- **Rear foot up on the bench** behind you, laces down or toes tucked
- **Step out far enough that the front shin stays roughly VERTICAL at the bottom** — too short a stance = the knee crashes past the toes
- **Front knee tracks over the front foot** — not caving in
- **Lower until the rear knee nearly touches the floor** — controlled, no dropping
- **Drive up through the FRONT HEEL** — the front leg does the work, the rear leg is a kickstand
- **Torso TALL** — a slight forward lean is fine, no folding over
- **2s descent**, own the bottom

**Watch:** if anything twitches/spasms, drop to bodyweight for the remaining sets and finish.

sets.name: Seated Leg Curl (3 Sets at 90, Before Incline RDL)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 90. 3 sets of 12, slow tempo.
- **Ankles UNDER the pad** — the ankle bone is the contact point, NOT the mid-calf
- **Settings: 5/m/0/1** (verify before loading)
- **Lap pad locked DOWN firmly** — a loose pad lets the torso lift and turns it into lower-back work
- **Curl the heels toward the glutes** — full ROM, full squeeze
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze** — the slow eccentric is the whole stimulus; you feel these deeply when you go slow
- Torso anchored, no lifting forward, no bouncing out of the bottom. This comes BEFORE incline RDL on purpose — take it fresh.

**LOAD:** 45lb plate. 3 sets of 15, dead slow with a 2s pause at the bottom.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the dead-slow hinge where tempo is the progression:**
- **Pad just below the hip crease** — NOT on the upper thigh, NOT on the stomach
- **Hip hinge** — a Romanian deadlift on the 45° bench, NOT a lumbar extension. Lower back NEUTRAL throughout
- **At the bottom:** the stretch is in the **hamstrings and glutes**, NOT the lower back. If the lumbar rounds, you're going too deep for current mobility
- **Drive up by squeezing the glutes and hamstrings**; at the top, stop at neutral — past neutral = lumbar load = QL irritation
- **Tempo: 3s eccentric, 2s pause at the bottom, 1s drive up.** The slow eccentric is the entire reason this lift works — hold the 45lb plate and keep slowing the tempo; don't chase the load

**Reflection:** where's the stretch landing — hamstrings/glutes (correct) or lower back (too deep / pad placement off)? If lower back, slow down further and check the pad before set 2. The tempo is the lift; the number stays.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Recovery Block (Hip/QL-Biased for Legs Day)

exercises.notes: 30s each side. Scissor the legs, reach overhead, lean away from the back leg — bookend the session with the same QL/psoas release as the warmup.
45s each side. Deep hip-flexor and glute release — the long hold lets the QL and psoas let go.
30s each side. Gentle twist for the QL — draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
45s each side. Hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Knees wide, arms extended forward. Parasympathetic shift.

sets.notes: 5-min recovery block, hip/QL-biased on legs day.

tips: **Steady state, station-grouped.** Squat 4 sets, leg press 4, calf raise 3, Bulgarian 3, leg curl 3, incline RDL 3.
**Squat holds 80 / 6-7-8-8** — keep building the reps back toward 8/8; reps are the progression lever, not heavier weight.
**Spotlight: squat depth + incline RDL.** Squat drills holding depth at 80; incline RDL drills the dead-slow hinge at the 45lb plate.
**Station-grouped:** warmup → squat → leg press → leg-press-calf-raise (same machine — stay there) → Bulgarian → leg curl → incline RDL → cool-down. No backtracking.
**Leg curl BEFORE incline RDL** — don't reverse them, or the hamstring work stacks.
**Bulgarian holds two 40lb DBs** — one per hand. Drop to bodyweight if anything twitches.
**Incline RDL is a 45lb plate, dead slow** — the tempo is the progression, not the number.
**Cross-leg lateral lean in the warmup AND cool-down** — QL/psoas release.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, hip/QL-biased on legs day.**
Rest: 3 min squats, 2 min leg press, 90s calf raise + Bulgarian + isolations.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state legs week. The squat and incline RDL get the deep-cue treatment: the squat for holding depth at the stepped-up 80 while the reps build back, the incline RDL for the dead-slow hinge where tempo — not load — is the whole progression. The sequence keeps the two hamstring lifts from stacking and the station order from backtracking. Form leads load — building decades, not weeks.

name: W17 Morning Flow — Bodyweight Spine + Hip (All Days, Rotated Variety)
description: 15 min bodyweight floor flow — universal W17 morning flow, used every training day (Mon push / Tue KB / Wed pull / Thu KB / Fri legs). Same three-part shape as W11-W16 with rotated moves for variety. Three-part: spine primer → bodyweight work → deep stretch arc. Day-specific therapeutic add-on at the end (push = pec-minor protocol; pull = dead hang + scap pull; legs = cross-leg lateral lean + pigeon + supine twist; KB days skip — banded prep covers it).

exercises.notes: Slow, full ROM each direction. Spine wave wakes the segment-by-segment articulation.

Rotates in for W17 — 45s each side. From a low lunge, plant the inside hand and rotate the top arm open to the ceiling, eyes following the hand. Hip flexor lengthen + thoracic rotation in one shape — opens the front of the hip and the mid-back together.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — the wrist dials a stretch up the back chain. Stays in the primer.

sets.name: Work Block — Bodyweight Activation (~5 min)

exercises.notes: **Greasing set — 1 quick set, NEVER to failure.** Daily frequency is the point, not max effort (same idea as the pull-up greasing set — the floor rises over time). Elbows ~45° (not flared), ribs down, glutes tight, body one line, **pack down not up.** Stop 2-3 reps short. Back off / drop to knees if the right shoulder talks at the bottom.
Feet flat, drive through the heels, squeeze the glutes to a tall bridge, ribs down — no arching the lower back. Posterior-chain wake-up.
Rotates in for W17 — 30s. On the back, opposite arm + leg extend and return, lower back PRESSED into the floor the whole time. Anti-extension core; the floor counterpart to the bird-dog.
30s each side. Anti-rotation — opposite arm + leg extend, hold a beat, hips stay square (no swinging).
Rotates in for W17 — slow walkouts. From a forward fold, walk the hands out to a plank, hold a beat, walk back. Dynamic hamstring + shoulder + core warm-up that wakes the whole front line.
30s each side. The windmill on the floor — lateral-hinge cue translation. Thread the top arm under the body, then reach it back to the ceiling.

sets.notes: Opens with a pushup greasing set (1 quick set, never to failure — daily habit). Dead bug + inchworm rotate in for variety; glute bridge + bird-dog (anti-rotation) stay.

sets.name: Yoga Flow — Deep Stretch Arc (~7 min)

exercises.notes: 30s each side. Stays every week — signature spine move.

Rotates in for W17 — knees wide, shins parallel, sink the hips back toward the heels. Deep adductor + medial-hip opener; the adductors take a beating on KB days + the wide-stance leg work. Ease in slowly, breathe.
30s each side. Hip flexor + adductor + back-leg quad. Drop to elbows if accessible. Stays — durable hip opener.
Bodyweight, slow. Stays every week — mirrors the Tuesday loaded cossack.

Rotates in for W17 — sit in a wide straddle, reach toward one foot, then center (chest toward the floor), then the other foot. Slow, breathe into each reach. Straddle + adductor + hamstring opener — the wide-leg shape the CLAUDE.md flow design calls for.
30s each side. Long hold on the hip release to close the arc.

sets.notes: Continuous arc — flow between shapes, breathe deeply. Anchors stay (scorpion, lizard, cossack BW); frog stretch + straddle reaches join and pigeon closes for W17.

sets.name: 📍 Day-Specific Add-On — Pick by Today's Training (~3-5 min)

exercises.notes: **📍 PUSH DAYS — KEY PROTOCOL MOVE.** 30s each at LOW / MID / HIGH elbow positions. Arm bent 90°, forearm on the door frame, step through and rotate the torso AWAY. Desk work continuously re-tightens pec minor — daily.
**📍 PUSH DAYS** — active side of the pec-minor fix. Lower trap + rotator cuff.
**📍 PUSH DAYS** — serratus activation, helps unstick a tight pec minor.
**📍 PUSH DAYS (optional)** — slow rotator cuff work. Add if the shoulder feels off.
**📍 PUSH DAYS (optional)** — pins the shoulder blades in the corrected position.
**📍 PULL DAYS** — 25s. Decompress the shoulders, warm the grip.
**📍 PULL DAYS** — scapulae retracting only, no elbow bend. Crisp scap engagement before loaded pulls.
**📍 LEGS DAYS** — 30s each side. Scissor one foot over the other, reach the same-side arm overhead, lean away from the back leg — QL/psoas release. Also in the legs-workout warmup.
**📍 LEGS DAYS — W8 QL-SPASM PROTOCOL.** 90s each side. Long hold lets the QL/psoas release. Non-negotiable on legs day.
**📍 LEGS DAYS** — 60s each side. Gentle twist for the QL. Lacrosse-ball QL roll above the iliac crest beforehand if available.

sets.notes: **Pick today's day-specific protocol — push / pull / legs.** ~3-5 min total. KB days (Tue/Thu) skip this block — the in-workout banded prep covers the equivalent.

tips: Same shape as W11-W16, rotated moves. Morning flows stay low-fatigue; variety keeps them fresh.
**15 min main flow + 3-5 min day-specific add-on** — universal across W17 (Mon push / Tue KB / Wed pull / Thu KB / Fri legs).
**Scorpion + cossack BW + lizard pose stay every week** — durable anchors.
**Low-lunge thoracic rotation, dead bug, inchworm, frog stretch, straddle reaches rotate in for W17** variety.
**Day-specific add-on at the end** — push days do the pec-minor protocol, pull days do dead hang + scap pull, legs days do cross-leg lean + 90s pigeon + supine twist. KB days skip the add-on.
If short on time: low-lunge rotation + lizard + cossack BW + pigeon, plus today's day-specific add-on.
formPhilosophy: Same as W11-W16 — variety means different shapes hitting the same patterns. Scorpion-family spine work + hip openers + adductor/straddle stretches. The low-lunge thoracic rotation joins as the primer's hip+mid-back opener; dead bug + inchworm freshen the work block; frog + straddle reaches deepen the adductor arc. Morning flows stay structured around the in-workout banded prep's logic on KB days, and the day-specific protocols on PPL days.

name: Week 17 Pull — Steady State (Spotlight: Chest-Supported Row + Reverse Fly)
description: Volume steady; the protective behind-back shrug stays front-loaded as activation. The DB row pyramid holds at 70/80/90 bare-hand — grip stays the honest limiter, no straps. Face pull moves to 47.5 with the fist / knuckles-up grip that unlocked it. Cable crunch drops to 62.5 to win back true ab flexion. Spotlights cycle forward to the chest-supported row and the reverse fly — the two upper-back / rear-delt lifts that keep the shoulder healthy, drilled for the glued-chest and slow-eccentric patterns. Cable lifts list a number per equipment option.

dayOverview.theme: Steady state. Shrug stays FIRST (protective activation). DB row pyramid holds 70/80/90, no straps. Face pull 47.5 (fist / knuckles-up grip). Cable crunch 62.5 for true ab flexion. Spotlights cycle to chest-supported row + reverse fly. Cable lifts list per-equipment numbers.

spotlights.why: Cycles forward — the glued-chest, elbow-to-hip pattern is the backbone of healthy rowing. Spotlight drills the chest-stays-down cue and the full stretch-to-squeeze ROM at 40, so the lats do the work and the lower back stays out of it.

Cycles forward — the rear-delt / mid-trap work that balances all the pressing and protects the shoulder. Spotlight drills the fixed soft elbow + lead-with-the-elbow sweep + 2s eccentric at 20, capping reps with tempo rather than chasing the number.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W15 chest-supported row + face pull · W16 lat pulldown + incline curl · W17 chest-supported row + reverse fly (current) · W18 cycle forward — pull-up + DB row refresh.
watchpoints: **Behind-back shrug stays FIRST (activation slot).** Front-loading it keeps pull day flare-free — it's the protective counter-movement to all the pulling and can't be the piece a rushed session drops. Right after the warmup.

**DB row holds 70/80/90, no straps.** The top set is 90 for ~5-6 reps. Grip is the limiter (left hand taps first) — that's deliberate, train the grip rather than bypass it. Set the DB down when grip gives.
**Grip is the ceiling on the pulling lifts, not the shoulder** — DB row, lat pulldown, and the push-day farmer carry all tap out at grip now. No straps.

**Face pull 47.5** — grip the rope ends in fists, knuckles up; that's what made 47.5 feel easy with the elbows still high. Keep the elbows-high / external-rotate cue; if 47.5 drops the elbows, go back to 45.
**Cable crunch 62.5 for form** — lighter on purpose, to get full ab flexion with the hips locked instead of yanking from the hip flexors. Earn the slow eccentric here before adding load back.
**Loads otherwise hold** — chest-supported row 40, pull-up bodyweight, lat pulldown dual-pulley 70, high cable curl 170, reverse fly 20.
**Shoulder management: ramp the tempo** — don't make every set all-slow-eccentric at once. The flares this cluster have been volume / time-under-tension, not weight.
**Left bicep first, every set** — keep the protocol as insurance even though the weak-left cleared.
**Pull-up frequency holds** — 4 sets here + 1 push warmup + 1-2 KB Tuesday. Slow tempo, not to failure.
**Cable lifts have per-equipment numbers** — pick what's free, log equipment + number.

exercises.notes: Scap activation. Squeeze the shoulder blades together, soft elbow.
Spine warm — slow, full ROM each direction.
Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — primes grip and the pulling chain before bar work.
Active hang, not collapsed — engage the lats, pull the shoulders DOWN away from the ears even at full extension.

sets.name: Behind-Back DB Shrug — Protective Activation (DO THIS FIRST)

exercises.equipment: DB pair, held behind the body
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40-50lb pair. 3 sets — first in the session.

**Why it's here, first:** this is the 'opposite movement' to all the pulling — a counter/decompression for the right shoulder. Front-loading it keeps pull day flare-free. It reads more like a stretch than a lift; that's the point.
- **DBs held BEHIND the body** at the sides of the hips/glutes — palms facing back
- **Shoulders pull DOWN and BACK** at the start — packed, not relaxed
- **Shrug UP and slightly BACK** — pinch the shoulder blades at the top
- **Hold 1s at the top**, slow descent
- **Pack DOWN, NOT up** as the resting position — the lower position IS the work
- Chest open, not slouched

sets.notes: Protective trap-chain activation, front of the session. ~4 min. Light-to-moderate, peak-squeeze — a decompression, not a max effort.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** Bodyweight. 4 sets of 6-8.
- **Straight bar** — the variant that's been feeling best
- **Active hang start**, not collapsed
- **Pull elbows DOWN to ribs**, NOT chin to bar
- **Chest leads to the bar at the top**, eyes ahead, head neutral
- **Slow eccentric ~2-3s**, active hang at the bottom of every rep — no dropping
- **Stop the set when the rep stops being clean** — never kip. The limiter now is strength + clean form, not the shoulder; quality reps, frequency over max effort.

sets.name: 🔆 DB Rack / Bench Block — Chest-Supported Row (Spotlight) + DB Row + Incline Curl + Reverse Fly (Spotlight) (3 Rounds)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40. 3 sets of 10-12.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the glued-chest row, drilled:**
- **Chest stays GLUED to the incline bench** the whole set — if the chest peels off to heave the DBs, the weight's ahead of the form
- **Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit** — keeps it in the lats
- **Don't rotate the torso** — both sides of the chest stay on the pad, no twisting up for the last reps
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the shoulder blade protract, then re-pull from the stretch
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze** at the top, no DB slam at the bottom

**Reflection:** does the chest stay glued and the torso stay square through the end of set 3, or does the chest start peeling to muscle the last reps? If it peels, that's the honest cap at 40 — slow the eccentric, don't heave.

**LOAD:** 70/80/90 ascending pyramid — one set per round (70, then 80, then 90). No straps.
- **Chest-supported on the incline bench** — same setup as the chest-supported row
- **Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit**
- **Don't rotate the torso** — chest glued, no twisting
- **Slow 2s descent, 1s squeeze** on the 70 and 80 sets — those hold clean form
- **On the 90 set, single-count tempo is honest** — grip won't hold a 2s eccentric there, so don't force it; drive the elbow, control what you can, and aim for ~5 clean reps before form breaks rather than grinding sloppy ones
- **Grip is the limiter** (left hand taps first) — set the DB down when grip gives, not when the back fails.

**LOAD:**
- **Incline bench, 25lb DBs** (default) — preacher-style chest-supported curl, 3 sets of 8-10
- **Actual preacher bench when it's open** — EZ bar, 2×10 on the bar felt clean; take the real preacher station whenever it's free, it locks the upper arm better than the incline lean

- **Incline bench ~45°, lean in chest-first** — armpit and the back of the upper arm flat on the pad; the upper arm stays flat the ENTIRE rep (don't lift the elbow)
- **Left arm first, every set** (DB version) — keep the protocol as insurance
- **Full stretch at the bottom — pause 2s**
- **Curl smoothly to the peak squeeze**, no swing; 2-3s eccentric
- **Both arms unsupported** (DB version) — keep both sides equal in quality, especially late in the block

**LOAD:** 20lb. 3 sets of 12 — cap at 12 with a slower eccentric rather than chasing reps.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the rear-delt sweep that protects the shoulder:**
- **30° reverse-incline** (chest-down on the incline bench), DBs hanging fully extended at the start
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED throughout** — these are a sweep, NOT a row; the elbow angle never changes
- **Lead with the elbow, hand passive** — the hand never lifts first
- **Wings out and slightly UP to shoulder height** — sweep wide, don't lift, don't shrug
- **Hold the top a beat, then 2s eccentric** — control the drop, no swinging the DBs back up

**Reflection:** does the work stay in the rear delts / mid-traps with the elbow fixed and no shrug, or does it drift into the upper traps and momentum by rep 10? If it drifts, cap the set — strict 12 beats a swung 15. This is shoulder-health work; quality is the whole point.

sets.notes: One trip to the DB rack covers all 4 lifts. Incline bench at ~30° for the rows + reverse fly (30° reverse-incline), set to ~45° for the incline curl. 3 rounds.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD (pick whichever station's free, log which one):**
- **Dual pulley: 70** (the current home — 'very little pain' here)
- **Regular lat pulldown machine: 140**
- **Cable column: 52.5-57.5**
- **Cable pulley: 47.5**

3 sets.
- **Wide grip near the bend** — more lat isolation, less bicep
- **Slight backward lean ~15°, NO further** — more = it becomes a row
- **Pull the bar to the UPPER CHEST — NEVER behind the neck**
- **'Lats squeezing oranges into the back pockets'** at the bottom
- **1s pause at the contraction, 2s controlled return** to a full overhead stretch
- **Grip is the limiter at the end** — that's the honest cap, same as the DB row.

sets.name: Cable Column — Face Pull (3 Sets at 47.5)

exercises.equipment: cable column (mid/upper-chest height + rope)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** cable column 47.5.
- **Grip the rope ends in fists, knuckles up** — that's the change that made 47.5 feel easy with the elbows still high; keep it
- **Pull the rope to face level** — not to the chest
- **ELBOWS HIGH (above the shoulders)** — the make-or-break cue; this is what moves the work into the back
- **External-rotate at the top** — knuckles point UP, like the top of a double-biceps pose
- **1s peak hold**, then a slow 2s return — let the cable pull the arms back, don't drop
- Rear-delt + mid-trap + external-rotator health work — the right-shoulder-protective end of pull day
- **If the front of the shoulder takes over, the elbows have dropped** — re-set them high. If 47.5 drops the elbows, go back to 45.

sets.name: Cable Column Finisher — High Cable Curl + Cable Crunch (2-3 Sets)

exercises.equipment: cable column (low pulley, single D-handle, one arm at a time)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD (single arm — scales differ, log which station):**
- Cable column (single D-handle): 170
- Pulley / weight-stack station: ~120
2 working sets per arm.
- **Single arm at a time, one D-handle** — stand sideways, arm out at shoulder level
- **Upper arm parallel to the floor, FIXED** — the whole point of the high-cable variant
- **Curl the hand toward the ear**, peak squeeze
- **Left arm first**; slow eccentric, no bounce at the start

**LOAD (pick whichever station's free, log which one):**
- **Cable pulley (rope): 62.5** — lighter on purpose, the form-first number
- **Cable column (rope): scale down similarly for form**

3 sets.
- **Lighter load = real ab flexion.** 77.5 was heavy enough to turn it into a hip-flexor yank; 62.5 lets the spine actually round and the slow eccentric come back. Earn the form here before adding load.
- **Kneel under the high cable**
- **HIPS LOCKED** — the most important cue. The hips do not move.
- **Crunch from the abs ONLY** — the spine flexes, the hips stay put. Hips moving = hip-flexor work, not abs.
- **Chest toward the thighs**, hold the crunch 1 second
- **Slow eccentric, all the way** — at 62.5 the controlled drop IS available; use it, that's the whole reason for the lighter load.

**DB row holds 70/80/90, no straps.** Top set is 90 for ~5-6 reps. Grip is the limiter (left hand) and that's deliberate — train it, don't bypass it.

**Cable crunch 62.5 — form-first.** Lighter to win back true ab flexion (hips locked, slow eccentric) instead of a hip-flexor yank. Earn the form before adding load.
**Grip is the ceiling on pulling, not the shoulder** — DB row, lat pulldown, farmer carry all tap out at grip now. No straps.

Cycles forward — the controlled-descent version at 45 has held steady. Spotlight drills the packed-shoulder, vertical-forearm-over-elbow setup that makes 45 feel honest, so the last set holds form instead of peeling off the bench.

watchpoints: **Light chest opener in the warmup** — a few easy, light Kinesis-fly (tree-hugger) reps to loosen the chest before pressing. The same logic as warming up before squats: open the range first so the presses move clean and you can put power in. Keep it light — it primes, it doesn't fatigue. (Working Kinesis fly is still at the end — you'll touch that machine twice, which is fine.)

**Run push press first when the rack's free** — the reps recover there, and it's the heavy overhead lift that wants fresh, un-pre-fatigued shoulders. If it ends up second after a long warmup trail, expect a couple fewer reps at 45 — that's the accepted trade-off for getting the session in.
**Tempo is your energy lever** — the explosive-up / controlled-down hybrid is the current go-to; a slower full eccentric is fine too. Pick by feel; form holds either way.
**Cable lateral raise holds at cable column 30** — the pain-free streak is the priority; don't chase load while it's alive. (Distinct from the DB lateral raise — the day has both.)
**Pack DOWN, not up** — push press, both lateral raises, incline DB, dips, farmer carry all carry the cue. If a lockout needs a shrug, the load's too heavy for the cue — pause the set.

**Dips are new — chest-bias / lean-forward, ease them in.** Lean forward ~15-30°, pack the shoulders down, lower only to ~90° at the elbow (not deep) while it's new. Use the supported / assisted dip machine the moment the front shoulder talks. Find a shoulder-happy depth before chasing reps.
**Pull-up greasing set + protective behind-back shrug stay in the warmup** — both cheap, both easy to forget.
**Cable block lists a number per machine** — pick what's free, log the equipment + number you used.

sets.name: Warmup + Shoulder Rehab (Non-Negotiable) + Chest Opener + Pull-Up Greasing + Protective Shrug

exercises.notes: Slow, big circles. Wake up scap glide before loading.
Full sequence with red band. Non-negotiable on push day.

**Light loosening opener — NOT a working set** (the working fly comes later). On the Kinesis (not the cable column), light load: 'hug a tree' forward, then let the cables pull the arms open into the pec stretch. The cable holds tension in the stretched position, so it actively loosens and opens the chest before pressing — the same way warming up lets you get power into your squats. Quick and easy; this primes, it doesn't fatigue.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — dials a stretch up the back chain from forearm to shoulder. Wakes the grip and shoulder line before loading.
Ribs down, glutes tight, body in one line. Slow eccentric, 1s pause with chest 1-2" off the floor.

**Pull-up greasing set.** 1 fresh set, slow tempo, NOT to failure. Active hang start, pull elbows down to ribs, chest leads. Frequency, not max effort — drop to scapular-pulls only if the shoulder talks, and finish the count.

**Protective shrug (greasing set).** 1 light set, DBs held behind the body, palms back. Pack the shoulders DOWN and BACK, shrug UP and slightly back, 1s peak squeeze, slow down. The 'opposite movement' that decompresses the right shoulder — costs no time, easy to forget.

**LOAD:** 45lb DBs per side. 3 sets of 8-10. Run first when the rack's open — fresh shoulders.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the dip-drive that keeps the shoulder stable:**
- **Feet parallel, hip-width** — not duck stance
- **Ribs DOWN before the dip** — catch any rib flare on set 1
- **Pack DOWN, not up** — shoulder blades into the back pockets, neck long; if the lockout needs a shrug, the load's too heavy for the cue
- **Shallow dip ~3-4"**, straight down through the heels — the drive comes from the legs, not a press
- **Vertical DB path** — DBs travel up next to the ears, head pokes through at the top
- **Hybrid tempo:** explosive drive up, controlled descent. Breath: in at the dip, out on the drive

**Reflection:** does the explosive-up / controlled-down tempo hold a clean rib-down lockout across all three sets, or does the dip start flaring the ribs / the lockout start shrugging by set 3? The stable shoulder is the win here, not the rep number.

**LOAD:** 15lb DBs. 3 sets of 15-18.
- **Targets the medial (side) deltoid** — the slow eccentric maxes time-under-tension on a small muscle, which is exactly why the last set stays hard even at 15
- **Lead with the elbow, hand passive** — the wrist follows the elbow, the hand never lifts first
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED** through the whole rep — a locking/unlocking elbow recruits the traps
- **Stop at shoulder height — never higher** (higher just shrugs the traps off the medial delt)
- **2s eccentric** — the slow descent is the stimulus; fight the drop
- **Scap reset between sets** — roll the shoulders, engage/disengage the scapula a few times before the next set; this is what's kept the right shoulder quiet here

sets.name: 🔆 Incline DB Press (Spotlight — 3 Sets at 45 pair)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 45lb pair. 3 sets — fast-up / controlled-down, 1s pause at the bottom.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the setup that makes 45 honest:**
- **Bench at 30°**, not 45° — steeper biases front delt over upper chest
- **Shoulders packed back AND down** — pin the back of the shoulder into the bench and hold it the whole set
- **Forearm stacked vertically over the elbow at the bottom** — the cue that keeps the load off the front of the shoulder
- **Elbows ~45° from torso**, not flared to 90°
- **1s pause at the bottom** ('dead weight'), press to a fingerwidth apart at the top. Breath: in on descent, out on press

**Reflection:** the last half of the last set has been the struggle. Does the packed-shoulder, vertical-forearm setup hold the chest glued and the shoulder pinned through the end of set 3 — or does the chest start peeling and the elbows flaring to grind the reps out? Stop the set when the setup breaks.

**LOAD / EQUIPMENT (pick by how the shoulder feels, log which):**
- **Bodyweight parallel-bar dips** (default) — 3 sets of 8-12, leave a rep in the tank early while you find the groove
- **Supported / assisted dip machine** if the front shoulder talks — same movement, dial in just enough assist to keep the depth controlled
- **Band-assisted** if the machine's taken

**Chest-bias setup — lean forward, protect the shoulder:**
- **Lean the torso forward ~15-30° and let the elbows flare slightly** — that's what shifts the load onto the chest (upright + elbows-tucked is the triceps-bias version)
- **Pack the shoulders DOWN and BACK at the top** — never let them shrug up around the ears; pack-down is the whole game on dips
- **Lower until the shoulders are about level with the elbows (~90° at the elbow), NOT deeper** while this is new — deep dips are where the front shoulder gets cranky
- **Controlled descent ~2s, drive up to a soft lockout** — don't drop into the bottom or snap the elbows straight at the top
- **Stop the set the moment the front of the shoulder talks** — switch to the supported machine or end the set; this is a new pattern, ease it in over finding the rep ceiling

**New movement — find a depth and tempo the shoulder is happy with before chasing reps.**

**Reflection:** does the front of the shoulder stay quiet through all three sets with the lean-forward, pack-down, half-depth setup — or does it start talking by set 3? If it talks, that's the signal to drop to the supported machine and shorten the range, not to push through.

**LOAD:** Kinesis 9 (drop to 8 only if 9 feels off on set 1).
- **Slight forward hinge at the hips** — chest leads, not the head
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED throughout** — these are NOT presses; the elbow angle never changes
- **'Hug a tree'** — the squeeze comes from the chest, not the arms pulling together
- **Stop a fistwidth apart at the top** — don't crash the handles
- **Slow eccentric (~3s)** — let the cables pull the arms into the deep pec stretch; the right shoulder/pec reads this loaded stretch as relief, protect that.

sets.name: Cable Column Block — Lat Raise → Tri Ext → Straight-Arm Pulldown (3 Rounds)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:**
- **Cable column: 30** (hold — the pain-free streak is the priority)
- **Kinesis: 5-6** (if the column's taken)

3 rounds, one arm at a time.
- **Lead with the elbow as a DIRECTION** — the elbow points, doesn't bend
- **Soft elbow ~10°, FIXED** throughout
- **Stand sideways** to the stack, working arm farther from it
- **Stop at shoulder height — higher = traps**
- **2s eccentric**, fight the cable down

**LOAD:**

- **Kinesis: 5** (fallback)

3 rounds. **Always kneeling — there's no bench at this station; the forward torso lean IS the 'incline.'**
- **Kneel facing AWAY from the high pulley**, rope overhead
- **Elbows PINNED** — only the forearms move
- **Hands shoulder-width on the rope**
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the rope pull the hands behind the head
- **Stop just shy of lockout**, slow eccentric. Set 1 feels easy, set 3 is brutal — that's the lift working.

**LOAD:**
- **Cable column: 120** (the working number — really hard here, runs last after both presses)
- **Kinesis: 6** (fallback)

3 rounds.
- **Stand a step back, hinge ~15° at the hips** — fixed hinge, the torso doesn't pump
- **Slight elbow bend (~5°), FIXED throughout**
- **Pull the bar to the thighs, NOT past** — past = shoulders roll forward, lats switch off
- **Squeeze the lats hard at the bottom** — 'oranges into the back pockets'
- **Slow controlled return to a full overhead stretch.** Reps may fall on the later sets at the end of the session — that's the load and the fatigue, both honest.

sets.notes: Cable block — sharp cues, 3 rounds. One trip to the chosen station covers all three. Pick what's free (cable column is the default for all three) and log what you used.

sets.name: Farmer Carry (3 Walks)

exercises.equipment: DB rack
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 50lb DBs. 3 walks of ~45-60s each — chase hold-time.
- **Stand TALL** — ribs down, crown reaching up, no leaning back
- **Shoulders pulled DOWN and BACK** — into the back pockets, never shrugged. The DBs pull the shoulders up the whole walk; resist the whole walk. This tall, packed posture doubles as right-shoulder decompression — it reads as relief.
- **Neck long, eyes forward** — no chin poke
- **Grip firm but NOT death-clenched** — grip is the limiter here (it taps before the shoulder), so let it be the trainable edge; set the bells down when grip fails rather than white-knuckling
- **Walk a straight line at a deliberate pace**, breathing steadily

sets.notes: Trap-chain + grip block. 3 walks at 50lb — packed-shoulder posture, grip as the honest edge. Set them down when grip gives, not before.

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow position. Pec minor lengthen — the antagonist to the upper-trap chain loaded all session.
Passive hang from the pull-up bar. **Don't engage** — let the shoulders unpack and the spine decompress.
30s each side on the mat. Draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
45s each side. Front leg + back leg at 90°. Sink the hips toward the floor — hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Knees wide, arms extended forward. Parasympathetic shift before leaving the gym.

tips: **Steady state — sets and loads hold.** The work is depth of execution at the established numbers.

**Light chest opener in the warmup** — a few easy, light Kinesis-fly (tree-hugger) reps to loosen the chest before pressing. Same logic as warming up before squats: open first, press clean. Keep it light.
**Spotlight: push press + incline DB.** Push press drills the rib-down dip + vertical path at 45; incline DB drills the packed-shoulder, vertical-forearm setup so the last set holds form.
**Run push press first when the rack's free** — fresh shoulders. Explosive-up / controlled-down hybrid tempo is the current go-to.
**Lateral raise targets the medial delt** — the slow eccentric on a small muscle is why the last set stays hard at 15. Don't chase load.

**Dips slot in for the bodyweight press — chest-bias / lean-forward.** New movement: ease in, half-depth (~90° elbow), pack the shoulders down, supported machine the moment the shoulder talks. Find a shoulder-happy depth before chasing reps.
**Pack DOWN, not up** — every press + the carry carries the cue.
**Pull-up greasing set + protective shrug in the warmup** — 1 slow set each, not to failure.
**Farmer carry: 50lb, chase hold-time** — grip is the edge; the tall packed posture relieves the right shoulder.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, permanent every gym day.**
Rest: 2 min push press + dips, 90s lateral raise + Kinesis fly + farmer carry, 75s cable block.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state push week — the gains come from sharper execution at established loads. A light chest opener in the warmup gets the range before the work; the push press and incline DB then get the deep-cue treatment as the two free-weight presses, drilling the dip-drive and the packed-shoulder setup as shoulder-stability work as much as strength. exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 4 plates/side. 4 sets of 12.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the deep ROM that trains the core:**
- **Full ROM — knees toward the chest.** W17 the depth got so deep it hit the machine catcher — that's the win, not a problem; the deep position trains the abs/QL/core more than the quads ('legs barely doing anything in the deep squat'), which is exactly the intent
- **Foot position:** shoulder-width, mid-foot on the platform, slight toe-out
- **It feels harder cold** — the deep ROM opens up once the hips are warm, so don't judge the load on set 1
- **Actively press to keep the lower back from lifting off the pad** at the bottom; if the hips roll off, back off a hair (or stop just shy of the catcher)
- **Press through the WHOLE foot** — heels grounded
- **Slow descent (3s), no bounce at the bottom**; don't lock out hard at the top

**Reflection:** does the bottom stay deep (knees to chest, back on the pad) for all 4 sets, or does the depth shorten as you tire? ROM is the work; if it shortens, that's the honest end of the set.

**LOAD:** 4 plates/side. 3 sets of 15. Stay on the leg press — same machine, no walking off.
- **Balls of both feet on the BOTTOM EDGE of the platform, heels hanging off**
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the heels drop as far below the edge as they'll go
- **Drive to FULL plantarflexion at the top**
- **Tempo by feel** — own the stretch at the bottom and the squeeze at the top, no bouncing. (3 sets, after the 4 leg-press sets — same station.)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** two 45lb DBs, one per hand (up from 40). 3 sets of 8-10 each leg. **Regular DB version is the default; the Smith machine is the swap-in when it's free.**

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the heavier load, dialed in:**
- **Rear foot up on the bench** behind you, laces down or toes tucked
- **Step out far enough that the front shin stays roughly VERTICAL at the bottom** — too short a stance = the knee crashes past the toes
- **Front knee tracks over the front foot** — not caving in
- **Lower until the rear knee nearly touches the floor** — controlled, no dropping
- **Drive up through the FRONT HEEL** — the front leg does the work, the rear leg is a kickstand
- **Torso TALL** — a slight forward lean is fine, no folding over
- **2s descent**, own the bottom

**Watch:** at double-45 this is real load — if anything twitches/spasms, drop to bodyweight for the remaining sets and finish. The Smith version cleared the QL test at 45/side W17 (capped at 6 reps), so it's available when free.

**Reflection:** does the front shin stay vertical and the torso stay tall at double-45, or does the stance shorten / the torso fold to move the heavier load? If form drifts, that's the honest cap at 45 — hold it, don't grind.
