exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 70 first set to center, then 90 working. Slow tempo.
- **Settings: 5/m/0/-1** (the setting that felt better than /1 in W17 — verify before loading)
- **Ankles UNDER the pad** — the ankle bone is the contact point, NOT the mid-calf
- **Lap pad locked DOWN firmly** — a loose pad lets the torso lift and turns it into lower-back work
- **First set at 70 to get centered** (it'll feel easy — that's the point), then 90 for the working sets
- **Curl the heels toward the glutes** — full ROM, full squeeze
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze** — the slow eccentric is the whole stimulus; you feel these deeply when you go slow
- Torso anchored, no lifting forward. This comes BEFORE incline RDL on purpose — take the 90 with the legs still relatively fresh.

**LOAD:** 45lb plate. 3 sets of 15, dead slow with a 2s pause at the bottom. (Tempo's getting 'easier over time' — that's the progression working; the number stays.)
- **Pad just below the hip crease** — NOT on the upper thigh, NOT on the stomach
- **Hip hinge** — a Romanian deadlift on the 45° bench, NOT a lumbar extension. Lower back NEUTRAL throughout
- **At the bottom:** the stretch is in the **hamstrings and glutes**, NOT the lower back. If the lumbar rounds, you're going too deep for current mobility
- **Drive up by squeezing the glutes and hamstrings**; at the top, stop at neutral — past neutral = lumbar load = QL irritation
- **Tempo: 3s eccentric, 2s pause at the bottom, 1s drive up.** The slow eccentric is the entire reason this works — hold the 45lb plate, keep slowing the tempo; don't chase the load. (If you want more volume, add a lighter back-off set rather than loading the 45.)

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Recovery Block (Hip/QL-Biased for Legs Day)

exercises.notes: 30s each side. Scissor the legs, reach overhead, lean away from the back leg — bookend the session with the same QL/psoas release as the warmup.
45s each side. Deep hip-flexor and glute release — the long hold lets the QL and psoas let go.
30s each side. Gentle twist for the QL — draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
45s each side. Hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Knees wide, arms extended forward. Parasympathetic shift.

sets.notes: 5-min recovery block, hip/QL-biased on legs day.

tips: **Steady state, station-grouped.** Squat 4 sets, leg press 4, calf raise 3, Bulgarian 3, leg curl 3, incline RDL 3.
**Squat holds 80 / 6-7-8-8** — keep building the reps; reps are the lever, not heavier weight.
**Spotlight: leg-press ROM + Bulgarian.** Leg press drills the deep knees-to-chest ROM (core stimulus); Bulgarian steps up to double-45 DBs.
**Bulgarian → double-45 DBs, regular version is the default.** Smith machine is the swap-in when free (cleared the QL test at 45/side W17). Drop to bodyweight if anything twitches.
**Leg curl: 5/m/0/-1 setting, 70 primer then 90 working** — slow tempo.
**Station-grouped:** warmup → squat → leg press → leg-press-calf-raise (same machine — stay there) → Bulgarian → leg curl → incline RDL → cool-down. No backtracking.
**Leg curl BEFORE incline RDL** — don't reverse them, or the hamstring work stacks.
**Incline RDL is a 45lb plate, dead slow** — tempo is the progression. Add a lighter back-off set if you want more volume; don't load the 45.
**Cross-leg lateral lean in the warmup AND cool-down** — QL/psoas release. QL's clear; keep bookending it.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, hip/QL-biased on legs day.**
Rest: 3 min squats, 2 min leg press, 90s calf raise + Bulgarian + isolations.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state legs week. The leg press and Bulgarian get the deep-cue treatment: the leg press for the deep knees-to-chest ROM that trains the core as much as the quads (so deep it hits the machine catcher — that's the win), and the Bulgarian for the step up to double-45 with the form held. Squat settles at 80 with reps as the lever. The sequence keeps the two hamstring lifts from stacking and the station order from backtracking. Form leads load — building decades, not weeks.

name: W18 Morning Flow — Bodyweight Spine + Hip (All Days, Rotated Variety)
description: 15 min bodyweight floor flow — universal W18 morning flow, used every training day (Mon push / Tue KB / Wed pull / Thu KB / Fri legs). Same three-part shape as W11-W17 with rotated moves for variety: this week cycles back W12-era favorites (thread-the-needle, happy baby, puppy pose) and freshens the work block (spiderman plank, plank shoulder taps, down-dog knee-to-head). Three-part: spine primer → bodyweight work → deep stretch arc. Day-specific therapeutic add-on at the end (push = pec-minor protocol; pull = dead hang + scap pull; legs = cross-leg lateral lean + pigeon + supine twist; KB days skip — banded prep covers it).

exercises.notes: Slow, full ROM each direction. Spine wave wakes the segment-by-segment articulation.

Cycles back for W18 (a W12-era favorite) — 45s each side. On all fours, thread one arm under the body and rotate the upper back, then reach it open to the ceiling. Pure thoracic rotation + shoulder opener — wakes the mid-back before the day's pulling or pressing.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — the wrist dials a stretch up the back chain. Stays in the primer.

sets.name: Work Block — Bodyweight Activation (~5 min)

exercises.notes: **Greasing set — 1 quick set, NEVER to failure.** Daily frequency is the point (same idea as the pull-up greasing set — the floor rises over time). Elbows ~45° (not flared), ribs down, glutes tight, body one line, **pack down not up.** Stop 2-3 reps short. Back off / drop to knees if the right shoulder talks at the bottom.
Feet flat, drive through the heels, squeeze the glutes to a tall bridge, ribs down — no arching the lower back. Posterior-chain wake-up.

Rotates in for W18 — 30s each side. From a plank, drive one knee out toward the same-side elbow, then back. Hip-opener + anti-rotation core in motion; wakes the obliques and the deep hip flexors together.
30s each side. Anti-rotation — opposite arm + leg extend, hold a beat, hips stay square (no swinging).
Rotates in for W18 — from a plank, tap the opposite shoulder slowly, fighting the hips' urge to rotate. Anti-rotation + scap stability; the standing-plank cousin of the bird-dog.

Rotates in for W18 — from downward dog, draw one knee toward the nose (round the spine), then extend the leg back and up to a three-legged dog. Slow, alternating. Dynamic hamstring + shoulder + core flow that warms the whole back line.

sets.notes: Opens with a pushup greasing set (1 quick set, never to failure — daily habit). Spiderman plank, plank shoulder taps, down-dog knee-to-head rotate in for W18; glute bridge + bird-dog (anti-rotation) stay.

sets.name: Yoga Flow — Deep Stretch Arc (~7 min)

exercises.notes: 30s each side. Stays every week — signature spine move.
Cycles back for W18 (a W12-era favorite) — on the back, knees wide toward the armpits, hold the feet, gently rock. Deep inner-hip + low-back release; an easy decompressor after the work block.
30s each side. Hip flexor + adductor + back-leg quad. Drop to elbows if accessible. Stays — durable hip opener.
Bodyweight, slow. Stays every week — keeps the loaded Tuesday cossack pattern grooved even when it's off the KB rotation.

Stays — sit in a wide straddle, reach toward one foot, then center (chest toward the floor), then the other foot. Slow, breathe into each reach. The straddle + adductor + hamstring opener the flow design calls for.

Cycles back for W18 (a W12-era favorite) — knees under hips, walk the hands forward and sink the chest toward the floor, hips stay stacked over the knees. Deep shoulder + thoracic opener to close the arc — useful before any pressing or pulling day.

sets.notes: Continuous arc — flow between shapes, breathe deeply. Anchors stay (scorpion, lizard, cossack BW, straddle reaches); happy baby + puppy pose cycle back from the W12-era for W18.

sets.name: 📍 Day-Specific Add-On — Pick by Today's Training (~3-5 min)

exercises.notes: **📍 PUSH DAYS — KEY PROTOCOL MOVE.** 30s each at LOW / MID / HIGH elbow positions. Arm bent 90°, forearm on the door frame, step through and rotate the torso AWAY. Desk work continuously re-tightens pec minor — daily.
**📍 PUSH DAYS** — active side of the pec-minor fix. Lower trap + rotator cuff.
**📍 PUSH DAYS** — serratus activation, helps unstick a tight pec minor.
**📍 PUSH DAYS (optional)** — slow rotator cuff work. Add if the shoulder feels off.
**📍 PUSH DAYS (optional)** — pins the shoulder blades in the corrected position.
**📍 PULL DAYS** — 25s. Decompress the shoulders, warm the grip.
**📍 PULL DAYS** — scapulae retracting only, no elbow bend. Crisp scap engagement before loaded pulls.
**📍 LEGS DAYS** — 30s each side. Scissor one foot over the other, reach the same-side arm overhead, lean away from the back leg — QL/psoas release. Also in the legs-workout warmup.
**📍 LEGS DAYS — QL-SPASM PROTOCOL.** 90s each side. Long hold lets the QL/psoas release. Non-negotiable on legs day.
**📍 LEGS DAYS** — 60s each side. Gentle twist for the QL. Lacrosse-ball QL roll above the iliac crest beforehand if available.

sets.notes: **Pick today's day-specific protocol — push / pull / legs.** ~3-5 min total. KB days (Tue/Thu) skip this block — the in-workout banded prep covers the equivalent.

tips: Same shape as W11-W17, rotated moves. Morning flows stay low-fatigue; variety keeps them fresh.
**15 min main flow + 3-5 min day-specific add-on** — universal across W18 (Mon push / Tue KB / Wed pull / Thu KB / Fri legs).
**Scorpion + cossack BW + lizard pose + straddle reaches stay every week** — durable anchors.
**Cycled back for W18 (W12-era favorites): thread-the-needle, happy baby, puppy pose.** Fresh in the work block: spiderman plank, plank shoulder taps, down-dog knee-to-head.
**Day-specific add-on at the end** — push days do the pec-minor protocol, pull days do dead hang + scap pull, legs days do cross-leg lean + 90s pigeon + supine twist. KB days skip the add-on.
If short on time: thread-the-needle + lizard + cossack BW + puppy pose, plus today's day-specific add-on.
formPhilosophy: Same as W11-W17 — variety means different shapes hitting the same patterns. Scorpion-family spine work + hip openers + adductor/straddle stretches. W18 cycles back the W12-era favorites (thread-the-needle, happy baby, puppy pose) so the flow doesn't calcify, and freshens the work block with anti-rotation + dynamic flow shapes; the rehab anchors and the day-specific PPL protocols stay. Building decades, not weeks.

name: Week 18 Pull — Steady State (Spotlight: Pull-Up + DB Row)
description: Volume steady; the protective behind-back shrug stays front-loaded as activation. Spotlights cycle forward to the pull-up and the DB row — the two heavy pulls, now that the shoulder's a non-issue and grip is the honest limiter, drilled for clean slow-eccentric reps and the grip-capped top set. Loads hold, with a couple of optional gradual nudges where there's headroom and the user isn't holding (face pull, cable crunch climb-back, high cable curl). DB row holds the 70/80/90 bare-hand pyramid — grip is the limiter, no straps. Cable lifts list a number per equipment option.

dayOverview.theme: Steady state. Shrug stays FIRST (protective activation). Spotlights cycle to pull-up + DB row — the two heavy pulls, drilled now that the shoulder's clear and grip is the cap. DB row holds 70/80/90, no straps. Optional gradual nudges: face pull 50 (if elbows stay high), cable crunch climb-back, high curl 180. Cable lifts list per-equipment numbers.

spotlights.why: Cycles forward — the shoulder's a non-issue now (W16: 8/8/7/6, 'pretty much no shoulder pain'), so the pull-up earns the deep-cue treatment as the build-the-reps frequency lift. Spotlight drills the active-hang start, elbows-to-ribs pull, and slow eccentric so the floor keeps rising on clean reps, grip + strength the only limiter.

Cycles forward — the heavy pull where grip is the honest cap. Spotlight drills the glued-chest setup on the 70/80 sets and the realistic single-count top set at 90, so the back does the work and the grip taps out before the form does — no straps.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W16 lat pulldown + incline curl · W17 chest-supported row + reverse fly · W18 pull-up + DB row (current) · W19 cycle forward — lat pulldown + face pull refresh.
watchpoints: **Behind-back shrug stays FIRST (activation slot).** Front-loading it keeps pull day flare-free — the protective counter-movement to all the pulling can't be the piece a rushed session drops. Right after the warmup.

**DB row holds 70/80/90, no straps.** The top set is 90 for ~5-6 reps. Grip is the limiter (left hand taps first) — that's deliberate, train the grip rather than bypass it. Set the DB down when grip gives.
**Grip is the ceiling on the pulling lifts, not the shoulder** — DB row, lat pulldown, and the push-day farmer carry all tap out at grip now. No straps.

**Optional gradual nudges (you pull these, not me):** face pull 47.5 → **50 if the elbows stay high** with the knuckles-up grip; cable crunch 62.5 → **65-67.5 if the hips-locked form is locked in**; high cable curl 170 → **180 if it moves clean.** Only nudge what feels easy at the current number; otherwise hold. The floor rising is the win, not the number.
**Face pull — knuckles-up grip stays.** Grip the rope ends in fists, knuckles up; that's what unlocked 47.5 with the elbows still high. If a step to 50 drops the elbows, go back to 47.5.
**Cable crunch — form-first.** 62.5 won back true ab flexion (hips locked, slow eccentric). Earn the climb-back; if the hips start yanking, stay at 62.5.
**Loads otherwise hold** — chest-supported row 40, reverse fly 20, lat pulldown dual-pulley 70, incline curl 25 / preacher when free.
**Left bicep first, every set** — keep the protocol as insurance even though the weak-left cleared.
**Pull-up frequency holds** — 4 sets here + 1 push warmup + KB Tuesday. Slow tempo, not to failure.
**Cable lifts have per-equipment numbers** — pick what's free, log equipment + number.

exercises.notes: Scap activation. Squeeze the shoulder blades together, soft elbow.
Spine warm — slow, full ROM each direction.
Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — primes grip and the pulling chain before bar work.
Active hang, not collapsed — engage the lats, pull the shoulders DOWN away from the ears even at full extension. Primes the pull-up spotlight.

sets.name: Behind-Back DB Shrug — Protective Activation (DO THIS FIRST)

exercises.equipment: DB pair, held behind the body
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40-50lb pair. 3 sets — first in the session.

**Why it's here, first:** this is the 'opposite movement' to all the pulling — a counter/decompression for the right shoulder. Front-loading it keeps pull day flare-free. It reads more like a stretch than a lift; that's the point.
- **DBs held BEHIND the body** at the sides of the hips/glutes — palms facing back
- **Shoulders pull DOWN and BACK** at the start — packed, not relaxed
- **Shrug UP and slightly BACK** — pinch the shoulder blades at the top
- **Hold 1s at the top**, slow descent
- **Pack DOWN, NOT up** as the resting position — the lower position IS the work
- Chest open, not slouched.

sets.notes: Protective trap-chain activation, front of the session. ~4 min. Light-to-moderate, peak-squeeze — a decompression, not a max effort.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** Bodyweight. 4 sets of 6-8 (W16 was 8/8/7/6 — keep building the clean-rep floor).

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — clean reps, grip + strength the only limiter now:**
- **Straight bar** — the variant that's been feeling best
- **Active hang start**, shoulders pulled down out of the ears — NOT a collapsed dead hang
- **Pull elbows DOWN to ribs**, NOT chin to bar — think 'drive the elbows into the back pockets'
- **Chest leads to the bar at the top**, eyes ahead, head neutral
- **Slow eccentric ~2-3s**, active hang at the bottom of every rep — no dropping, no kip
- **Stop the set when the rep stops being clean** — frequency over max effort; the floor rises on quality reps

**Reflection:** the shoulder's a non-issue now — so does the set end on grip / honest strength, or does form get sloppy (kipping, half-ROM) to make the number? Clean reps are the whole point; bank 6 clean over 8 sloppy.

sets.name: 🔆 DB Rack / Bench Block — DB Row (Spotlight) + Chest-Supported Row + Incline Curl + Reverse Fly (3 Rounds)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 70/80/90 ascending pyramid — one set per round (70, then 80, then 90). No straps.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the grip-capped heavy pull, drilled:**
- **Chest-supported on the incline bench** — chest glued to the pad, no twisting up for the last reps
- **Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit** — keeps it in the lats
- **Slow 2s descent, 1s squeeze on the 70 and 80** — those hold clean form
- **On the 90 set, single-count tempo is honest** — grip won't hold a 2s eccentric there, so don't force it; drive the elbow, aim for ~5 clean reps before form breaks rather than grinding sloppy ones
- **Grip is the limiter** (left hand taps first) — set the DB down when grip gives, not when the back fails. No straps — train the grip

**Reflection:** does the grip tap out before the back form breaks (correct — that's the honest cap), or is the back rounding to muscle the 90? If the back goes first, the chest peeled off the pad — re-glue it and let the grip be the cap.

**LOAD:** 40. 3 sets of 10-12.
- **Chest stays GLUED to the incline bench** the whole set — if the chest peels off to heave the DBs, the weight's ahead of the form
- **Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit**
- **Don't rotate the torso** — both sides stay on the pad
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the shoulder blade protract, then re-pull from the stretch
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze** at the top, no DB slam at the bottom.

**LOAD:**
- **Actual preacher bench when it's open** — EZ bar, ~2×10 on the bar; take the real preacher station whenever it's free, it locks the upper arm better than the incline lean
- **Incline bench, 25lb DBs** (fallback) — chest-supported curl, 3 sets of 8-10

- **Incline bench ~45°, lean in chest-first** — armpit and the back of the upper arm flat on the pad; the upper arm stays flat the ENTIRE rep (don't lift the elbow)
- **Left arm first, every set** (DB version) — keep the protocol as insurance
- **Full stretch at the bottom — pause 2s**
- **Curl smoothly to the peak squeeze**, no swing; 2-3s eccentric.

**LOAD:** 20lb. 3 sets of 12 — cap at 12 with a slower eccentric rather than chasing reps.
- **30° reverse-incline** (chest-down on the incline bench), DBs hanging fully extended at the start
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED throughout** — a sweep, NOT a row; the elbow angle never changes
- **Lead with the elbow, hand passive** — the hand never lifts first
- **Wings out and slightly UP to shoulder height** — sweep wide, don't lift, don't shrug
- **Hold the top a beat, then 2s eccentric** — control the drop. Rear-delt / mid-trap shoulder-health work; quality over the number.

sets.notes: One trip to the DB rack covers all 4 lifts. Incline bench at ~30° for the rows + reverse fly (30° reverse-incline), set to ~45° for the incline curl. DB row leads the block (spotlight, run while fresh). 3 rounds.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD (pick whichever station's free, log which one):**
- **Dual pulley: 70** (the current home — 'very little pain' here)
- **Regular lat pulldown machine: 140**
- **Cable column: 52.5-57.5**
- **Cable pulley: 47.5**

3 sets.
- **Wide grip near the bend** — more lat isolation, less bicep
- **Slight backward lean ~15°, NO further** — more = it becomes a row
- **Pull the bar to the UPPER CHEST — NEVER behind the neck**
- **'Lats squeezing oranges into the back pockets'** at the bottom
- **1s pause at the contraction, 2s controlled return** to a full overhead stretch
- **Grip is the limiter at the end** — the honest cap, same as the DB row.

sets.name: Cable Column — Face Pull (3 Sets at 47.5, optional 50)

exercises.equipment: cable column (mid/upper-chest height + rope)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** cable column **47.5** — optional step to **50 if the elbows stay high** with the knuckles-up grip (you pull this; don't force it).
- **Grip the rope ends in fists, knuckles up** — that's the change that made 47.5 feel easy with the elbows still high; keep it
- **Pull the rope to face level** — not to the chest
- **ELBOWS HIGH (above the shoulders)** — the make-or-break cue; this is what moves the work into the back
- **External-rotate at the top** — knuckles point UP, like the top of a double-biceps pose
- **1s peak hold**, then a slow 2s return — let the cable pull the arms back, don't drop
- **If the front of the shoulder takes over, the elbows have dropped** — re-set them high. If 50 drops the elbows, go back to 47.5.

sets.name: Cable Column Finisher — High Cable Curl + Cable Crunch (2-3 Sets)

exercises.equipment: cable column (low pulley, single D-handle, one arm at a time)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD (single arm — scales differ, log which station):**
- Cable column (single D-handle): **170** — optional **180 if it moves clean** (you pull this)
- Pulley / weight-stack station: ~120
2 working sets per arm.
- **Single arm at a time, one D-handle** — stand sideways, arm out at shoulder level
- **Upper arm parallel to the floor, FIXED** — the whole point of the high-cable variant
- **Curl the hand toward the ear**, peak squeeze
- **Left arm first**; slow eccentric, no bounce at the start.

**LOAD (pick whichever station's free, log which one):**
- **Cable pulley (rope): 62.5** — the form-first number; optional **65-67.5 if the hips-locked form is locked in** (you pull this)
- **Cable column (rope): scale similarly for form**

3 sets.
- **HIPS LOCKED** — the most important cue. The hips do not move.
- **Crunch from the abs ONLY** — the spine flexes, the hips stay put. Hips moving = hip-flexor work, not abs.
- **Chest toward the thighs**, hold the crunch 1 second
- **Slow eccentric, all the way** — at 62.5 the controlled drop IS available; use it. Only climb the load if the form holds; if the hips start yanking, stay at 62.5.

sets.notes: Same cable column as the face pull. 2 rounds = 2 sets each; round the cable crunch to 3 if there's time and the abs aren't fried.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow position. Pec minor lengthen.
Passive hang. Don't engage — let the shoulders unpack and the spine decompress.
30s each side. Draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
45s each side. Hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Parasympathetic shift.

sets.notes: 5 minutes of recovery work, non-negotiable closing block.

tips: **Behind-back shrug stays FIRST** — protective decompression that keeps pull day flare-free.
**Spotlight: pull-up + DB row.** Pull-up drills clean active-hang reps (shoulder's a non-issue, build the floor); DB row drills the glued-chest 70/80 + the honest single-count 90, grip as the cap.
**DB row holds 70/80/90, no straps.** Top set 90 for ~5-6 reps. Grip is the limiter (left hand) and that's deliberate — train it.
**Optional gradual nudges (you pull these):** face pull 50 if elbows stay high, cable crunch 65-67.5 if form's locked, high curl 180 if clean. Otherwise hold; the floor rising is the win.
**Face pull — knuckles-up grip stays.** Drop back if a step to 50 drops the elbows.
**Grip is the ceiling on pulling, not the shoulder** — DB row, lat pulldown, farmer carry all tap out at grip. No straps.
**Loads otherwise hold** — chest-supported row 40, reverse fly 20, lat pulldown dual-pulley 70, incline curl 25 / preacher when free.
**Left bicep first, every set** — keep the protocol as insurance.
**Cable lifts list per-equipment numbers** — lat pulldown (70 dual pulley / 140 machine / 52.5-57.5 column / 47.5 pulley). Pick what's free, log it.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, permanent every gym day.**
Rest: shrug 60s, 2.5 min pull-ups, 90s DB block, 2 min lat pulldown, 90s face pull, 60s finisher.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state pull week with the protective shrug leading. The spotlights drill the two heavy pulls now that the shoulder's cleared — the pull-up as the build-the-floor frequency lift and the DB row as the grip-capped top set — because clean reps with grip as the honest limiter is how the floor rises here, no straps. Loads hold, with a few optional gradual nudges the user pulls where there's headroom. Building decades, not weeks.

name: Week 18 Push — Steady State (Spotlight: Dips + Cable Block)
description: Volume and loads hold. The light Kinesis-fly opener stays in the warmup so the chest moves through full range before pressing. Spotlights cycle forward to dips — now settled enough to earn the deep-cue treatment — and the cable block, which gets a cue refresh and lists per-equipment numbers (column / rope pulley / Kinesis) after W17's whole block ran on the pulley. The presses hold at 45: the W17 read was that fuller rest, not lighter load, is what recovers the set-3 reps. Push press runs first when the rack's free.

dayOverview.theme: Steady state — sets and loads hold; the work is rest discipline + depth of execution. Light Kinesis-fly opener stays in the warmup. Spotlight cycles to dips (settled in, deep cues now) + the cable block (cue refresh + per-equipment numbers). Push press runs first, fresh; fuller rest is the lever to recover the set-3 reps. Dips stay bodyweight, fuller ROM (the shoulder tolerated it W17); watch the front pec stays pressure, not pain.

spotlights.why: Cycles forward — dips debuted clean W17 (bodyweight 12/(6+6)/8, full ROM, no shoulder complaint), so they earn the deep-cue treatment now. Spotlight drills the lean-forward chest-bias, the pack-down at the top, and the front-pec-pressure-not-pain watch so the new pattern grooves without waking the at-risk shoulder.

Cycles forward as the cable-block refresh — W17's whole cable block ran on the rope pulley (column was taken), so the block gets sharper cues and per-equipment numbers. Spotlight drills the fixed-hinge, lats-to-the-thighs pull and the front-pec-quiet setup that backed 57.5 down to a clean 50 on the pulley.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W16 lateral raise + Kinesis fly · W17 push press + incline DB · W18 dips + cable block (current) · W19 cycle forward — push press + lateral raise refresh.
watchpoints: **Rest is the lever, not load.** W17 showed the set-3 fades come from short rest (push press dropped to 8 on ~30s rest; incline finished when rested longer). Take the prescribed ~2 min on the presses — expect the reps to hold. Don't drop weight to chase a feeling that fuller rest fixes.

**Light Kinesis-fly opener stays in the warmup** — a few easy, light tree-hugger reps to open the chest before pressing (same logic as warming up before squats). It primes, it doesn't fatigue. Working Kinesis fly is still later in the day.
**Run push press first when the rack's free** — fresh shoulders; the heavy overhead lift wants no pre-fatigue.

**Dips spotlight — bodyweight, fuller ROM is fine now.** The shoulder tolerated full depth W17 with no complaint; keep going deep, chest-bias / lean-forward, pack down. Watch the **front pec stays 'pressure,' not pain** — if it tips to pain, shorten the depth or move to the supported machine.
**Pack DOWN, not up** — push press, lateral raise, incline DB, dips, farmer carry all carry the cue. A lockout that needs a shrug = the load's too heavy for the cue.

**Cable block lists per-equipment numbers (column / rope pulley / Kinesis)** — pick what's free, log the equipment + number. After W17 the pulley numbers are known: tri ext ~35, straight-arm pulldown 50, lateral raise (reg-pulley d-handle) 10.
**Day is at capacity** — W17 ran long and left you wiped. No adds; this is the full menu.

sets.name: Warmup + Shoulder Rehab (Non-Negotiable) + Chest Opener + Pull-Up Greasing + Protective Shrug

exercises.notes: Slow, big circles. Wake up scap glide before loading.
Full sequence with red band. Non-negotiable on push day.

**Light loosening opener — NOT a working set** (the working fly comes later). On the Kinesis, light load: 'hug a tree' forward, then let the cables pull the arms open into the pec stretch. The cable holds tension in the stretched position, so it actively opens the chest before pressing. Quick and easy; this primes, it doesn't fatigue.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — dials a stretch up the back chain from forearm to shoulder. Wakes the grip and shoulder line before loading.
Ribs down, glutes tight, body in one line. Slow eccentric, 1s pause with chest 1-2" off the floor.

**Pull-up greasing set.** 1 fresh set, slow tempo, NOT to failure. Active hang start, pull elbows down to ribs, chest leads. Frequency, not max effort — drop to scapular-pulls only if the shoulder talks, and finish the count.

**Protective shrug (greasing set).** 1 light set, DBs held behind the body, palms back. Pack the shoulders DOWN and BACK, shrug UP and slightly back, 1s peak squeeze, slow down. The 'opposite movement' that decompresses the right shoulder — costs no time, easy to forget.

sets.name: Push Press (3 Sets at 45 — Run First, Rest Full)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 45lb DBs per side. 3 sets of 8-10. Run first when the rack's open.
- **Rest the full ~2 min between sets** — W17 set 3 fell to 8 on ~30s rest; with full rest it holds 10. The rest is the fix, not a lighter bell.
- **Ribs DOWN before the dip** — catch any rib flare on set 1
- **Shallow dip ~3-4"**, straight down through the heels — the drive comes from the legs
- **Vertical DB path** — DBs travel up next to the ears, head pokes through at the top
- **Pack DOWN, not up** at the lockout — if it needs a shrug, the load's too heavy for the cue
- **Hybrid tempo:** explosive drive up, controlled descent.

**LOAD:** 15lb DBs. 3 sets of 15-18.
- **Targets the medial (side) deltoid** — the slow eccentric maxes time-under-tension on a small muscle, which is why the last set stays hard even at 15
- **Lead with the elbow, hand passive** — the wrist follows the elbow, the hand never lifts first
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED** through the whole rep
- **Stop at shoulder height — never higher** (higher just shrugs the traps off the medial delt)
- **2s eccentric** — the slow descent is the stimulus
- **Scap reset between sets** — roll the shoulders, engage/disengage the scapula a few times; this is what's kept the right shoulder quiet here.

sets.name: Incline DB Press (3 Sets at 45 pair — Rest Full)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 45lb pair. 3 sets — fast-up / controlled-down, 1s pause at the bottom.
- **Rest the full ~2 min** — W17 the last set completed once rested longer ('rest helps apparently'). 12 reps is the hypertrophy range by design; let the rest keep each set quality.
- **Bench at 30°**, not 45° — steeper biases front delt over upper chest
- **Shoulders packed back AND down** — pin the back of the shoulder into the bench, hold it the whole set
- **Forearm stacked vertically over the elbow at the bottom** — keeps the load off the front of the shoulder
- **Elbows ~45° from torso**, not flared to 90°
- **1s pause at the bottom**, press to a fingerwidth apart at the top.

**LOAD / EQUIPMENT (pick by how the shoulder feels, log which):**
- **Bodyweight parallel-bar dips** (default) — 3 sets of 8-12
- **Supported / assisted dip machine** if the front shoulder talks — same movement, just enough assist to keep the depth controlled
- **Band-assisted** if the machine's taken

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the chest-bias dip, now grooving:**
- **Lean the torso forward ~15-30° and let the elbows flare slightly** — that's what shifts the load onto the chest (upright + tucked = triceps-bias)
- **Pack the shoulders DOWN and BACK at the top** — never shrug up around the ears; pack-down is the whole game on dips
- **Fuller ROM is fine now** — W17 you went full depth with no shoulder complaint, so keep going deep, controlled
- **Controlled descent ~2s, drive up to a soft lockout** — don't drop into the bottom or snap the elbows at the top
- **Front-pec watch:** a little pressure on the front pec at the bottom stretch is expected (chest-bias dip). If it tips from 'pressure' to PAIN, shorten the depth or move to the supported machine — that's the cue, not the rep count
- **Body-bob settles with reps** — keep the feet folded behind, brace the core to stop the swing

**Reflection:** does the front pec stay 'pressure' (fine) through all three sets, and the shoulder stay quiet — or does the pec tip to pain / the shoulder start talking by set 3? Quiet shoulder is the win; if it talks, supported machine + shorter range, don't push through.

**LOAD:** Kinesis 9 (drop to 8 only if 9 feels off on set 1).
- **Slight forward hinge at the hips** — chest leads, not the head
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED throughout** — these are NOT presses; the elbow angle never changes
- **'Hug a tree'** — the squeeze comes from the chest, not the arms pulling together
- **Stop a fistwidth apart at the top** — don't crash the handles
- **Slow eccentric (~3s)** — let the cables pull the arms into the deep pec stretch; the right shoulder/pec reads this loaded stretch as relief, protect that.

sets.name: 🔆 Cable Block — Lat Raise → Tri Ext → Straight-Arm Pulldown (Refresh + Per-Equipment Numbers, 3 Rounds)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD (pick what's free, log which):**
- **Cable column: 30** (the pain-free home)
- **Regular pulley, D-handle at ankle height: 10** (W17 — 'felt about the same as cable column')
- **Kinesis: 5-6**

3 rounds, one arm at a time.
- **Lead with the elbow as a DIRECTION** — the elbow points, doesn't bend
- **Soft elbow ~10°, FIXED** throughout
- **Stand sideways** to the stack, working arm farther from it
- **Stop at shoulder height — higher = traps**
- **2s eccentric**, fight the cable down.

**LOAD (pick what's free, log which):**
- **Cable column: 70** (default)
- **Rope pulley: ~35** (W17 — 30 was too easy, 35 'died at 10')
- **Kinesis: 5**

3 rounds. **Always kneeling — there's no bench at this station; the forward torso lean IS the 'incline.'**
- **Kneel facing AWAY from the high pulley**, rope overhead
- **Elbows PINNED** — only the forearms move
- **Hands shoulder-width on the rope**
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the rope pull the hands behind the head
- **Stop just shy of lockout**, slow eccentric. Set 1 feels easy, set 3 is brutal — that's the lift working.

**LOAD (pick what's free, log which):**
- **Cable column: 120** (the column working number)
- **Rope pulley: 50** (W17 — 57.5 was 'insanely hard' + woke the front pec, 50 was the clean working weight)
- **Kinesis: 6**

3 rounds. **🔆 SPOTLIGHT — fixed hinge, lats to the thighs:**
- **Stand a step back, hinge ~15° at the hips** — fixed hinge, the torso doesn't pump
- **Slight elbow bend (~5°), FIXED throughout**
- **Pull the bar to the thighs, NOT past** — past = shoulders roll forward, lats switch off (this is also where the front pec gets pulled into it; keep it short)
- **Squeeze the lats hard at the bottom** — 'oranges into the back pockets'
- **Slow controlled return to a full overhead stretch.** Runs last after both presses — reps may fall on the later sets; that's the load and the fatigue, both honest.

**Reflection:** does the work stay in the lats with the front pec quiet, or does the pec start taking over (the W17 57.5 signal)? If the pec lights up, the load's too high for the line of pull — back it down, like 57.5 → 50 on the pulley.

sets.notes: Cable block — sharp cues, 3 rounds, one trip to the chosen station covers all three. Per-equipment numbers listed (column is the default; the pulley numbers are from W17 when the column was taken). Pick what's free and log it.

sets.name: Farmer Carry (3 Walks)

exercises.equipment: DB rack
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 50lb DBs. 3 walks of ~45-60s each — chase hold-time.
- **Stand TALL** — ribs down, crown reaching up, no leaning back
- **Shoulders pulled DOWN and BACK** — into the back pockets, never shrugged. The DBs pull the shoulders up the whole walk; resist the whole walk. This tall, packed posture doubles as right-shoulder decompression — it reads as relief.
- **Neck long, eyes forward** — no chin poke
- **Grip firm but NOT death-clenched** — grip is the limiter here (it taps before the shoulder); set the bells down when grip fails rather than white-knuckling
- **Walk a straight line at a deliberate pace**, breathing steadily.

sets.notes: Trap-chain + grip block. 3 walks at 50lb — packed-shoulder posture, grip as the honest edge. Set them down when grip gives, not before.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow position. Pec minor lengthen — the antagonist to the upper-trap chain loaded all session.
Passive hang from the pull-up bar. **Don't engage** — let the shoulders unpack and the spine decompress.
30s each side on the mat. Draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
45s each side. Front leg + back leg at 90°. Sink the hips toward the floor — hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Knees wide, arms extended forward. Parasympathetic shift before leaving the gym.

sets.notes: 5 minutes of recovery work, non-negotiable closing block.

tips: **Rest is the lever** — take the full ~2 min on push press + incline DB; W17 showed the set-3 fades are under-rest, not load. Don't drop weight.
**Light Kinesis-fly opener in the warmup** — open the chest before pressing; keep it light, it primes not fatigues.
**Spotlight: dips + cable block.** Dips drill the chest-bias lean + pack-down + front-pec-pressure-not-pain watch (fuller ROM is fine now); the cable block gets a cue refresh + per-equipment numbers.
**Run push press first when the rack's free** — fresh shoulders.
**Dips stay bodyweight, fuller ROM** — the shoulder tolerated full depth W17; supported machine the moment the front shoulder (not pec) talks.
**Pack DOWN, not up** — every press + the carry carries the cue.
**Cable block per-equipment numbers** — column 30/70/120; rope pulley 10(reg, lat raise)/35/50; Kinesis 5-6. Pick what's free, log it.
**Farmer carry: 50lb, chase hold-time** — grip is the edge; the tall packed posture relieves the right shoulder.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, permanent every gym day.**
**Day is at capacity** — no adds; W17 already ran long. Rest: 2 min push press + dips + incline, 90s lateral raise + Kinesis fly + farmer carry, 75s cable block.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state push week — the gains come from rest discipline and sharper execution at established loads, not heavier bells. W17's lesson bakes in: fuller rest recovers the reps, so the presses hold 45 and rest full. Dips graduate to spotlight now that they've proven shoulder-friendly — drilled as chest-bias, pack-down, fuller-ROM work with the front pec watched. The cable block gets its per-equipment map so a taken column never derails the session. Building decades, not weeks.

name: Week 19 KB Saturday Cardio — Conditioning (Spotlight: High Pull; Round-the-Clock Finisher)
description: Saturday KB OPTION — pure conditioning, distinct from Tue (Leggy Flow + cossack) and Thu (lighter skill template). **Warmup reminder:** halo → easy two-handed swings → goblet squat → internal core fist rotation → bottoms-up press (18lb, 8/side, forward + T-plane), then the abbreviated 4-move banded prep. Light bell throughout (16-20lb) — breathing rate and sustainability are the targets, not load. Deliberately compact so it stays a clean skip when the week's been heavy: the Asgooch cardio complex carries over, then the finisher rotates this week to a round-the-clock single-bell chain. Spotlight rotates to the high pull — the explosive hip-snap pull. Optional light push-press ladder if you want a strength touch. Choice-of-the-day on D6 alongside stairmaster, easy run, or rest.

dayOverview.theme: Saturday conditioning — light bell, breathing-rate target. Kept compact: Asgooch cardio complex + a round-the-clock single-bell chain finisher (rotated from W18's high-rep ladder) — so it's a clean skip on a heavy week. Day after Friday legs — squatting stays LIGHT on purpose. Spotlight rotates to the high pull. Optional light push-press ladder available.

spotlights.why: Rotates in as this week's spotlight (W18 was the swing clean). The high pull is the explosive hip-snap pull that bridges the swing and the snatch — spotlight the hip drive (the snap floats the bell, the arm just guides), the high elbows at the top, and the controlled lower, so the power comes from the hips, not the shoulder. Right-shoulder-friendly when the hip does the work.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: Finisher rotates: W17 controlled-power · W18 high-rep descending ladder · W19 round-the-clock single-bell chain (current) · W20 cycle forward — a fresh complex. Spotlight rotates: W18 swing clean · W19 high pull · W20 front squat or snatch. The Asgooch cardio complex stays; the finisher + spotlight rotate so Saturday stays fresh.
watchpoints: **Saturday is optional and deliberately compact** — keep it a clean skip when the week's been heavy. The point is to not over-train into a weak Monday; weekends stay light.
**Day after Friday legs.** Squatting (front squat × 6 in the complex; the finisher goblet squat) stays LIGHT — 16-20lb. Skip the squat reps if the QL/quads are talking.
**Light bell is the whole point** — 16-20lb working. Conditioning means breathing rate, not bell weight.
**Asgooch CARDIO complex ≠ Tuesday's work** — row/clean/squat/snatch, low-and-explosive.
**High-pull spotlight** — hip snap floats the bell, elbows high at the top, controlled lower; the hip does the work, not the arm. Right shoulder watch — keep it light, smooth.

**Finisher rotated to a round-the-clock single-bell chain** — swing → high pull → swing clean → push press → goblet squat, one continuous lap, 3-4 rounds. Light bell, keep moving, break a move into chunks if needed.

**OPTIONAL light push-press ladder** — you did 40/45/50 × 8/7/6 here W17 and it 'worked great.' If you want a strength touch, run it after the warm-up (clean to rack, dip-drive, pack the shoulder down). Keep it light and optional — Saturday's still a conditioning day.
**Choice-of-the-day on D6** — not mandatory. Skip if Friday legs cooked you; swap for stairmaster / easy run if cardio-only is the call. No pull-up greasing here — Saturday is the conditioning flank.

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 16-20lb. Loosen the shoulders fast — the cardio complex is its own warmup.
Easy two-handed swings. Prime the hinge.
Light, open the hips. Skip if Friday legs left the quads sore.
Standing, torso hinged slightly forward. Wakes the grip + forearm + posterior chain — primes the clean catch + the high pull.

**LOAD:** 18lb. Your bottoms-up shoulder warmup — bell inverted/balanced over a vertical forearm, hard grip, shoulder packed. **8/side in two planes:** forward press (straight overhead) + T-press (out toward a T at shoulder height). **Keep the T-plane lighter.** Fires the rotator cuff and primes the right shoulder before the overhead work.

sets.name: Quick Banded Prep (~2 min — abbreviated)

exercises.notes: Mini-band overhead.
Scaps depress.
Rear delts fire.
Sternum height, ribs down.

sets.notes: **Abbreviated prep** — 4 moves instead of the full 7. Saturday is conditioning; the full 7-move prep is overkill for a light-bell day. (If you run the optional push-press ladder, do the full 7 instead.)

sets.name: Asgooch Cardio Complex — LEFT

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 16-20lb. Left hand. Hips back, back flat, pull the elbow past the ribs. 2s pull, 2s lower.
Left hand. Hip drive into the rack — the hinge throws the bell up, the arm guides it; soft catch, knees absorb, elbow tucks to the ribs, no forearm bang. Ribs down at the rack.
Left rack. **LIGHT** — Friday legs is yesterday. Sit tall, full depth IF the legs are fresh; reduce depth before load if they're cooked.
Left hand. Hips drive the bell, punch the hand THROUGH at the top for a soft catch, no bang. **Right shoulder watch** — sub high pulls for the last 2 rounds if it crackles on the catch.

sets.notes: 5 rounds LEFT. Continuous within a round — row → clean → squat → snatch with no rest. Rest 30-45s between rounds. **Weak side first.**

sets.name: Asgooch Cardio Complex — RIGHT

exercises.notes: Right hand. Same form — hips back, full extension.
Right hand. Hip drive, soft knees-absorb catch, no forearm bang.
Right rack. Same depth/load discipline as the left.
Right hand. Punch-through + right shoulder watchpoint on the catch — same modify-to-high-pull rule.

sets.notes: 5 rounds RIGHT. Continuous within a round. **If the workout is running long after the left side, drop to 3-4 rounds right — don't grind a quality session into a sloppy one.**

sets.name: 🔆🕐 Round-the-Clock Single-Bell Chain (Rotated In for W19 — Spotlight: High Pull)

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 16-20lb. Two-handed swings — snap the hips, float to chest height, arms are ropes. Opens the chain.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the explosive hip-snap pull:**
- **Hip snap does the work** — the hinge-and-snap floats the bell, the arm just guides it up; don't muscle it with the shoulder
- **Elbows HIGH at the top** — pull the bell to about chin height, elbow leads above the wrist
- **Controlled lower** back into the hinge — re-load the hips for the next rep
- **Right shoulder watch** — keep it light; the moment the arm starts doing the lifting, drop the load or switch to a plain swing

**Reflection:** does the bell float up on the hip snap (elbow high, shoulder relaxed), or are you yanking it up with the arm once you tire? Hip-driven is the win — and the shoulder-safe version.
Hip drive into the rack, soft knees-absorb catch, no forearm bang. Ribs down at the rack.
Light dip-drive — the legs power the press, pack the shoulder DOWN on the lockout. **Right shoulder watch** — keep it light; lighten or skip if the overhead gets ugly.
Full depth, chest up — **LIGHT**, Friday legs is yesterday. Skip or halve if the quads are tight; smooth controlled tempo, not a burnout.

sets.notes: **Round-the-clock chain — one continuous lap through the five moves, 4 rounds.** Single light bell (16-20lb). Move swing → high pull → swing clean → push press → goblet squat with minimal rest within a lap, ~30-45s between laps. Posture + breathing-rate focus, not max effort. Drop to 3 laps if the session's running long. (Rotated in from W18's high-rep ladder.)

exercises.notes: Slow spine wave. Decompress after the finisher.
60s each side. Hip flexor release — counters the cardio-complex squat reps.
60s. Adductors take a hit from the lateral shapes.

tips: **Saturday conditioning option — choice-of-the-day on D6.** Alternates with stairmaster, easy run, or rest. Skip if Friday legs cooked you; deliberately compact so skipping it costs nothing.
**LIGHT bell throughout: 16-20lb working.** This is the whole point. Conditioning = breathing rate, not load.
**Core block carries over:** the Asgooch CARDIO complex (row/clean/squat/snatch × 6 × 5 rounds per side).
**Finisher rotated to a round-the-clock single-bell chain** — swing → high pull → swing clean → push press → goblet squat, one continuous lap, 4 rounds, light bell.
**Spotlight rotates to the high pull** — hip snap floats the bell, elbows high, controlled lower; the hip does the work, not the arm.

**OPTIONAL light push-press ladder** — you ran 40/45/50 × 8/7/6 here W17 and it 'worked great.' Add it after the warm-up if you want a strength touch; keep it light, run the full banded prep if you do.
**Squatting stays LIGHT** — Friday legs is yesterday. Skip the squat reps if the quads are tight.
**Right shoulder watch on the high pull / clean / snatch / push press** — light bell, hip-driven; switch to plain swings if it crackles.
**Bottoms-up press now standard in the warmup** — 18lb, 8/side, forward + T-plane (T-plane light).
**No pull-up greasing here** — Saturday is the conditioning flank.
Cooldown mandatory — cat-cow + pigeon + butterfly.
Rotation plan: W20 rotates the finisher to a fresh complex + the spotlight to the front squat or snatch.
formPhilosophy: Saturday is conditioning, distinct from the Tue and Thu KB days. Light bell, more reps. Kept deliberately compact — the Asgooch complex plus a rotating finisher (this week a round-the-clock single-bell chain) — so it's a genuine choice, not an obligation: easy to skip on a heavy week, and light enough it never bleeds into a weak Monday. The high-pull spotlight drills the hip-driven, shoulder-safe pull. The optional push-press ladder is there because the user liked it W17, but it stays optional so Saturday's identity as the light conditioning flank holds. Building decades, not weeks.

name: Week 19 KB Conditioning — Thursday, Flow + Coordination Block (Spotlight: Split-Stance Pass-Through)
description: KB Thursday, full template, kept light on the legs so Friday legs stays strong. **Warmup reminder:** halo → bottoms-up press (18lb, 8/side, forward + T-plane) → internal core fist rotation → protective behind-back shrug, then the 7-move banded shoulder prep. The permanent Flow + Coordination block rotates this week to the split-stance pass-through (pass the bell between the legs in a held lunge — grip + coordination, core-led). The mobility maintenance block rotates its cue focus to the windmill. The rest holds — lighter strength block (rows + strict press at the new 40/45/50), the canonical Bent Press Flow kept light, a balance closer, cooldown. Bottoms-up press is now standard in the KB warmup.

dayOverview.theme: Thursday KB day, full template, kept light on the legs so Friday legs stays strong. Flow + Coordination block rotates to the split-stance pass-through (grip + coordination, core-led, light). Mobility maintenance rotates its cue focus to the windmill. Strength block runs the new 40/45/50 strict press + 40 rows. Bent Press Flow kept light to protect Friday. Bottoms-up press now standard in the warmup. Conditioning + skill + balance — never a metabolic finisher.

spotlights.why: This week's content of the permanent Flow + Coordination block. A split-stance (lunge) hold while passing the bell between the legs hand-to-hand — grip + coordination with the legs under constant tension, but core-led and light, which is the Thursday brief (skill over leg load so Friday legs stays fresh). Spotlight drills the stay-low split stance + the smooth hand-to-hand pass so the chain flows without standing up out of the lunge.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: Flow + Coordination block (permanent): W17 figure-8 weave · W18 halo → reverse lunge · W19 split-stance pass-through · W20 a GymFiesta-trio move or figure-8 march. Mobility maintenance rotates its cue focus: W18 TGU left-side checkpoints → W19 windmill refresh → W20 bent-press refresh.
watchpoints: **Permanent Flow + Coordination block — right after the banded prep.** Light-bell base-skill work: a familiar halo to warm up, then the week's chain. Skill + coordination is the point, NOT cardio burn — keep it light and clean.

**Split-stance pass-through — STAY LOW in the lunge.** Don't stand up to pass the bell; hold the split stance, pass hand-to-hand between the legs, keep the torso tall and core braced. Light bell — coordination + grip, not leg load. Switch the front leg halfway.

**Thursday is kept LIGHT ON THE LEGS on purpose** — Friday legs is tomorrow. The split-stance pass-through is core/coordination-led; the Bent-Press-Flow front squat + lateral lunge stay light (~25-30lb), and the balance-closer single-leg RDL stays light. The leg-heavy KB work lives on Tuesday.

**Bent Press Flow is the canonical 5-move flow** — dead clean → front squat → lateral lunge → bent press → tactical clean. Bent press is move #4, in the flow. Light groove, 2 rounds, ~25-30lb (keep it light to protect Friday legs — 40 is doable but the flow's leg work the day before legs isn't worth it).

**Mobility maintenance = windmill refresh this week** — the windmill gets the sharper cues (hinge AWAY from the bell side, stretch in the back-leg hip flexor NOT the lower back, long spine, eyes on the bell). TGU + bent press stay light maintenance. Windmill ~20-25lb for the cue work; up to ~40 only if the long-spine form holds (W18 did 40 with no flare — keep the cues tight, back off range before grinding).
**Right shoulder watch on the overhead work** (windmill, TGU lockout, bent press leverage) — if it talks, lighten and slow down; back off range before grinding.
**Bottoms-up press now standard in the warmup** — 18lb, 8/side, forward + T-plane (T-plane light). Rotator-cuff prep.
**Protective shrug greasing set in the warmup** — 1 light set, DBs or a bell behind the body. Cheap, easy to forget.
**Balance closer, not a metabolic finisher** — single-leg RDL → bird-dog → standing side-to-side twist, light bell. Thursday is conditioning + skills + balance, and Friday legs is tomorrow.

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 15-20lb. Slow circles, both directions. Shoulder loosener — and the warm-up for the day's flow + coordination work.

**LOAD:** 18lb. Now standard in the KB warmup — bell inverted/balanced over a vertical forearm, grip HARD, shoulder packed. **8/side in two planes:** forward press + T-press (out toward a T). **Keep the T-plane lighter.** Rotator-cuff prep before the overhead work.
Standing, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — wakes the grip and forearms for the pass-through + clean catches.

exercises.equipment: light DB pair or a kettlebell held behind the body
exercises.notes: **Protective shrug (greasing set).** 1 light set held behind the body, palms back. Pack the shoulders DOWN and BACK, shrug UP and slightly back, 1s peak squeeze, slow down. The 'opposite movement' that decompresses the right shoulder — costs nothing, easy to forget.

sets.name: Banded Shoulder Prep (~3 min)

exercises.notes: Mini-band overhead OR blue rope band gripped in hands.
Elbows drive to the ribs, scaps depress.
Press out to a T — fires rear delts and mid-traps.
Pull apart at the sternum, scaps retract, ribs down.
Sweep the arms back. Don't overarch.
15s each side. Primes the lateral hinge for the windmill + bent press.
Both arms in a V/Y overhead. Hold and breathe — lower traps fire, primes the strict press + TGU lockout.

sets.notes: 1 round of all 7 banded moves (~3 min). Sustained tension, no rest between positions.

sets.name: 🔆🌀 Flow + Coordination (permanent block — Spotlight: Split-Stance Pass-Through)

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 15-20lb. Warm-up familiar — slow halos to groove the tight orbit before the pass-through.

**LOAD:** ~20lb (LIGHT — coordination + grip, not leg load). 3 rounds, switch the front leg halfway.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — stay low, pass smooth:**
- **Drop into a split stance (lunge) and STAY LOW** — rear knee toward the floor, front shin vertical, hold the depth the whole set
- **Pass the bell hand-to-hand between the legs** — front-to-back or in a figure-8 around the front leg, smooth and continuous
- **Torso TALL, core braced** — the lunge hold + the pass is the work; don't stand up out of the lunge to pass
- **Eyes forward, soft hands** on the catch
- **Switch the front leg halfway** through the round

**Reflection:** does the split stance stay LOW and stable while the bell passes, or do you pop up out of the lunge to make the pass easier? Staying low under the pass is the whole skill. Light bell, clean reps over fast reps.

sets.notes: **Permanent Flow + Coordination block.** Base KB skill-building — light bell, flowing coordination. A familiar halo to warm up, then this week's chain (split-stance pass-through). 3 rounds, ~5 min, short rest. Keep it light and clean; it precedes the strength + flow work and shouldn't fatigue the legs.

sets.name: Strength Block (Lighter — Thursday Variant)

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 40lb (the new working bell — W18 stepped these up from 30). 8 each side. Hips hinged, back flat, pull the elbow to the hip.

**LOAD:** 40/45/50 ascending — strict single-arm press (clean to rack, press straight up, NO push-press). 5 each side, THREE sets, go up the rack across them (50 the new top — W18 hit 50x5, 'should start edging up a bit').
- **Strict, not push-press** — the legs don't help; the shoulder presses it
- **Ribs DOWN** before the press — no rib flare
- **Bicep finishes by the ear, full lockout, pack the shoulder DOWN**
- Slow descent back to the rack
- **Both sides to the same standard** — press the left as clean as the right.

sets.notes: Lighter strength block — single-arm row + strict press. The bigger compound presses / conditioning are Tuesday's job. ~5 min.

sets.name: Bent Press Flow (Light Groove — Skill Practice)

exercises.notes: Bell starts on the floor between the feet, hips drive the lift, catch in the rack with the knees slightly bent.
Goblet/rack position. **LIGHT** — Thursday before Friday legs, keep depth without grinding. Sit tall, full depth, no bouncing.
Stride out wide, sit into the working leg, keep the other leg long. Mobility, not strength.

The deliberate leverage move inside the flow — **the body goes DOWN, the bell barely moves.** From the rack, hinge and rotate AWAY from the bell side, eyes tracking the bell, until the arm locks out overhead — you lower your body under the bell, you don't press it up. Slow and smooth; it's leverage, not a press.
Control on the way down — bell to the floor as cleanly as it came up. Closes the flow before switching sides.

sets.name: 🔆 Strength + Loaded Cossack + Hand-to-Hand Swing (Spotlight: Loaded Cossack)

description: Volume steady, station-grouped. **Warmup reminder:** bodyweight squat (depth check) → cross-leg lateral lean (QL/psoas) → hip circles → tibialis raise → cat-cow → internal core fist rotation → dead-bug core/QL primer (the W19 test) → bodyweight lunge (QL check). dayOverview.theme: Steady state, station-grouped. Spotlights cycle to squat depth (formalize the 45→70→80 ROM ramp — depth is the lever) + leg curl (form-first at 80, 70 primer grooves the pattern).
