**Squat spotlight — the 45→70→80 ROM ramp, depth is the lever.** 45x8 to drill max depth, 70x6-8 as the ROM intermediary, then 80 working — chase the bottom every set ('better ROM than last week, ~85%'). Reps are NOT the point right now; ROM + the mid-range are. Run 80 for as many working sets as depth holds; stop adding sets when the depth shortens. Hips still super tight — keep breathing into the bottom.

**Leg curl spotlight — form-first at 80.** Settings 5/m/0/-1 (verify before loading). First set at 70 to groove the pattern ('primes my brain to do it correctly'), then 80 working with the slow eccentric. 80 done correctly beats 90 with drift — let 90 return only once 80 is automatic. Don't push back to 90.

**Dead-bug core/QL primer in the warmup — the W19 test.** W18's leg press was unusually brutal ('sweating like a wet dog') with the core/QL pre-fatigued from Thursday's figure-8s; your read was 'should do more to wake it up.' This week a short dead-bug set wakes the deep core before the leg press — watch whether the leg press feels more normal when the QL ISN'T pre-fatigued from Thursday. It's a test, not a fix.

**Bulgarian → double-45 DBs (regular DB is the DEFAULT).** The Smith machine is the SWAP-IN when it's free — it's cleared the QL test at 45/side two weeks running (W17 + W18). **Pigeon on the bench between sets** kept the hip/QL loose W18 ('really helped') — use it as a station option. If anything twitches, drop to bodyweight and finish.
**Leg press ROM** — deep knees-to-chest, lower back stays on the pad. It feels harder cold and opens by the end; don't judge the load on set 1. Hold 4 plates, ROM-first.
**Station-grouped sequence:** warmup → squat → leg press → leg-press-calf-raise (SAME machine, stay there) → Bulgarian (bench station) → leg curl → incline RDL → cool-down. No backtracking.
**Keep leg curl BEFORE incline RDL** — reversed, the two hamstring lifts stack and smoke the second.

**QL/psoas watch** — cross-leg lateral lean in the warmup AND cool-down. QL's been clear (W18 'sore but no spasms' even going in tight from Thursday's figure-8s). If anything talks in the warmup, modify the day; mid-session, drop a set + take stretch breaks (your self-regulation W18 worked).

sets.name: Warmup (incl. Cross-Leg Lateral Lean — QL/Psoas Release + Dead-Bug Core/QL Primer)

exercises.notes: Full depth, slow. Find where the hips are tight and breathe into it. Depth check before loading.

30s each side. Scissor one foot over the other, reach the same-side arm overhead, lean away from the back leg — the stretch runs down the side of the waist into the QL and lateral hip. Do this before loading the squat.
Big slow circles. Wake up the hip stabilizers.

Back to a wall, heels a step out, weight on the heels. Pull the toes UP toward the shins as high as they'll go, lower slow. Wakes the shins (the calf's antagonist), preps ankle dorsiflexion for squat depth, and it's shin insurance for the run-in. ~30s, bodyweight.
Spine mobility — slow, full ROM each direction.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension. Quick posterior-chain and low-back opener before loading the squat.

**Core/QL primer — the W19 test.** On your back, arms up, knees over hips. Press the lower back FLAT into the floor and HOLD it there as you slowly extend the opposite arm + leg, then switch. The brace is the work — wakes the deep core before the leg press. (W18 the leg press ran brutal with the core pre-fatigued; this is the test of whether waking it early changes that — watch how the leg press feels today.)
Bodyweight. QL check — if anything talks here, modify the day. Also previews the Bulgarian pattern.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT (depth refresh) — the bottom half of your 45→70→80 ramp:**
- **Set 1: 45/side x8** — used to DRILL max depth. Depth isn't 100% even here, so chase it light: sit all the way into the bottom, breathe, feel where the hips block.
- **Set 2: 70/side x6** — the intermediary ROM-builder (your W18 self-found tool). Same depth as the working sets, heavier than the 45 so the bottom is honest. This is where the mid-range gets drilled before 80.

**LOAD:** 80/side. Working sets off the ramp — run 80 for 6-8 reps, as many sets as your depth holds (W18 was 80x6 then 80x8, ROM '~85%, better than last week'). **Depth is the lever, not reps or load** — your stated goal is fixing the ROM + the mid-range; hips still super tight.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — chase the bottom set by set:**
- Bar high on the upper traps (NOT the neck), upper-back shelf squeezed
- **Brace like prepping for a punch** — deep belly breath at the top, HOLD through the descent, exhale on the drive up
- **Hips back AND down**, not just down
- **'Spread the floor'** — screw the feet in, knees track over the toes
- **Sit into the bottom** — keep chasing depth; you find depth easier under load, so trust the 80 to help you sink
- Drive through the WHOLE foot
- **Stop adding working sets when the depth shortens** — a shallow grind isn't the work; bank the deep ones

**Reflection:** does the bottom get deeper as you warm through the ramp (45 → 70 → 80), and does 80 hold ~85%+ depth — or does it shorten under load? Deep at 80 is the win; if depth caps, that's the honest end, hold 80 and keep drilling the ramp.

sets.name: Leg Press + Calf Raise Station (Same Machine — Leg Press ROM)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 4 plates/side. 4 sets of 12.
- **Full ROM — knees toward the chest.** The deep position trains the abs/QL/core as much as the quads — that's the intent ('legs barely doing anything in the deep squat')
- **Foot position:** shoulder-width, mid-foot on the platform, slight toe-out
- **It feels harder cold** — the deep ROM opens up once the hips are warm, so don't judge the load on set 1
- **Actively press to keep the lower back from lifting off the pad** at the bottom; if the hips roll off, back off a hair (or stop just shy of the catcher)
- **Press through the WHOLE foot** — heels grounded
- **Slow descent (3s), no bounce at the bottom**; don't lock out hard at the top
- **Note for the test:** W18 this ran unusually brutal ('sweating like a wet dog') with the core pre-fatigued. With the dead-bug primer + a clear QL today, see if it feels more normal. Hold 4 plates, ROM-first — don't read one hard session as a load change.

**LOAD:** 4 plates/side. 3 sets of 15. Stay on the leg press — same machine, no walking off.
- **Balls of both feet on the BOTTOM EDGE of the platform, heels hanging off**
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the heels drop as far below the edge as they'll go
- **Drive to FULL plantarflexion at the top**
- **Tempo by feel** — own the stretch at the bottom and the squeeze at the top, no bouncing. (3 sets, after the 4 leg-press sets — same station.)

sets.name: Bulgarian Split Squat (Double-45 DBs — Smith @45 the Alternate; Pigeon Between Sets)

exercises.equipment: bench + DBs (regular default) — Smith machine if free (use smith-machine-bulgarian-split-squat)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** two 45lb DBs, one per hand. 3 sets of 8-10 each leg. **Regular DB version is the default; the Smith machine is the swap-in when it's free** (it's cleared the QL test at 45/side two weeks — W17 + W18 — so it's a confirmed QL-safe alternate).

**Pigeon on the bench between sets** — W18 keeper ('really helped' keep the hip/QL loose under the split-squat load). Take it between sets, plus stretch breaks as needed.
- **Rear foot up on the bench** behind you, laces down or toes tucked
- **Step out far enough that the front shin stays roughly VERTICAL at the bottom** — too short a stance = the knee crashes past the toes
- **Front knee tracks over the front foot** — not caving in
- **Lower until the rear knee nearly touches the floor** — controlled, no dropping
- **Drive up through the FRONT HEEL** — the front leg does the work, the rear leg is a kickstand
- **Torso TALL** — a slight forward lean is fine, no folding over
- **2s descent**, own the bottom

**Watch:** at double-45 this is real load — if anything twitches/spasms, drop to bodyweight for the remaining sets and finish.

sets.name: 🔆 Seated Leg Curl (Spotlight — 5/m/0/-1, 70 Primer + 80 Working, Before Incline RDL)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 70 first set to center, then 80 working. Slow tempo. **Settings: 5/m/0/-1** (verify before loading — the setting that felt better than /1 in W17).

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the correct feel at 80, form-first:**
- **First set at 70 to groove the pattern** — 'primes my brain to do it correctly' (it'll feel easy; that's the point)
- **Then 80 for the working sets** — W18 this 'felt pretty correct vs what it used to be.' 80 done right beats 90 with drift; let 90 return only once 80 is automatic — don't push back to 90
- **Ankles UNDER the pad** — the ankle bone is the contact point, NOT the mid-calf
- **Lap pad locked DOWN firmly** — a loose pad lets the torso lift and turns it into lower-back work
- **Curl the heels toward the glutes** — full ROM, full squeeze
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze** — the slow eccentric is the whole stimulus; you feel these deeply when you go slow
- Torso anchored, no lifting forward. This comes BEFORE incline RDL on purpose — take the working sets with the legs still relatively fresh.

**Reflection:** does 80 keep that 'correct' feel (heels driving, hamstring doing the work, no torso lift) for all the working sets — or does it start drifting? The correct feel IS the win here, not the number. When 80 is automatic, 90 comes back on its own.

**LOAD:** 45lb plate. 3 sets of 15, dead slow with a 2s pause at the bottom. (W18 the slow squeeze was dialing in — hitting the hamstrings/glutes so well it was 'hard to get off the machine'; that's the form landing.)
- **Pad just below the hip crease** — NOT on the upper thigh, NOT on the stomach
- **Hip hinge** — a Romanian deadlift on the 45° bench, NOT a lumbar extension. Lower back NEUTRAL throughout
- **At the bottom:** the stretch is in the **hamstrings and glutes**, NOT the lower back. If the lumbar rounds, you're going too deep for current mobility
- **Drive up by squeezing the glutes and hamstrings**; at the top, stop at neutral — past neutral = lumbar load = QL irritation
- **Tempo: 3s eccentric, 2s pause at the bottom, 1s drive up.** The slow eccentric is the entire reason this works — hold the 45lb plate, keep slowing the tempo; don't chase the load. (If the legs are smoked from the leg press, cutting the last set is the honest end, not a regression.)

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Recovery Block (Hip/QL-Biased for Legs Day)

exercises.notes: 30s each side. Scissor the legs, reach overhead, lean away from the back leg — bookend the session with the same QL/psoas release as the warmup.
45s each side. Deep hip-flexor and glute release — the long hold lets the QL and psoas let go.
30s each side. Gentle twist for the QL — draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
45s each side. Hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Knees wide, arms extended forward. Parasympathetic shift.

sets.notes: 5-min recovery block, hip/QL-biased on legs day.

tips: **Steady state, station-grouped.** Squat ramp (45/70 + 80 working), leg press 4, calf raise 3, Bulgarian 3, leg curl 3, incline RDL 3.
**Spotlight: squat depth + leg curl.** Squat formalizes your 45→70→80 ROM ramp (depth the lever, not load); leg curl drills the correct feel at 80 (form-first, 70 primer grooves it).
**Squat holds 80 — depth is the work.** Chase the bottom each set; stop adding working sets when depth shortens. Hips still tight — breathe into the bottom.
**Leg curl 80 working, not 90** — 80 done correctly beats 90 with drift. Let 90 return only once 80 is automatic.
**Dead-bug core/QL primer in the warmup — the W19 test.** Wakes the core before the leg press; watch whether the leg press normalizes with the QL not pre-fatigued from Thursday.
**Bulgarian double-45 DBs, regular version is the default.** Smith @45 is the confirmed QL-safe alternate (2 weeks clear). Pigeon on the bench between sets ('really helped' W18).
**Station-grouped:** warmup → squat → leg press → leg-press-calf-raise (same machine — stay there) → Bulgarian → leg curl → incline RDL → cool-down. No backtracking.
**Leg curl BEFORE incline RDL** — don't reverse them, or the hamstring work stacks.
**Incline RDL is a 45lb plate, dead slow** — tempo is the progression; the slow squeeze is dialing in.
**Cross-leg lateral lean in the warmup AND cool-down** — QL/psoas release. QL held W18 even going in tight; keep bookending it + take stretch breaks.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, hip/QL-biased on legs day.**
Rest: 3 min squats, 2 min leg press, 90s calf raise + Bulgarian + isolations.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state legs week. The squat and leg curl get the deep-cue treatment — both around quality, not load: the squat formalizes the user's own 45→70→80 ROM-building ramp with depth as the explicit lever (goal = fix the ROM + the mid-range), and the leg curl drills the correct feel at 80 (the 70 primer grooves the pattern; 90 returns only once 80 is automatic). A dead-bug core/QL primer joins the warmup to test the user's instinct that the core is the exposed weak link. The sequence keeps the two hamstring lifts from stacking and the station order from backtracking. Form leads load — building decades, not weeks.

name: W19 Morning Flow — Bodyweight Spine + Hip (All Days, Rotated Variety)
description: 15 min bodyweight floor flow — universal W19 morning flow, used every training day (Mon push / Tue KB / Wed pull / Thu KB / Fri legs). Same three-part shape as W11-W18 with ~half the moves rotated for variety: this week brings in low-lunge thoracic rotation, dead-bug, inchworm walkout, McGill crunch, and cycles back the W12-era couch stretch + frog stretch. Three-part: spine primer → bodyweight work → deep stretch arc. Day-specific therapeutic add-on at the end (push = pec-minor protocol; pull = dead hang + scap pull; legs = cross-leg lateral lean + pigeon + supine twist; KB days skip — banded prep covers it).

exercises.notes: Slow, full ROM each direction. Spine wave wakes the segment-by-segment articulation.

Rotates in for W19 — 45s each side. In a low lunge, hand down inside the front foot, reach the other arm to the ceiling and rotate the upper back open, then thread it back under. Thoracic rotation + hip-flexor opener in one — wakes the mid-back and the hips before the day's work.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — the wrist dials a stretch up the back chain. Stays in the primer.

sets.name: Work Block — Bodyweight Activation (~5 min)

exercises.notes: **Greasing set — 1 quick set, NEVER to failure.** Daily frequency is the point (same idea as the pull-up greasing set — the floor rises over time). Elbows ~45° (not flared), ribs down, glutes tight, body one line, **pack down not up.** Stop 2-3 reps short. Back off / drop to knees if the right shoulder talks at the bottom.

Rotates in for W19 — on your back, arms up, knees over hips. Press the lower back FLAT into the floor and HOLD it as you slowly extend the opposite arm + leg, then switch. The brace is the work — deep-core anti-extension (also the legs-day warmup primer).
Feet flat, drive through the heels, squeeze the glutes to a tall bridge, ribs down — no arching the lower back. Posterior-chain wake-up.
30s each side. Anti-rotation — opposite arm + leg extend, hold a beat, hips stay square (no swinging).

Rotates in for W19 — from standing, hinge and walk the hands out to a plank, hold a beat (ribs down), then walk the hands back and stand tall. Dynamic hamstring + shoulder + core warm-up that links the whole front and back line.

Rotates in for W19 — McGill curl-up (his Big 3): one knee bent, hands under the low back to keep its natural arch, lift the head/shoulders just an inch WITHOUT flexing the spine. A posture-safe core brace — hold each rep a beat. Switch the bent leg halfway.

sets.notes: Opens with a pushup greasing set (1 quick set, never to failure — daily habit). Dead-bug, inchworm walkout, McGill crunch rotate in for W19; glute bridge + bird-dog (anti-rotation) stay.

sets.name: Yoga Flow — Deep Stretch Arc (~7 min)

exercises.notes: 30s each side. Stays every week — signature spine move.

Cycles back for W19 (a W12-era favorite) — 45s each side. Back knee on the mat, shin up a wall or couch, front foot planted, sink the hips forward and stand tall. Deep hip-flexor + quad stretch — counters all the sitting and primes the squat/hinge work.
30s each side. Hip flexor + adductor + back-leg quad. Drop to elbows if accessible. Stays — durable hip opener.
Bodyweight, slow. Stays every week — keeps the loaded cossack pattern grooved (and it's back on KB Tuesday this week).

Stays — sit in a wide straddle, reach toward one foot, then center (chest toward the floor), then the other foot. Slow, breathe into each reach. The straddle + adductor + hamstring opener the flow design calls for.

Cycles back for W19 (a W12-era favorite) — knees wide on the mat, shins out, sink the hips back toward the heels. Deep adductor + inner-hip opener to close the arc — useful before legs day, and a counter to all the lateral KB work this week.

sets.notes: Continuous arc — flow between shapes, breathe deeply. Anchors stay (scorpion, lizard, cossack BW, straddle reaches); couch stretch + frog stretch cycle back from the W12-era for W19.

sets.name: 📍 Day-Specific Add-On — Pick by Today's Training (~3-5 min)

exercises.notes: **📍 PUSH DAYS — KEY PROTOCOL MOVE.** 30s each at LOW / MID / HIGH elbow positions. Arm bent 90°, forearm on the door frame, step through and rotate the torso AWAY. Desk work continuously re-tightens pec minor — daily.
**📍 PUSH DAYS** — active side of the pec-minor fix. Lower trap + rotator cuff.
**📍 PUSH DAYS** — serratus activation, helps unstick a tight pec minor.
**📍 PUSH DAYS (optional)** — slow rotator cuff work. Add if the shoulder feels off.
**📍 PUSH DAYS (optional)** — pins the shoulder blades in the corrected position.
**📍 PULL DAYS** — 25s. Decompress the shoulders, warm the grip.
**📍 PULL DAYS** — scapulae retracting only, no elbow bend. Crisp scap engagement before loaded pulls.
**📍 LEGS DAYS** — 30s each side. Scissor one foot over the other, reach the same-side arm overhead, lean away from the back leg — QL/psoas release. Also in the legs-workout warmup.
**📍 LEGS DAYS — QL-SPASM PROTOCOL.** 90s each side. Long hold lets the QL/psoas release. Non-negotiable on legs day.
**📍 LEGS DAYS** — 60s each side. Gentle twist for the QL. Lacrosse-ball QL roll above the iliac crest beforehand if available.

sets.notes: **Pick today's day-specific protocol — push / pull / legs.** ~3-5 min total. KB days (Tue/Thu) skip this block — the in-workout banded prep covers the equivalent.

tips: Same shape as W11-W18, ~half the moves rotated. Morning flows stay low-fatigue; variety keeps them fresh.
**15 min main flow + 3-5 min day-specific add-on** — universal across W19 (Mon push / Tue KB / Wed pull / Thu KB / Fri legs).
**Scorpion + cossack BW + lizard pose + straddle reaches stay every week** — durable anchors.
**Rotated in for W19:** low-lunge thoracic rotation, dead-bug, inchworm walkout, McGill crunch. **Cycled back (W12-era): couch stretch, frog stretch.**
**Day-specific add-on at the end** — push days do the pec-minor protocol, pull days do dead hang + scap pull, legs days do cross-leg lean + 90s pigeon + supine twist. KB days skip the add-on.
If short on time: low-lunge thoracic rotation + lizard + cossack BW + frog stretch, plus today's day-specific add-on.
formPhilosophy: Same as W11-W18 — variety means different shapes hitting the same patterns. Scorpion-family spine work + hip openers + adductor/straddle stretches. W19 rotates ~half: fresh core/dynamic work in the work block (dead-bug, inchworm, McGill crunch), a thoracic-rotation primer, and the W12-era couch + frog stretches cycled back so the flow doesn't calcify; the rehab anchors and the day-specific PPL protocols stay. Building decades, not weeks.

name: Week 19 Pull — Steady State (Spotlight: Lat Pulldown + Face Pull)
description: Volume steady; the protective behind-back shrug stays front-loaded as activation. **Warmup reminder:** behind-back shrug FIRST (protective activation, 3 sets) → band-pull-apart → cat-cow → internal core fist rotation → active dead hang. Spotlights cycle forward to the lat pulldown (stepped to 150 on the regular machine W18 — 'clearly the new weight') and the face pull (stepped to 50 — 'hard even with good form'), drilling both at the new working numbers. W18's user-pulled steps are now the defaults: chest-supported row 45, lat pulldown 150, face pull 50, high cable curl 180. DB row holds the 70/80/90 bare-hand pyramid (grip the cap, no straps). Pull-up goes back to the straight bar — the swivel grip rotates toward the bicep and pulls work off the lats. Cable lifts list a number per equipment option.

dayOverview.theme: Steady state. Shrug stays FIRST (protective activation). Spotlights cycle to lat pulldown (now 150, regular machine) + face pull (now 50) — drilled at the new working numbers. New defaults from W18's user-pulled steps: chest-supported row 45, lat pulldown 150, face pull 50, high curl 180. DB row holds 70/80/90, no straps. Pull-up back to the straight bar. Both shoulders pain-free now ('only regular weakness') — grip is the cap, not the shoulder.

spotlights.why: Cycles forward — stepped from 140 to 150 on the regular machine W18 ('140 was easy last week… clearly this is the new weight'), finished a bit ugly on the late sets. Spotlight drills the wide-grip, lats-to-the-back-pockets pull and the slow controlled return so 150 cleans up into solid reps — grip + back the honest cap, no straps.

Cycles forward — took the optional step to 50 W18 ('hard at 50 even with good form!') with the elbows still high. Spotlight drills the knuckles-up grip + elbows-above-the-shoulders cue that's the make-or-break for moving the work into the back, so 50 stays clean and the front shoulder never takes over.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W17 chest-supported row + reverse fly · W18 pull-up + DB row · W19 lat pulldown + face pull (current) · W20 cycle forward — high cable curl + cable crunch refresh.
watchpoints: **Behind-back shrug stays FIRST (activation slot).** Front-loading it keeps pull day flare-free — the protective counter-movement to all the pulling can't be the piece a rushed session drops. Right after the warmup.

**Pull-up back to the STRAIGHT BAR.** The adjustable swivel grip rotates toward the bicep mid-pull and pulls work off the lats (W18 self-discovery: 'probably not the best for pull ups'). Straight bar is the preferred variant — W18 held a clean 8/8/8/8 on it.

**Lat pulldown spotlight — 150 on the regular machine (back-left).** New working number; W18 it 'finished ugly / did too many,' so the reps will clean up as it settles. Per-equipment numbers below — pick what's free, log which.

**Face pull spotlight — 50, knuckles-up grip stays.** Grip the rope ends in fists, knuckles up, elbows ABOVE the shoulders — that's what unlocked 50 with the form holding. If the elbows drop, the front shoulder takes over — re-set them high.

**DB row holds 70/80/90, no straps.** Top set 90 felt good W18 ('could go up in reps') — let the reps creep on the 90 as the grip allows; grip is the limiter (left hand taps first), set the DB down when grip gives.
**High cable curl 180** — was 'easy on all sides, can go up' W18. A small further step (185-190) is earned IF it moves clean (you pull it); otherwise hold 180.

**Cable crunch — watch the magnetic micro add-ons.** The stack has add-on weights that can be on without you noticing (W18: a '67.5' was actually 70.5). Read the actual stack. 62.5 is the clean form-first base, 66.5 comfortable at x15, 70.5 the current brutal ceiling.
**Loads otherwise hold** — chest-supported row 45, reverse fly 20, incline curl 25 / preacher when free.
**Left bicep first, every set** — keep the protocol as insurance; the left still struggles to hit 9-10 on the last incline-curl sets.
**Grip is the ceiling on the pulling lifts, not the shoulder** — DB row, lat pulldown, farmer carry all tap out at grip now. No straps.
**Cable lifts have per-equipment numbers** — pick what's free, log equipment + number.

exercises.notes: Scap activation. Squeeze the shoulder blades together, soft elbow.
Spine warm — slow, full ROM each direction.
Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — primes grip and the pulling chain before bar work.
Active hang, not collapsed — engage the lats, pull the shoulders DOWN away from the ears even at full extension. Primes the pull-ups.

sets.name: Behind-Back DB Shrug — Protective Activation (DO THIS FIRST)

exercises.equipment: DB pair, held behind the body
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40-50lb pair. 3 sets — first in the session.

**Why it's here, first:** this is the 'opposite movement' to all the pulling — a counter/decompression for the right shoulder. Front-loading it keeps pull day flare-free. It reads more like a stretch than a lift; that's the point.
- **DBs held BEHIND the body** at the sides of the hips/glutes — palms facing back
- **Shoulders pull DOWN and BACK** at the start — packed, not relaxed
- **Shrug UP and slightly BACK** — pinch the shoulder blades at the top
- **Hold 1s at the top**, slow descent
- **Pack DOWN, NOT up** as the resting position — the lower position IS the work
- Chest open, not slouched.

sets.notes: Protective trap-chain activation, front of the session. ~4 min. Light-to-moderate, peak-squeeze — a decompression, not a max effort.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** Bodyweight. 4 sets of 6-8 (W18 held a clean 8/8/8/8).

**Back to the STRAIGHT BAR** — the adjustable swivel grip rotates toward the bicep mid-pull and pulls work off the lats ('probably not the best for pull ups'). The straight bar's been feeling best and keeps the work in the back.
- **Active hang start**, shoulders pulled down out of the ears — NOT a collapsed dead hang
- **Pull elbows DOWN to ribs**, NOT chin to bar — 'drive the elbows into the back pockets'
- **Chest leads to the bar at the top**, eyes ahead, head neutral
- **Slow eccentric ~2-3s**, active hang at the bottom of every rep — no dropping, no kip
- **Stop the set when the rep stops being clean** — frequency over max effort; both shoulders are pain-free now ('only regular weakness'), so grip + honest strength are the limiter, not the shoulder. Bank 6 clean over 8 sloppy.

sets.name: DB Rack / Bench Block — DB Row + Chest-Supported Row + Incline Curl + Reverse Fly (3 Rounds)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 70/80/90 ascending pyramid — one set per round (70, then 80, then 90). No straps.
- **Chest-supported on the incline bench** — chest glued to the pad, no twisting up for the last reps
- **Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit** — keeps it in the lats
- **Slow 2s descent, 1s squeeze on the 70 and 80** — those hold clean form
- **On the 90 set, let the reps creep** — W18 was 90x6 and 'felt good, could go up in reps.' Drive the elbow, aim for clean reps before form breaks rather than grinding sloppy ones
- **Grip is the limiter** (left hand taps first) — set the DB down when grip gives, not when the back fails. No straps — train the grip.

**LOAD:** 45 (the new working weight — stepped up from 40 W18, 'I guess this is my new working weight,' x12 all sets slow eccentric). 3 sets of 10-12.
- **Chest stays GLUED to the incline bench** the whole set — if the chest peels off to heave the DBs, the weight's ahead of the form
- **Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit**
- **Don't rotate the torso** — both sides stay on the pad
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the shoulder blade protract, then re-pull from the stretch
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze** at the top, no DB slam at the bottom.

**LOAD:**
- **Actual preacher bench when it's open** — EZ bar, ~2×10 on the bar; take the real preacher whenever it's free, it locks the upper arm better than the incline lean
- **Incline bench, 25lb DBs** (default) — chest-supported curl, 3 sets of 8-10

- **Incline bench ~45°, lean in chest-first** — armpit and the back of the upper arm flat on the pad; the upper arm stays flat the ENTIRE rep (don't lift the elbow)
- **Left arm first, every set** — the left still struggles to hit 9-10 on the last two sets, so keep the left-first protocol as insurance
- **Full stretch at the bottom — pause 2s**
- **Curl smoothly to the peak squeeze**, no swing; 2-3s eccentric.

**LOAD:** 20lb. 3 sets of 12 — cap at 12 with a slower eccentric rather than chasing reps ('getting hard at end, still good working weight' W18).
- **30° reverse-incline** (chest-down on the incline bench), DBs hanging fully extended at the start
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED throughout** — a sweep, NOT a row; the elbow angle never changes
- **Lead with the elbow, hand passive** — the hand never lifts first
- **Wings out and slightly UP to shoulder height** — sweep wide, don't lift, don't shrug
- **Hold the top a beat, then 2s eccentric** — control the drop. Rear-delt / mid-trap shoulder-health work; quality over the number.

sets.notes: One trip to the DB rack covers all 4 lifts. Incline bench at ~30° for the rows + reverse fly (30° reverse-incline), set to ~45° for the incline curl. 3 rounds.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD (pick whichever station's free, log which one + the number):**
- **Regular lat pulldown machine: 150** (the new working number, back-left — stepped from 140 W18)
- **Dual pulley: 70**
- **Cable column: 52.5-57.5**
- **Cable pulley: 47.5**

3 sets.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — clean reps at the new 150:**
- **Wide grip near the bend** — more lat isolation, less bicep
- **Slight backward lean ~15°, NO further** — more = it becomes a row
- **Pull the bar to the UPPER CHEST — NEVER behind the neck**
- **'Lats squeezing oranges into the back pockets'** at the bottom
- **1s pause at the contraction, 2s controlled return** to a full overhead stretch
- **Grip is the limiter at the end** — the honest cap, same as the DB row; no straps

**Reflection:** W18 the 150 'finished ugly / did too many' on the late sets — does it clean up this week (full reps, controlled return), or is 150 still grinding on set 3? The reps will tidy as it settles; bank clean reps over ugly ones.

sets.name: 🔆 Cable Column — Face Pull (Spotlight — 3 Sets at 50)

exercises.equipment: cable column (mid/upper-chest height + rope)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** cable column **50** (the new working number — stepped from 47.5 W18, 'hard at 50 even with good form!').

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — elbows high, work in the back:**
- **Grip the rope ends in fists, knuckles up** — that's the change that made 50 feel right with the elbows still high; keep it
- **Pull the rope to face level** — not to the chest
- **ELBOWS HIGH (above the shoulders)** — the make-or-break cue; this is what moves the work into the back
- **External-rotate at the top** — knuckles point UP, like the top of a double-biceps pose
- **1s peak hold**, then a slow 2s return — let the cable pull the arms back, don't drop

**Reflection:** do the elbows stay above the shoulders for all 3 sets at 50, or do they drop and the front of the shoulder start taking over? Elbows high = the work's in the back. If they drop and stay dropped, that's the honest cap — back to 47.5 rather than grind 50 with low elbows.

sets.name: Cable Column Finisher — High Cable Curl + Cable Crunch (2-3 Sets)

exercises.equipment: cable column (low pulley, single D-handle, one arm at a time)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD (single arm — scales differ, log which station):**
- Cable column (single D-handle): **180** — was 'easy on all sides, can go up' W18; optional **185-190 if it moves clean** (you pull this)
- Pulley / weight-stack station: ~120
2 working sets per arm.
- **Single arm at a time, one D-handle** — stand sideways, arm out at shoulder level
- **Upper arm parallel to the floor, FIXED** — the whole point of the high-cable variant
- **Curl the hand toward the ear**, peak squeeze
- **Left arm first**; slow eccentric, no bounce at the start.

**LOAD (pick whichever station's free, log which one — AND read the actual stack):**
- **Cable pulley (rope): 62.5** — the clean form-first base; **66.5 comfortable at x15**, **70.5 the current brutal ceiling**
- **Watch the magnetic micro add-ons** — they can be on without you noticing (W18: a '67.5' was actually 70.5). Read the stack before you start.

3 sets.
- **HIPS LOCKED** — the most important cue. The hips do not move.
- **Crunch from the abs ONLY** — the spine flexes, the hips stay put. Hips moving = hip-flexor work, not abs.
- **Chest toward the thighs**, hold the crunch 1 second
- **Slow eccentric, all the way** — at 62.5 the controlled drop IS available; use it. Only climb the load if the form holds; if the hips start yanking, stay at 62.5.

sets.notes: Same cable column as the face pull. 2 rounds = 2 sets each; round the cable crunch to 3 if there's time and the abs aren't fried.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow position. Pec minor lengthen.
Passive hang. Don't engage — let the shoulders unpack and the spine decompress.
30s each side. Draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
45s each side. Hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Parasympathetic shift.

sets.notes: 5 minutes of recovery work, non-negotiable closing block.

tips: **Behind-back shrug stays FIRST** — protective decompression that keeps pull day flare-free.
**Spotlight: lat pulldown + face pull.** Lat pulldown drills clean reps at the new 150 (regular machine); face pull drills the knuckles-up / elbows-high cue at the new 50.
**Pull-up back to the straight bar** — the swivel grip rotates to the bicep and pulls work off the lats. W18 held 8/8/8/8 clean on the straight bar.
**New defaults from W18's user-pulled steps:** chest-supported row 45, lat pulldown 150, face pull 50, high cable curl 180.
**DB row holds 70/80/90, no straps.** Let the reps creep on the 90 ('could go up in reps' W18). Grip is the limiter (left hand).
**High cable curl 180** — optional 185-190 if it moves clean (you pull it); otherwise hold.
**Cable crunch — read the stack** (magnetic micro add-ons can be on unnoticed). 62.5 base, 66.5 comfortable, 70.5 ceiling.
**Loads otherwise hold** — reverse fly 20, incline curl 25 / preacher when free.
**Left bicep first, every set** — the left still lags on the last incline-curl sets.
**Grip is the ceiling on pulling, not the shoulder** — both shoulders pain-free now ('only regular weakness'). No straps.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, permanent every gym day.**
Rest: shrug 60s, 2.5 min pull-ups, 90s DB block, 2 min lat pulldown, 90s face pull, 60s finisher.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state pull week with the protective shrug leading. The spotlights drill the two lifts the user stepped up himself last week — the lat pulldown at the new 150 and the face pull at the new 50 — because clean reps at the new working number is how a fresh step settles in. Both shoulders are pain-free now, so grip is the honest cap on the heavy pulls (no straps), and the pull-up goes back to the straight bar to keep the work in the back. Loads otherwise hold; the floor rising is the win. Building decades, not weeks.

name: Week 19 Push — Steady State (Spotlight: Push Press + Lateral Raise)
description: Volume and loads hold; the work is rest discipline + depth of execution. **Warmup reminder:** arm circles → Yuri's band shoulder warmup → bottoms-up press (18lb, 8/side, forward + T-plane, T-plane light) → light Kinesis-fly chest opener → internal core fist rotation → push-up → pull-up greasing set → protective behind-back shrug. Spotlights cycle forward to the push press (where the rest experiment lives) and the DB lateral raise. Push-press note now spells out the rest explicitly: take a FULL 2 min between sets — W18 showed ~1 min recovered the feel but not the set-3 rep, so this week run the real 2 min once before reading anything into the set-3 number. Push press holds at 45, lateral raise at 15; incline DB steps to 50 this week as a set-1 test (50/45/45 fallback) after 5 clean weeks at 3×12/45. The bottoms-up press joins the warmup as rotator-cuff prep, and the mini-dip-on-the-bar warmup stays on the dip station.

dayOverview.theme: Steady state — loads hold, the work is rest discipline + depth. Spotlight cycles to the push press (run the FULL 2 min rest this week — the experiment) + the DB lateral raise. Push press first, fresh. Bottoms-up press joins the warmup (rotator-cuff prep before pressing). Mini-dip warmup stays on the dip station. Shoulder's been the best in a while ('weakness, not pain') — keep banking the headroom, don't spend it.

spotlights.why: Cycles forward — it's the lift carrying the open question. W18 ~1 min rest improved the feel ('first set super easy, last super hard') but set 3 still hit 8, not 10. Spotlight drills the explosive leg drive + vertical path AND makes the rest the experiment: run a true 2 min between sets this week and see whether set 3 recovers to 10. If it does, the 8 was under-rest; if not, 8 is the honest set-3 number at 45. Either way hold 45.

Cycles forward — the medial-delt isolation that's quietly become 'wasn't too bad actually' at 15 (W18), a floor-rising read on a lift that used to be 'always hard.' Spotlight drills the lead-with-the-elbow, stop-at-shoulder-height, 2s-eccentric pattern + the scap reset between sets that's kept the right shoulder quiet here.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W17 push press + incline DB · W18 dips + cable block · W19 push press + lateral raise (current) · W20 cycle forward — incline DB + Kinesis fly refresh.
watchpoints: **Push press — run the FULL 2 min rest this week (the experiment).** W18 ~1 min helped the feel but set 3 still landed at 8. This is the one session to take the real 2 min and see if set 3 recovers the rep. The rest is the lever, not the load — hold 45 either way.

**Incline DB steps to 50 — as a set-1 test.** Run 50 on set 1 first (full rest); if it craters, 50/45/45. The pack-down cue is the stop sign — shrug-up-to-finish = too heavy for the cue, back to 45. Expect reps to reset to ~8-10 at 50 and rebuild toward 12; that's the cycle, not a regression.

**Bottoms-up press is now in the warmup** — 18lb, 8/side, forward press + T-press; rotator-cuff prep before pressing. Keep the T-plane lighter (abducted-and-loaded is the angle the right shoulder likes least); bail to forward-only if it talks.

**Light Kinesis-fly opener stays in the warmup** — a few easy, light tree-hugger reps to open the chest before pressing. Primes, doesn't fatigue. Working Kinesis fly is later, and the free progression there is to STEP FORWARD to deepen the stretch (W18 find) — not more load.
**Run push press first when the rack's free** — fresh shoulders for the heavy overhead lift.

**Mini-dip warmup stays on the dip station** — leaning on the bar, a few mini-dips warm the shoulder and 'crack' the same spot the protective shrug does (W18 self-discovery, the user's read on the shoulder/front-pec root cause). Do it before the working dips.
**Pack DOWN, not up** — push press, lateral raise, incline DB, dips, farmer carry all carry the cue. A lockout that needs a shrug = the load's too heavy for the cue.
**Cable block lists per-equipment numbers (column / rope pulley / Kinesis)** — pick what's free, log the equipment + number.

**Day is at capacity** — no adds. Anterior delt is already covered three ways (push press + incline + dips); if a front raise ever goes in, it's light + controlled in the warmup slot, never a 4th pressing station.
**Shoulder's been the best report in a while** ('more weakness than pain') — that's the taper working. Bank the headroom; don't load up to chase a feeling.

sets.name: Warmup + Shoulder Rehab (Non-Negotiable) + Bottoms-Up Cuff Prep + Chest Opener + Pull-Up Greasing + Protective Shrug

exercises.notes: Slow, big circles. Wake up scap glide before loading.
Full sequence with red band. Non-negotiable on push day.

**LOAD:** 18lb. Rotator-cuff prep before pressing — bell inverted/balanced over a vertical forearm, grip HARD, shoulder packed. **8/side in two planes:** forward press (straight overhead) + T-press (out toward a T at shoulder height). **Keep the T-plane lighter** — the abducted-and-loaded angle is the one the right shoulder likes least; bail to forward-only if it talks. Balance quality over rep count.

**Light loosening opener — NOT a working set** (the working fly comes later). On the Kinesis, light load: 'hug a tree' forward, then let the cables pull the arms open into the pec stretch. Primes the chest before pressing; quick and easy, it doesn't fatigue.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — dials a stretch up the back chain from forearm to shoulder. Wakes the grip and shoulder line before loading.
Ribs down, glutes tight, body in one line. Slow eccentric, 1s pause with chest 1-2" off the floor.

**Pull-up greasing set.** 1 fresh set, slow tempo, NOT to failure. Active hang start, pull elbows down to ribs, chest leads. Frequency, not max effort — drop to scapular-pulls only if the shoulder talks, and finish the count.

**Protective shrug (greasing set).** 1 light set, DBs held behind the body, palms back. Pack the shoulders DOWN and BACK, shrug UP and slightly back, 1s peak squeeze, slow down. The 'opposite movement' that decompresses the right shoulder — costs no time, easy to forget.

sets.name: 🔆 Push Press (Spotlight — 3 Sets at 45, Run First, FULL 2 Min Rest)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 45lb DBs per side. 3 sets of 8-10. Run first when the rack's open.

**REST: a FULL 2 minutes between sets.** This is the experiment this week — W18 you rested ~1 min and set 3 still hit 8 (not 10). Set 3 capping at 8 reads as under-rest, not a load ceiling — give the strength time to come back. Take the real 2 min and see if set 3 recovers the rep.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the explosive overhead lift, dialed:**
- **Ribs DOWN before the dip** — catch any rib flare on set 1
- **Shallow dip ~3-4"**, straight down through the heels — the drive comes from the legs, not the shoulders
- **Vertical DB path** — DBs travel up next to the ears, head pokes through at the top
- **Pack DOWN, not up** at the lockout — if it needs a shrug, the load's too heavy for the cue
- **Hybrid tempo:** explosive drive up, controlled descent

**Reflection:** with the full 2 min rest, does set 3 come back to 10 — or does it still land at 8? If 10, the rest was the fix. If still 8, that's the honest set-3 number at 45 right now, and that's fine — there's a rep there to win over time, no need to load up.

**LOAD:** 15lb DBs. 3 sets of 15-18.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the medial-delt isolation, drilled:**
- **Targets the medial (side) deltoid** — the slow eccentric maxes time-under-tension on a small muscle, which is why the last set stays hard even at 15
- **Lead with the elbow, hand passive** — the wrist follows the elbow, the hand never lifts first
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED** through the whole rep
- **Stop at shoulder height — never higher** (higher just shrugs the traps off the medial delt)
- **2s eccentric** — the slow descent is the stimulus
- **Scap reset between sets** — roll the shoulders, engage/disengage the scapula a few times; this is what's kept the right shoulder quiet here

**Reflection:** does the work stay in the side delt with the traps quiet, or do the shoulders start shrugging up to finish the set? If the traps take over, that's the end of the clean set — bank quality reps, the floor's already risen here ('wasn't too bad' at 15).

sets.name: Incline DB Press (Test 50 on Set 1 — 50/45/45 Fallback, FULL 2 Min Rest)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD — step to 50, tested:** run **50 pair on set 1** (freshest, full rest). If set 1 is clean, ride 50 for all 3 sets; if it craters, fall back to **50/45/45** (top set 50, the other two at 45). Fast-up / controlled-down, 1s pause at the bottom.

**REST: a FULL ~2 min between sets** — fuller rest keeps each set quality.

**The pack-down cue is the stop sign, not the number** — if you have to shrug UP to finish a rep at 50, it's too heavy *for the cue*; back to 45. The front delt is loaded here and the right shoulder's still 'weakness not pain,' so the cue wins over the number.

**Reps reset at 50 — expect ~8-10, not 12.** That's the strength end of the range; rebuild the reps toward 12 over the next weeks, then nudge again. Not a regression.
- **Bench at 30°**, not 45° — steeper biases front delt over upper chest
- **Shoulders packed back AND down** — pin the back of the shoulder into the bench, hold it the whole set
- **Forearm stacked vertically over the elbow at the bottom** — keeps the load off the front of the shoulder
- **Elbows ~45° from torso**, not flared to 90°
- **1s pause at the bottom**, press to a fingerwidth apart at the top.

sets.name: Kinesis Cable Fly (3 Sets — Step Forward to Deepen)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** Kinesis 9. **Free progression: STEP FORWARD** to deepen the stretch and make it harder (W18 find) — that's the ROM-as-progression lever, not more load.

- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED throughout** — these are NOT presses; the elbow angle never changes
- **'Hug a tree'** — the squeeze comes from the chest, not the arms pulling together
- **Stop a fistwidth apart at the top** — don't crash the handles
- **Slow eccentric (~3s)** — let the cables pull the arms into the deep pec stretch; the right shoulder/pec reads this loaded stretch as relief, protect that.

- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the rope pull the hands behind the head
- **Stop just shy of lockout**, slow eccentric. Set 1 feels easy, set 3 is brutal — that start-easy/end-hard shape is the lift working, not a load problem.

**LOAD (pick what's free, log which):**

- **Rope pulley: 50**
- **Kinesis: 6**

3 rounds.

- **Slight elbow bend (~5°), FIXED throughout**
- **Pull the bar to the thighs, NOT past** — past = shoulders roll forward, lats switch off (and the front pec gets pulled in; keep it short)

sets.name: Farmer Carry (3 Walks)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 50lb DBs. 3 walks of ~45-60s each — chase hold-time.

- **Grip firm but NOT death-clenched** — grip is the limiter here (it taps before the shoulder); set the bells down when grip fails rather than white-knuckling. No straps — train the grip.
- **Walk a straight line at a deliberate pace**, breathing steadily.

sets.notes: Trap-chain + grip block. 3 walks at 50lb — packed-shoulder posture, grip as the honest edge. Set them down when grip gives, not before.

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow position. Pec minor lengthen — the antagonist to the upper-trap chain loaded all session.
Passive hang from the pull-up bar. **Don't engage** — let the shoulders unpack and the spine decompress.
30s each side on the mat. Draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
45s each side. Front leg + back leg at 90°. Sink the hips toward the floor — hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Knees wide, arms extended forward. Parasympathetic shift before leaving the gym.

sets.notes: 5 minutes of recovery work, non-negotiable closing block.

tips: **Push press spotlight — run the FULL 2 min rest this week.** W18 ~1 min helped the feel but set 3 still hit 8. Take the real 2 min and see if set 3 recovers to 10. Hold 45 either way.
**Incline DB steps to 50 — set-1 test.** Ride 50 if set 1's clean, else 50/45/45. Pack-down is the stop sign; reps reset to ~8-10 and rebuild.
**Bottoms-up press is now in the warmup** — 18lb, 8/side, forward + T-plane, T-plane light. Rotator-cuff prep before pressing.
**Lateral raise spotlight** — lead with the elbow, stop at shoulder height, 2s eccentric, scap reset between sets. 15lb holds; it's become 'not too bad' (floor rising).
**Mini-dip warmup stays on the dip station** — warms the shoulder and 'cracks' the same spot the protective shrug does (your root-cause read).
**Kinesis fly — step forward to deepen the stretch** (free ROM progression, not more load).
**Run push press first when the rack's free** — fresh shoulders.
**Pack DOWN, not up** — every press + the carry carries the cue.
**Cable block per-equipment numbers** — column 30/70/120; rope pulley 10/35/50; Kinesis 5-6. Pick what's free, log it.
**Farmer carry: 50lb, chase hold-time** — grip is the edge, no straps; the tall packed posture relieves the right shoulder.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, permanent every gym day.**
**Day is at capacity** — no adds. Rest: 2 min push press + dips + incline, 90s lateral raise + Kinesis fly + farmer carry, 75s cable block.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state push week — the gains come from rest discipline and sharper execution at established loads, not heavier bells. The push-press spotlight makes the rest the experiment: run a true 2 min and settle the half-confirmed W18 question of whether the set-3 cap is under-rest or the honest number. The lateral raise spotlight drills the medial-delt isolation that's quietly become easier. The bottoms-up press joins the warmup as rotator-cuff prep, and the mini-dip warmup stays — both feed the same already-improving shoulder ('weakness, not pain' now). Building decades, not weeks.

**Strict overhead press 50 across, chase reps toward 8** — strict, no push-press; W19 was 50 × 5/6/7 'felt easy.' Pull it, don't force it.
**Front squat 25-35lb** — racked, sit tall, full depth. Leg-athletic Tuesday is fine, far from Friday legs.
**Bottoms-up press standard in the warmup** — 18lb, 8/side, forward + T-plane (T-plane light). Also primes the bottoms-up rack for the spotlight.
**Heavy figure-8 @50 fits here** if you want the fun-layer — Tuesday's the right day for the heavy one.
**Protective behind-back shrug greasing set in the warm-up.**
Cooldown mandatory — pigeon + butterfly.
Rotation plan: W21 bring the Leggy Flow or a windmill/TGU complex back; fold bottoms-up carry in. Trim the figure-8 complex to 3 rounds if short on time.
formPhilosophy: KB Tuesday as the carousel, working as designed: the figure-8 → tactical clean complex returns (a W12-W14 favorite, off the menu since the Leggy weeks), the bottoms-up clean comes off the rotation pool into loaded practice as the spotlight, and the front squat covers the squat pattern — variety is cheap on KB days, so rotate freely while keeping the strict-press strength anchor and the shoulder scaffolding (bottoms-up prep, banded prep, protective shrug). The skill flow + front squat are leg-athletic, which is exactly why they sit on Tuesday, three days clear of Friday legs. Building decades, not weeks.

name: Week 20 Legs — Steady State, Station-Grouped (Spotlight: Leg Press + Bulgarian)
description: Volume steady, station-grouped. **Warmup reminder:** bodyweight squat (depth check) → cross-leg lateral lean (QL/psoas) → hip circles → tibialis raise → cat-cow → internal core fist rotation → dead-bug core/QL primer → bodyweight lunge (QL check). Spotlights cycle forward to the leg press (deep-ROM refresh — it 'felt super open' W19 with the QL fresh) and the Bulgarian (stepped to double-50 DBs). The squat keeps the 45→70→80 ramp with the catcher bars set at your max-depth reference (W19: catcher at 14 = full bodyweight depth) — 80 held, depth the lever. Leg curl runs an explicit pyramid to a tested top (the W19 accidental 100 looked real on ~1 min rest). New this week: each lift is tagged 🔥 (near-failure/pyramid OK) or 🛑 (the cue/depth is the cap).

dayOverview.theme: Steady state, station-grouped. Spotlights cycle to the leg press (deep-ROM refresh — 'felt super open' W19) + the Bulgarian (double-50 DBs now). Squat keeps the 45→70→80 ramp + the catcher-14 max-depth reference; 80 held, depth the lever. Leg curl pyramids to a tested top (the W19 accidental 100 looked real). Dead-bug core primer stays in the warmup. Leg curl stays before incline RDL so the hamstring work doesn't stack.

spotlights.why: Cycles forward — W19 it 'felt super open' at 4 plates, a total contrast to W18's 'sweating like a wet dog' (the difference was a fresh, non-pre-fatigued QL). Spotlight drills the deep knees-to-chest ROM (the deep position trains the core/QL as much as the quads). The progression here is DEPTH + a near-failure last set at 4 plates — NOT more plates, because heavier plates shorten the deep ROM that's the whole point.

Cycles forward — W19 you stepped the DBs to double-50 ('feels fine, hard at end,' QL quiet). Spotlight drills the vertical-front-shin split stance + the drive through the front heel so double-50 stays clean and the QL stays quiet. Pigeon on the bench between sets (your W18 keeper) stays.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W18 leg-press ROM + Bulgarian · W19 squat depth + leg curl · W20 leg press + Bulgarian (current) · W21 cycle forward — squat depth + calf / incline RDL refresh.
watchpoints: **🔥/🛑 intensity tags — decide before the set.** 🔥 near-failure / pyramid OK (safe machine/isolation): leg press (near-failure last set at 4 plates — depth is the load lever, not plates), calf raise, leg curl (pyramid the load to a tested top). 🛑 keep it shy, the cue/depth is the cap: squat (never grind a loaded squat — 'I'll fall on my face'), Bulgarian (QL/knee — form is the cap), incline RDL (hinge/lumbar — tempo is the lever). **Order:** form lever first (tempo/ROM), load second, near-failure/pyramid only on 🔥.

**Leg press spotlight — DEPTH is the lever, not plates.** Hold 4 plates; the deep knees-to-chest ROM is the work (it trains the core/QL). 🔥 It's a safe machine, so a near-failure LAST set at 4 plates is fair game if it feels open — but don't add plates to chase it, because heavier plates shorten the deep ROM and miss the point.

**Bulgarian spotlight — double-50 DBs (Smith @45 the QL-safe alternate).** W19 double-50 'feels fine, hard at end.' 🛑 form is the cap: front shin vertical, drive through the front heel, rear knee nearly to the floor. Pigeon on the bench between sets. If anything twitches, drop to bodyweight and finish.

**Leg curl pyramids to a tested top — the W19 100 looked real.** Run 70 primer → 80 → 90 → 100, judging the top by the FEEL (heels driving, no torso lift, slow eccentric), on NORMAL rest (the W19 100 was ~1 min rest = normal isolation rest, so it's a legit signal, not rest-flattered). 🔥 If 100 keeps the correct feel, it's yours; if it drifts, that's the honest top. Settings 5/m/0/-1 (verify before loading).

**Squat keeps the 45→70→80 ramp + the catcher-14 reference.** Set the catcher bars at your max bodyweight-bar depth (W19: 14) as a depth target + safety. 80 held — W19 was 'the most solid i ever felt, really stable' but not full depth; depth is the next unlock. 🛑 depth is the lever, never grind a loaded squat to failure. Stop adding working sets when the depth shortens.
**Dead-bug core/QL primer stays in the warmup.** W19 the leg press normalized with the QL fresh; keep waking the deep core before the leg press.
**Incline RDL holds 45, dead slow.** W19 did all 3 clean ('hard as always when done slowly'). 🛑 tempo (3s eccentric, 2s pause) is the lever, not the load.
**Station-grouped sequence:** warmup → squat → leg press → leg-press-calf-raise (SAME machine, stay there) → Bulgarian (bench station) → leg curl → incline RDL → cool-down. No backtracking.
**Keep leg curl BEFORE incline RDL** — reversed, the two hamstring lifts stack and smoke the second.

**QL/psoas watch** — cross-leg lateral lean in the warmup AND cool-down. QL's been clear (W19 legs 'felt easy,' no spasm). If anything talks in the warmup, modify the day; mid-session, drop a set + take stretch breaks.

sets.name: Warmup (incl. Cross-Leg Lateral Lean — QL/Psoas Release + Dead-Bug Core/QL Primer)

exercises.notes: Full depth, slow. Find where the hips are tight and breathe into it. Depth check before loading.

30s each side. Scissor one foot over the other, reach the same-side arm overhead, lean away from the back leg — the stretch runs down the side of the waist into the QL and lateral hip. Do this before loading the squat.
Big slow circles. Wake up the hip stabilizers.

Back to a wall, heels a step out, weight on the heels. Pull the toes UP toward the shins as high as they'll go, lower slow. Preps ankle dorsiflexion for squat depth + shin insurance for the run-in. ~30s, bodyweight.
Spine mobility — slow, full ROM each direction.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension. Quick posterior-chain + low-back opener before loading the squat.

**Core/QL primer.** On your back, arms up, knees over hips. Press the lower back FLAT into the floor and HOLD it there as you slowly extend the opposite arm + leg, then switch. The brace is the work — wakes the deep core before the leg press (W19: the leg press felt open with the QL primed + fresh).
Bodyweight. QL check — if anything talks here, modify the day. Also previews the Bulgarian pattern.

**The bottom half of the 45→70→80 ramp — set the catcher bars at your max-depth reference first (W19: 14 = full bodyweight-bar depth), as a depth target + safety.**
- **Set 1: 45/side x8** — drill max depth: sit all the way into the bottom, tap the catcher if you can, controlled reps, no bounce. W19 the 45 was deep, no 'hanging' moment.
- **Set 2: 70/side x8** — the intermediary ROM-builder. Same depth as the working sets, heavier so the bottom's honest. W19 the 70 was 'much deeper with more rest' but still a mid-range 'hanging moment' — breathe through it.
- **🛑 Move fast through these submaximal ramp sets** (short rest) — save the full rest for the 80 working sets.

**LOAD:** 80/side. Working sets off the ramp — run 80 for as many sets as the depth holds (W19 was 80x8 x2, 'the most solid i ever felt, really stable' but not full depth). **Depth is the lever, not reps or load.**
- Bar high on the upper traps, upper-back shelf squeezed
- **Brace like prepping for a punch** — deep belly breath at the top, HOLD through the descent, exhale on the drive up
- **Hips back AND down**, 'spread the floor' — screw the feet in, knees track over the toes
- **Sit into the bottom** — keep chasing depth toward the catcher; you find depth easier under load
- **Take the FULL rest here (2-3 min)** — W19 the deeper/more-solid sets came with more rest
- **🛑 Never grind a loaded squat to failure** — stop adding working sets when the depth shortens; a shallow grind isn't the work. Bank the deep, stable ones.

**Reflection:** does 80 hold the W19 stability AND start reaching closer to the catcher this week? Stability was last week's win; depth is the next. Deep + stable at 80 is the goal — if depth caps, that's the honest end.

sets.name: 🔆 Leg Press + Calf Raise Station (Same Machine — Leg Press Spotlight, Deep ROM) 🔥

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 4 plates/side. 4 sets of 12.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — depth is the load lever, not plates:**
- **Full ROM — knees toward the chest.** The deep position trains the abs/QL/core as much as the quads — that's the intent
- **Foot position:** shoulder-width, mid-foot on the platform, slight toe-out
- **It feels harder cold** — the deep ROM opens once the hips are warm (W19 'felt super open'); don't judge the load on set 1
- **Actively press to keep the lower back from lifting off the pad** at the bottom; if the hips roll off, back off a hair
- **Press through the WHOLE foot; slow descent (3s), no bounce at the bottom**; don't lock out hard at the top
- **🔥 A near-failure LAST set at 4 plates is fair game** if it feels open — but DON'T add plates to chase it. Heavier plates shorten the deep ROM, and the deep ROM is the whole point. Depth first, then a hard last set at the SAME load.

**Reflection:** does the deep knees-to-chest ROM hold on all 4 sets (W19 'felt super open'), and does a near-failure last set stay deep — or does chasing the last few reps shorten the ROM? Deep-and-hard beats shallow-and-heavy.

**LOAD:** 4 plates/side. 3 sets of 15. Stay on the leg press — same machine, no walking off. 🔥
- **Balls of both feet on the BOTTOM EDGE of the platform, heels hanging off**
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the heels drop as far below the edge as they'll go
- **Drive to FULL plantarflexion at the top**
- **Tempo by feel** — own the stretch at the bottom and the squeeze at the top, no bouncing. 🔥 A hard last set is fine — it's a safe isolation. (3 sets, after the 4 leg-press sets — same station.)

sets.name: 🔆 Bulgarian Split Squat (Spotlight — Double-50 DBs; Smith @45 the Alternate; Pigeon Between Sets) 🛑

exercises.equipment: bench + DBs (regular default, double-50) — Smith machine if free (use smith-machine-bulgarian-split-squat)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** two 50lb DBs, one per hand (stepped up W19 — 'feels fine, hard at end'). 3 sets of 8-10 each leg. **Regular DB version is the default; the Smith machine @45 is the QL-safe alternate when it's free.**

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — clean double-50, QL quiet:**
- **Rear foot up on the bench** behind you, laces down or toes tucked
- **Step out far enough that the front shin stays roughly VERTICAL at the bottom** — too short a stance = the knee crashes past the toes
- **Front knee tracks over the front foot** — not caving in
- **Lower until the rear knee nearly touches the floor** — controlled, no dropping
- **Drive up through the FRONT HEEL** — the front leg does the work, the rear leg is a kickstand
- **Torso TALL** — a slight forward lean is fine, no folding over; 2s descent, own the bottom
- **Pigeon on the bench between sets** — your W18 keeper, keeps the hip/QL loose under the load
- **🛑 Form is the cap — don't grind double-50 to failure.** At double-50 this is real load; if the QL/knee twitches, drop to bodyweight for the remaining sets and finish.

**Reflection:** does the front shin stay vertical and the drive stay in the front heel at double-50, or does the torso fold / the knee crash forward to move the weight? Clean double-50 is the win; a folding rep is the honest cap.

sets.name: Seated Leg Curl (Pyramid to a Tested Top — 5/m/0/-1, Before Incline RDL) 🔥

exercises.notes:
**LOAD — pyramid to a tested top:** 70 primer → 80 → 90 → 100. Slow tempo. **Settings: 5/m/0/-1** (verify before loading).

**🔥 The pyramid, judged by FEEL not the number:**
- **First set at 70 to groove the pattern** — 'primes my brain to do it correctly' (it'll feel easy; that's the point)
- **Then climb 80 → 90 → 100**, testing the top on NORMAL rest (~60-90s — the W19 accidental 100 was on ~1 min rest, which IS normal isolation rest, so it's a legit signal, not rest-flattered)
- **Ankles UNDER the pad** — the ankle bone is the contact point, NOT the mid-calf
- **Lap pad locked DOWN firmly** — a loose pad lets the torso lift and turns it into lower-back work
- **Curl the heels toward the glutes** — full ROM, full squeeze; **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze** — the slow eccentric is the whole stimulus
- **🔥 Judge the top by the correct FEEL** — heels driving, hamstring doing the work, torso anchored (no lifting forward). If 100 keeps that feel, it's yours; if it starts drifting (torso lifts, momentum creeps in), that's the honest top — drop back. The feel is the cap, not the stack.

**Reflection:** does 100 keep the 'correct' feel on normal rest, or does it drift into torso-lift and momentum? Correct feel at the top = the real number. This is a safe isolation — pyramiding up is exactly right here.

**LOAD:** 45lb plate. 3 sets of 15, dead slow with a 2s pause at the bottom (W19 did all 3 clean — 'hard as always when done slowly'). 🛑
- **Pad just below the hip crease** — NOT on the upper thigh, NOT on the stomach
- **Hip hinge** — a Romanian deadlift on the 45° bench, NOT a lumbar extension. Lower back NEUTRAL throughout
- **At the bottom:** the stretch is in the **hamstrings and glutes**, NOT the lower back. If the lumbar rounds, you're going too deep for current mobility
- **Drive up by squeezing the glutes and hamstrings**; at the top, stop at neutral — past neutral = lumbar load = QL irritation
- **Tempo: 3s eccentric, 2s pause at the bottom, 1s drive up.** 🛑 The slow eccentric is the entire lever — hold the 45lb plate, keep slowing the tempo; don't chase load or grind to failure on a hinge.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Recovery Block (Hip/QL-Biased for Legs Day)

exercises.notes: 30s each side. Scissor the legs, reach overhead, lean away from the back leg — bookend the session with the same QL/psoas release as the warmup.

45s each side. Hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Knees wide, arms extended forward. Parasympathetic shift.

sets.notes: 5-min recovery block, hip/QL-biased on legs day.

**Squat keeps the 45→70→80 ramp + the catcher-14 max-depth reference.** 80 held; depth is the next unlock after last week's stability win. 🛑
**Dead-bug core/QL primer stays in the warmup** — wakes the deep core before the leg press.
**Incline RDL holds 45, dead slow** — tempo (3s down, 2s pause) is the lever. 🛑
**Station-grouped:** warmup → squat → leg press → leg-press-calf-raise (same machine — stay there) → Bulgarian → leg curl → incline RDL → cool-down. No backtracking.
**Leg curl BEFORE incline RDL** — don't reverse them, or the hamstring work stacks.

name: W20 Morning Flow — Bodyweight Spine + Hip (All Days, Rotated Variety)

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — the wrist dials a stretch up the back chain. Stays in the primer.

exercises.notes: **Greasing set — 1 quick set, NEVER to failure.** Daily frequency is the point (the floor rises over time). 30s each side. Anti-rotation — opposite arm + leg extend, hold a beat, hips stay square (no swinging).

Rotates in for W20 — from a plank, tap the opposite shoulder with one hand while keeping the hips DEAD STILL (no rocking). Anti-rotation core + shoulder stability — the stillness is the work.

sets.notes: Opens with a pushup greasing set (1 quick set, never to failure — daily habit). Spiderman plank + plank shoulder taps rotate in for W20; glute bridge + bird-dog (anti-rotation) stay.

30s each side. Hip flexor + adductor + back-leg quad. Drop to elbows if accessible. Stays — durable hip opener.
Bodyweight, slow. Stays every week — keeps the loaded cossack pattern grooved.

Stays — sit in a wide straddle, reach toward one foot, then center (chest toward the floor), then the other foot. Slow, breathe into each reach. The straddle + adductor + hamstring opener the flow design calls for.

sets.name: 📍 Day-Specific Add-On — Pick by Today's Training (~3-5 min)

exercises.notes: **📍 PUSH DAYS — KEY PROTOCOL MOVE.** 30s each at LOW / MID / HIGH elbow positions. Arm bent 90°, forearm on the door frame, step through and rotate the torso AWAY. Desk work continuously re-tightens pec minor — daily.
**📍 PUSH DAYS** — active side of the pec-minor fix. Lower trap + rotator cuff.
**📍 PUSH DAYS** — serratus activation, helps unstick a tight pec minor.

**📍 PUSH DAYS (optional)** — pins the shoulder blades in the corrected position.

**📍 LEGS DAYS — QL-SPASM PROTOCOL.** 90s each side. Long hold lets the QL/psoas release. Non-negotiable on legs day.
**📍 LEGS DAYS** — 60s each side. Gentle twist for the QL. Lacrosse-ball QL roll above the iliac crest beforehand if available.

sets.notes: **Pick today's day-specific protocol — push / pull / legs.** ~3-5 min total. KB days (Tue/Thu) skip this block — the in-workout banded prep covers the equivalent.

**15 min main flow + 3-5 min day-specific add-on** — universal across W20 (Mon push / Tue KB / Wed pull / Thu KB / Fri legs).
**Scorpion + cossack BW + lizard pose + straddle reaches stay every week** — durable anchors.
