W20 rotates ~half: a thread-the-needle thoracic primer, fresh anti-rotation core work (spiderman plank, plank shoulder taps), and the W12-era puppy pose + happy baby cycled back so the flow doesn't calcify; the rehab anchors and the day-specific PPL protocols stay. Building decades, not weeks.

name: Week 20 Pull — Steady State (Spotlight: High Cable Curl + Cable Crunch)
description: Volume steady; the protective behind-back shrug stays front-loaded as activation. **Warmup reminder:** behind-back shrug FIRST (protective activation, 3 sets) → band-pull-apart → cat-cow → internal core fist rotation → active dead hang. Spotlights cycle forward to the high cable curl (the single-pulley reads 62.5 and it's brutal — a different scale than the cable-column 180) and the cable crunch (read the stack — magnetic add-ons hide). Lat pulldown holds 150 (W19 didn't clean up — keep drilling the controlled return, don't step up); face pull holds the settled 50; chest-supported row holds 45 with a slower eccentric; DB row holds the 70/80/90 bare-hand pyramid. Pull-up stays on the straight bar. New this week: each lift is tagged 🔥 (near-failure last set OK) or 🛑 (grip/form is the cap) so you decide before the set.

dayOverview.theme: Steady state. Shrug stays FIRST (protective activation). Spotlights cycle to the high cable curl (single-pulley 62.5, the NEW scale) + the cable crunch (read the stack). Lat pulldown holds 150 (didn't clean up W19 — drill the return, don't step up); face pull holds the settled 50. DB row holds 70/80/90, no straps. Both shoulders pain-free — grip is the cap, not the shoulder.

spotlights.why: Cycles forward — W19 the single-pulley station read 62.5 and was brutal ('barely finished set 2 but did all'), a different, harder scale than the cable-column 180 est. Spotlight drills the fixed upper-arm (parallel to the floor) high-cable variant so the number gets honest on the scale you actually used — and it's a safe isolation, so this is a lift where a near-failure last set (or a clean pyramid up) is fair game.

Cycles forward — W19 you read the stack correctly (67.5, not 66.5 — the magnetic-add-on lesson landed) and it was 'super hard at the end.' Spotlight drills the hips-LOCKED, abs-only crunch so the load is honest ab work, not a hip-flexor pull — a safe core isolation where the last set can ride close to failure.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W18 pull-up + DB row · W19 lat pulldown + face pull · W20 high cable curl + cable crunch (current) · W21 cycle forward — chest-supported row + incline curl refresh.
watchpoints: **🔥/🛑 intensity tags — decide before the set.** 🔥 near-failure last set OK (safe isolation / supported): chest-supported row, incline curl, reverse fly, face pull, high cable curl, cable crunch. 🛑 keep it shy, grip/form is the cap: pull-up, DB row, lat pulldown (grip fails first — failure just means the hands quit, not that the back got worked; no straps). **Order:** form lever first (tempo/ROM), load second, near-failure last set only on 🔥 — by pushing the existing last set, not adding a round.

**High cable curl spotlight — the single-pulley reads 62.5 (the harder scale).** W19 62.5 was brutal on the single pulley; the cable column runs ~180. Log which station + number. 🔥 — a near-failure last set or a clean pyramid up is fair game here (isolation); if 62.5 keeps the correct feel, let it climb.

**Cable crunch spotlight — hips LOCKED, read the stack.** 62.5 clean base / 66.5 comfortable / 70.5 brutal ceiling — and the magnetic micro add-ons can be on unnoticed (W19: a '67.5' read). Read the actual stack. 🔥 — the last set can ride close to failure as long as the hips stay locked (hips moving = hip-flexor work, that's the real cap).
**Behind-back shrug stays FIRST (activation slot).** Front-loading it keeps pull day flare-free — the protective counter to all the pulling can't be the piece a rushed session drops.

**Lat pulldown holds 150 — 🛑 don't step up.** W19 was 12/12/10-with-form-lost — the same honest ceiling as W18, 150 hasn't cleaned up yet. Drill the wide-grip pull + the slow controlled return; the reps tidy over more weeks. Grip's the end limiter, no straps.
**Face pull holds the settled 50.** W19 'felt good, did all sets' — the knuckles-up / elbows-above-the-shoulders cue is holding. 🔥 quality over number; keep the elbows high.

**Chest-supported row holds 45 — cue the slower eccentric.** W19 'could go slower, good working weight' — so the progression this week is a slower 2-3s eccentric at 45, not a load step. 🔥 supported and safe.

**Pull-up stays on the STRAIGHT BAR.** The swivel grip rotates to the bicep and pulls work off the lats. 🛑 grip was the limiter W19 (6/6/8/6, 'grip not holding') — frequency over max, bank clean reps, no straps.

**DB row holds 70/80/90, no straps.** W19 the right hand topped ~99 with grip to spare, left tapped first — let the strong-side top set creep as grip allows; 🛑 set the DB down when grip gives, not when the back fails.
**Left bicep first, every set** — the left still struggles to hit 9-10 on the last incline-curl sets. Keep the protocol as insurance.
**Cable lifts have per-equipment numbers** — pick what's free, log equipment + number.

exercises.notes: Scap activation. Squeeze the shoulder blades together, soft elbow.
Spine warm — slow, full ROM each direction.
Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — primes grip and the pulling chain before bar work.
Active hang, not collapsed — engage the lats, pull the shoulders DOWN away from the ears even at full extension. Primes the pull-ups.

sets.name: Behind-Back DB Shrug — Protective Activation (DO THIS FIRST)

exercises.equipment: DB pair, held behind the body
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40-50lb pair. 3 sets — first in the session.

**Why here, first:** the 'opposite movement' to all the pulling — a counter/decompression for the right shoulder. Front-loading it keeps pull day flare-free. Reads more like a stretch than a lift; that's the point.
- **DBs held BEHIND the body** at the sides of the hips/glutes — palms facing back
- **Shoulders pull DOWN and BACK** at the start — packed, not relaxed
- **Shrug UP and slightly BACK** — pinch the shoulder blades at the top
- **Hold 1s at the top**, slow descent; **pack DOWN, NOT up** as the resting position — the lower position IS the work
- Chest open, not slouched.

sets.notes: Protective trap-chain activation, front of the session. ~4 min. Light-to-moderate, peak-squeeze — a decompression, not a max effort.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** Bodyweight. 4 sets of 6-8 (W19 was 6/6/8/6 on the straight bar with slow eccentrics — grip was the limiter, not the shoulder).

**Straight bar** — the swivel grip rotates toward the bicep mid-pull and pulls work off the lats. Straight bar keeps the work in the back.
- **Active hang start**, shoulders pulled down out of the ears — NOT a collapsed dead hang
- **Pull elbows DOWN to ribs**, NOT chin to bar — 'drive the elbows into the back pockets'
- **Chest leads to the bar at the top**, eyes ahead, head neutral
- **Slow eccentric ~2-3s**, active hang at the bottom of every rep — no dropping, no kip
- **🛑 Stop the set when the rep stops being clean** — grip + honest strength are the limiter now (both shoulders pain-free, 'only regular weakness'), so bank 6 clean over 8 sloppy. Frequency over max effort; no straps.

sets.name: DB Rack / Bench Block — DB Row 🛑 + Chest-Supported Row 🔥 + Incline Curl 🔥 + Reverse Fly 🔥 (3 Rounds)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 70/80/90 ascending pyramid — one set per round (70, then 80, then 90). No straps. 🛑
- **Chest-supported on the incline bench** — chest glued to the pad, no twisting up for the last reps
- **Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit** — keeps it in the lats
- **Slow 2s descent, 1s squeeze on the 70 and 80** — those hold clean form
- **On the 90 set, let the strong side creep** — W19 the right hand topped ~99 with grip to spare; drive the elbow, chase clean reps before form breaks
- **🛑 Grip is the limiter** (left hand taps first) — set the DB down when grip gives, not when the back fails. No straps — train the grip.

**LOAD:** 45 (dialed W19 — 'could go slower, good working weight'). 3 sets of 10-12. 🔥
- **The progression this week is a SLOWER eccentric at 45** — 2-3s down, not a load step (your own W19 cue)
- **Chest stays GLUED to the incline bench** — if the chest peels off to heave the DBs, the weight's ahead of the form
- **Pull the elbow toward the HIP, not the armpit**; don't rotate the torso
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the shoulder blade protract, then re-pull from the stretch
- **🔥 Safe supported row — the last set can ride close to failure at 45** (push the set you have).

**LOAD:** incline bench 25lb DBs (default) — or the actual preacher bench (EZ bar ~2×10) when it's free. 3 sets of 8-10. 🔥
- **Incline bench ~45°, lean in chest-first** — the upper arm stays flat on the pad the ENTIRE rep (don't lift the elbow)
- **Left arm first, every set** — the left still struggles on the last two sets (W19 'left arm crazy weak'), so keep the left-first protocol as insurance
- **Full stretch at the bottom — pause 2s**; curl smoothly to the peak squeeze, no swing; 2-3s eccentric
- **🔥 Isolation — a near-failure last set is fine** (mind the left keeping up).

**LOAD:** 20lb. 3 sets of 12 — cap at 12 with a slower eccentric rather than chasing reps ('so so hard today' W19, back was sore). 🔥
- **30° reverse-incline** (chest-down on the incline bench), DBs hanging fully extended at the start
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED throughout** — a sweep, NOT a row
- **Lead with the elbow, hand passive**; wings out and slightly UP to shoulder height — sweep wide, don't shrug
- **Hold the top a beat, then 2s eccentric** — rear-delt / mid-trap shoulder-health work; 🔥 quality over the number.

sets.notes: One trip to the DB rack covers all 4 lifts. Incline bench at ~30° for the rows + reverse fly (30° reverse-incline), set to ~45° for the incline curl. 3 rounds.

sets.name: Lat Pulldown (3 Sets at 150 — Drill the Return, Don't Step Up) 🛑

exercises.notes:
**LOAD (pick whichever station's free, log which + the number):** Regular machine **150** (the working number, back-left) · dual pulley **70** · cable column **52.5-57.5** · cable pulley **47.5**. 3 sets.
- **Hold 150 — don't step up** (W19 was 12/12/10-with-form-lost, same as W18; 150 hasn't cleaned up yet). The reps tidy as it settles.
- **Wide grip near the bend** — more lat isolation, less bicep
- **Slight backward lean ~15°, NO further** — more = it becomes a row
- **Pull the bar to the UPPER CHEST — NEVER behind the neck**; 'lats squeezing oranges into the back pockets'
- **1s pause at the contraction, 2s controlled return** — the slow return is the thing to drill; that's where 150 cleans up
- **🛑 Grip is the end limiter, and set 3 breaking around 10 is the honest cap** — bank clean reps over ugly ones, no straps, don't grind.

sets.name: Cable Column — Face Pull (3 Sets at the Settled 50) 🔥

exercises.equipment: cable column (mid/upper-chest height + rope)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** cable column **50** (settled W19 — 'felt good at this weight, did all sets'). 🔥
- **Grip the rope ends in fists, knuckles up** — the change that made 50 feel right
- **Pull the rope to face level** — not to the chest
- **ELBOWS HIGH (above the shoulders)** — the make-or-break cue; this moves the work into the back
- **External-rotate at the top** — knuckles point UP, like the top of a double-biceps pose
- **1s peak hold, slow 2s return** — let the cable pull the arms back, don't drop
- **🔥 Rear-delt safe — the last set can ride close to failure** as long as the elbows stay high; if they drop, that's the honest end, re-set them or stop.

sets.name: 🔆 Cable Column Finisher — High Cable Curl (Spotlight) + Cable Crunch (Spotlight) 🔥

exercises.equipment: cable column or single pulley (low pulley, single D-handle, one arm at a time)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD (single arm — scales differ, LOG which station):**
- **Single pulley: 62.5** — the NEW scale from W19, and it's brutal ('barely finished set 2 but did all')
- **Cable column (single D-handle): ~180**
2-3 working sets per arm.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the fixed upper-arm high-cable curl:**
- **Stand sideways, arm out at shoulder level, upper arm PARALLEL to the floor and FIXED** — the whole point of the high-cable variant; the elbow doesn't drop
- **Curl the hand toward the ear**, peak squeeze
- **Left arm first**; slow eccentric, no bounce at the start
- **🔥 Safe isolation — a near-failure last set is fair game, and a clean pyramid up on the single pulley is fine** if 62.5 keeps the correct feel (fixed upper arm, no swing). Judge by the feel, not the number — the single-pulley scale is different from the column.

**Reflection:** does the upper arm stay pinned parallel through the whole set, or does the elbow drop to help? Fixed upper arm = the isolation's honest. If 62.5 holds the feel on a normal-rested set, it's real.

**LOAD (pick whichever station's free, log which — AND read the actual stack):** Cable pulley (rope) **62.5** clean base · **66.5** comfortable at x15 · **70.5** brutal ceiling. **Watch the magnetic micro add-ons** — they can be on without you noticing (W19: a '67.5' read). Read the stack before you start. 3 sets.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — abs only, hips locked:**
- **HIPS LOCKED** — the most important cue; the hips do not move. Hips moving = hip-flexor work, not abs
- **Crunch from the abs ONLY** — the spine flexes, the hips stay put
- **Chest toward the thighs**, hold the crunch 1 second
- **Slow eccentric, all the way** — at 62.5-67.5 the controlled drop IS available; use it
- **🔥 Core isolation — the last set can ride close to failure**, but the hips locking is the real cap: if the hips start yanking to move more weight, that's the end, not a rep to grind.

**Reflection:** do the hips stay dead-still for all three sets, or do they start pulling in to move the stack? Hips locked = honest ab work. That's the cap, not the number on the stack.

sets.notes: Same cable column / single-pulley station. Both spotlights here — the high cable curl (log which scale) and the cable crunch (read the stack). 3 sets each.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow position. Pec minor lengthen.
Passive hang. Don't engage — let the shoulders unpack and the spine decompress.
30s each side. Draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
45s each side. Hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Parasympathetic shift.

sets.notes: 5 minutes of recovery work, non-negotiable closing block.

tips: **🔥/🛑 intensity tags this week.** 🔥 (near-failure last set OK): chest-supported row, incline curl, reverse fly, face pull, high cable curl, cable crunch. 🛑 (grip/form is the cap): pull-up, DB row, lat pulldown. Form lever → load → near-failure last set only on 🔥, by pushing the set you have.
**High cable curl spotlight — single pulley reads 62.5 (the harder scale), cable column ~180.** Log which. Fixed upper arm parallel to the floor. 🔥 near-failure or clean pyramid up is fair game.
**Cable crunch spotlight — hips LOCKED, read the stack** (magnetic add-ons hide). 62.5 base / 66.5 comfortable / 70.5 ceiling. 🔥 last set close to failure, hips-locked is the real cap.
**Behind-back shrug stays FIRST** — protective decompression that keeps pull day flare-free.
**Lat pulldown holds 150 — don't step up.** Drill the slow controlled return; the reps clean up over weeks. 🛑
**Face pull holds the settled 50** — knuckles-up, elbows high. 🔥
**Chest-supported row holds 45 — slower eccentric is the progression**, not a load step.
**Pull-up on the straight bar** — grip's the limiter, frequency over max, no straps. 🛑
**DB row holds 70/80/90, no straps** — the strong side can creep toward ~99; grip is the cap. 🛑
**Left bicep first, every set** — the left lags on the last incline-curl sets.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, permanent every gym day.**
Rest: shrug 60s, 2.5 min pull-ups, 90s DB block, 2 min lat pulldown, 90s face pull, 75s finisher.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state pull week with the protective shrug leading. The spotlights drill the two isolations that get to run hot — the high cable curl (honest on the single-pulley scale you actually use) and the cable crunch (hips locked, load honest) — because those are exactly the safe lifts where a near-failure last set or a clean pyramid up belongs. The heavy pulls (pull-up, DB row, lat pulldown) stay grip- and form-capped, no straps, because on those 'failure' just means the hands quit. Both shoulders pain-free; grip is the honest ceiling. Building decades, not weeks.

name: Week 20 Push — Steady State (Spotlight: Incline DB Press + Kinesis Fly)
description: Loads hold where they've settled; the work is rest discipline + depth of execution. **Warmup reminder:** arm circles → Yuri's band shoulder warmup → bottoms-up press (18lb, 8/side, forward + T-plane, T-plane light) → light Kinesis-fly chest opener → internal core fist rotation → push-up → pull-up greasing set → protective behind-back shrug. Spotlights cycle forward to the incline DB press (now 50, building reps toward a clean 12 across) and the Kinesis fly (the step-forward ROM progression is the lever). Push press holds 45 on the FULL 2 min rest that W19 confirmed unlocked it — an optional 47.5 nudge if you pull it. Lateral raise holds 15. New this week: each lift is tagged 🔥 (near-failure last set OK) or 🛑 (the cue is the cap) so you decide before the set, not mid-set.

dayOverview.theme: Steady state — loads hold, the work is rest discipline + depth. Spotlight cycles to the incline DB press (50 confirmed W19 with big headroom — build reps toward 12 across) + the Kinesis fly (step forward to deepen the stretch). Push press holds 45 on the full 2 min rest. Shoulder's the best it's been ('weakness, not pain') — bank the headroom, don't spend it.

spotlights.why: Cycles forward — W19 the step to 50 landed clean: rode 50 for all three sets (not the 50/45/45 fallback), reps reset to 10/10 as predicted, and the last set to failure was 17. Big headroom. Spotlight drills the pack-down + the vertical-forearm setup so the front shoulder stays protected while the reps build toward a clean 12 across — reps are the runway here, not more load.

Cycles forward — the loaded pec stretch the right shoulder reads as relief, and the free progression is ROM, not load. Spotlight drills the fixed-elbow 'hug a tree' + the STEP-FORWARD-to-deepen lever (W19 find) + the slow 3s eccentric, so the stretch gets deeper without ever chasing the stack.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W18 dips + cable block · W19 push press + lateral raise · W20 incline DB + Kinesis fly (current) · W21 cycle forward — dips + farmer carry refresh.
watchpoints: **🔥/🛑 intensity tags — decide before the set.** 🔥 near-failure last set OK (safe isolation): lateral raise, cable lateral raise, cable tri ext, straight-arm pulldown. 🛑 keep it shy, the cue is the cap (shoulder/press-loaded): push press, incline DB, dips, Kinesis fly. Farmer carry: grip caps it — set the bells down when grip gives. **Order:** form lever first (tempo/ROM), load second, near-failure last set only on the 🔥 lifts — and by pushing the existing last set, not adding a round.

**Incline DB spotlight — 50 is the working pair now; build the reps.** W19 was 10/10/17-to-failure — the reps rebuild toward a clean 12 across all three sets, THEN the next nudge is earned. The pack-down cue is the stop sign: shrug-up-to-finish = too heavy for the cue, back to 45. 🛑 — don't chase failure here (the front delt + right shoulder); the 17 was a one-time headroom check, not the plan.

**Kinesis fly spotlight — step forward to deepen, don't add load.** Kinesis 9; the ROM-as-progression lever is stepping forward into a deeper stretch (W19 find). Slow 3s eccentric, fixed soft elbow — 🛑 the deep loaded stretch is the point, control not failure.

**Push press holds 45 on the FULL 2 min rest.** W19 confirmed the full rest made 45 'very easy, all sets' — the rest was the lever, not the load. An optional 47.5 is earned IF you pull it; otherwise hold 45 and keep the rest honest. 🛑 (overhead) — reps/quality, never a grind.
**Bottoms-up press stays in the warmup** — 18lb, 8/side, forward press + T-press, T-plane lighter. Rotator-cuff prep before pressing; bail to forward-only if the shoulder talks.
**Light Kinesis-fly opener stays in the warmup** — a few easy tree-hugger reps to open the chest; primes, doesn't fatigue. The working fly (spotlight) is later.
**Run push press first when the rack's free** — fresh shoulders for the heavy overhead lift.
**Mini-dip warmup stays on the dip station** — lean on the bar, a few mini-dips warm the shoulder and 'crack' the same spot the protective shrug does. Pre-dip ritual.
**Pack DOWN, not up** — push press, lateral raise, incline DB, dips, farmer carry all carry the cue. A lockout that needs a shrug = the load's too heavy for the cue.
**Cable block lists per-equipment numbers (column / rope pulley / Kinesis)** — pick what's free, log the equipment + number.
**Day is at capacity — no adds.** Anterior delt is covered three ways (push press + incline + dips). Shoulder's been the best report in a while — bank the headroom.

sets.name: Warmup + Shoulder Rehab (Non-Negotiable) + Bottoms-Up Cuff Prep + Chest Opener + Pull-Up Greasing + Protective Shrug

exercises.notes: Slow, big circles. Wake up scap glide before loading.
Full sequence with red band. Non-negotiable on push day.

**LOAD:** 18lb. Rotator-cuff prep before pressing — bell inverted/balanced over a vertical forearm, grip HARD, shoulder packed. **8/side in two planes:** forward press (straight overhead) + T-press (out toward a T at shoulder height). **Keep the T-plane lighter** — the abducted-and-loaded angle is the one the right shoulder likes least; bail to forward-only if it talks.

**Light loosening opener — NOT a working set** (the working fly is the spotlight later). Light load: 'hug a tree' forward, then let the cables pull the arms open into the pec stretch. Primes the chest before pressing; quick and easy, doesn't fatigue.
Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension. Wakes the grip and shoulder line before loading.
Ribs down, glutes tight, body in one line. Slow eccentric, 1s pause with chest 1-2" off the floor.

**Pull-up greasing set.** 1 fresh set, slow tempo, NOT to failure. Active hang start, pull elbows down to ribs, chest leads. Frequency over max effort — drop to scapular-pulls if the shoulder talks, and finish the count.

**Protective shrug (greasing set).** 1 light set, DBs held behind the body, palms back. Pack the shoulders DOWN and BACK, shrug UP and slightly back, 1s peak squeeze, slow down. The 'opposite movement' that decompresses the right shoulder — costs no time, easy to forget.

sets.name: Push Press (3 Sets at 45, Run First, FULL 2 Min Rest) 🛑

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 45lb DBs per side (optional 47.5 if you pull it — earned, not required). 3 sets of 8-10. Run first when the rack's open.

**REST: a FULL 2 minutes between sets** — W19 confirmed this made 45 'very easy, all sets.' The rest is the lever; keep it honest.

**🛑 The cue is the cap — no grinding to failure on the overhead lift.**
- **Ribs DOWN before the dip** — catch any rib flare on set 1
- **Shallow dip ~3-4"**, straight down through the heels — the drive comes from the legs
- **Vertical DB path** — DBs travel up next to the ears, head pokes through at the top
- **Pack DOWN, not up** at the lockout — if it needs a shrug, the load's too heavy for the cue
- Explosive drive up, controlled descent.

sets.name: 🔆 Incline DB Press (Spotlight — 50 Working, Build Reps Toward 12) 🛑

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 50 pair (the new working weight — W19 rode 50 all three sets, reps 10/10, last-set-to-failure 17). Fast-up / controlled-down, 1s pause at the bottom. **REST: a FULL ~2 min between sets.**

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — build the reps at 50, pack-down protected:**
- **The rep-build IS the progression** — chase a clean 12 across all three sets before the next load nudge; the failure-set 17 was a one-time headroom check, not the weekly plan
- **Bench at 30°**, not 45° — steeper biases front delt over upper chest
- **Shoulders packed back AND down** — pin the back of the shoulder into the bench, hold it the whole set
- **Forearm stacked vertically over the elbow at the bottom** — keeps the load off the front of the shoulder
- **Elbows ~45° from torso**, not flared to 90°
- **1s pause at the bottom**, press to a fingerwidth apart at the top
- **🛑 Pack-down is the stop sign** — if you shrug UP to finish a rep, it's too heavy for the cue; back to 45. The front delt's loaded and the right shoulder's still 'weakness not pain,' so the cue wins over the number — never grind this to failure.

**Reflection:** do all three sets hold a clean 12 with the pack-down intact, or does set 3 start needing a shrug? Clean 12 across is the green light for the next nudge; a shrug is the honest cap.

sets.name: Dips — Chest-Bias / Lean-Forward (3 Sets, Mini-Dip Warmup First) 🛑

exercises.notes:
**LOAD / EQUIPMENT (pick by how the shoulder feels, log which):**
- **Bodyweight parallel-bar dips** (default) — 3 sets of 8-12 (W18 clean 10/10/8, full ROM, no shoulder complaint)
- **Supported / assisted dip machine** if the front shoulder talks
- **Band-assisted** if the machine's taken

**Mini-dip warmup FIRST:** lean on the bar and do a few mini-dips — warms the shoulder and 'cracks' the same spot the protective shrug does. Pre-dip ritual.
- **Lean the torso forward ~15-30°, elbows flare slightly** — shifts load onto the chest (legs fold back behind you for the lean)
- **Pack the shoulders DOWN and BACK at the top** — never shrug up; pack-down is the whole game on dips
- **Controlled descent ~2s, drive up to a soft lockout** — 🛑 going past ~10 clean reps is the honest ceiling; bodyweight reps creep on their own, no need to grind
- **Front-pec watch:** pressure at the bottom stretch is expected; if it tips to PAIN, shorten the depth or move to the supported machine.

**LOAD:** 15lb DBs. 3 sets of 15-18. W19 'also easy, did all sets' — the floor's risen here.
- **Lead with the elbow, hand passive** — the wrist follows the elbow, the hand never lifts first
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED** through the whole rep
- **Stop at shoulder height — never higher** (higher just shrugs the traps off the medial delt)
- **2s eccentric** — the slow descent is the stimulus
- **🔥 Fair game for a near-failure LAST set** — this is a safe isolation, so take set 3 to ~0-1 in the tank if it still feels easy at 15; push the set you have, don't add a round. Scap reset between sets keeps the right shoulder quiet.

sets.name: 🔆 Kinesis Cable Fly (Spotlight — Step Forward to Deepen) 🛑

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** Kinesis 9.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — ROM is the progression, not the stack:**
- **STEP FORWARD to deepen the stretch** (W19 find) — that's the lever; a step forward makes it harder than more load ever would
- **Slight forward hinge at the hips** — chest leads, not the head
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED throughout** — these are NOT presses; the elbow angle never changes
- **'Hug a tree'** — the squeeze comes from the chest, not the arms pulling together
- **Stop a fistwidth apart at the top** — don't crash the handles
- **Slow eccentric (~3s)** — let the cables pull the arms into the deep pec stretch; the right shoulder/pec reads this loaded stretch as relief
- **🛑 Control-capped, not failure** — protect the deep stretch, own the eccentric; never grind a loaded fly.

**Reflection:** can you step a little further forward than last week and still own the slow eccentric? Deeper stretch with control is the win — the stack stays at 9.

sets.name: Cable Block — Lat Raise → Tri Ext → Straight-Arm Pulldown (Per-Equipment Numbers, 3 Rounds) 🔥

exercises.notes:
**LOAD (pick what's free, log which):** Cable column **30** (the pain-free home) · regular pulley D-handle at ankle height **10** · Kinesis **5-6**. 3 rounds, one arm at a time.
- **Lead with the elbow as a DIRECTION** — the elbow points, doesn't bend
- **Soft elbow ~10°, FIXED**; stand sideways, working arm farther from the stack
- **Stop at shoulder height — higher = traps**; 2s eccentric, fight the cable down.
- **🔥 Safe isolation — the last round can ride close to failure if it's easy.**

**LOAD (pick what's free, log which):** Cable column **70** (default) · rope pulley **~35** · Kinesis **5**. 3 rounds. **Always kneeling — no bench at this station; the forward torso lean IS the 'incline.'**
- **Kneel facing AWAY from the high pulley**, rope overhead; **elbows PINNED** — only the forearms move
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the rope pull the hands behind the head; stop just shy of lockout, slow eccentric
- Set 1 feels easy, set 3 is brutal — that shape is the lift working. **🔥 Ride set 3 close to failure if you want the extra stimulus.**

**LOAD (pick what's free, log which):** Cable column **120** · rope pulley **50** · Kinesis **6**. 3 rounds.
- **Stand a step back, hinge ~15° at the hips** — fixed hinge, torso doesn't pump; slight elbow bend (~5°), FIXED
- **Pull the bar to the thighs, NOT past** — past = shoulders roll forward, lats switch off; squeeze the lats hard ('oranges into the back pockets')
- **Slow controlled return to a full overhead stretch.** Runs last — reps may fall on later sets; that's honest. **🔥 Isolation-ish — a hard last set is fine.**

sets.notes: Cable block — sharp cues, 3 rounds, one trip to the chosen station covers all three. Column is the default; the pulley numbers are the fallback when the column's taken. Pick what's free and log it.

sets.name: Farmer Carry (3 Walks — Grip Caps It)

exercises.equipment: DB rack
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 50lb DBs. 3 walks of ~45-60s each — chase hold-time.
- **Stand TALL** — ribs down, crown reaching up, no leaning back
- **Shoulders pulled DOWN and BACK** — into the back pockets, never shrugged; the tall packed posture doubles as right-shoulder decompression
- **Neck long, eyes forward** — no chin poke
- **Grip firm but NOT death-clenched** — grip is the limiter (it taps before the shoulder). Set the bells down when grip fails rather than white-knuckling. No straps — train the grip.
- **Walk a straight line at a deliberate pace**, breathing steadily.

sets.notes: Trap-chain + grip block. 3 walks at 50lb — packed-shoulder posture, grip as the honest edge. Set them down when grip gives, not before.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow position. Pec minor lengthen — the antagonist to the upper-trap chain loaded all session.
Passive hang from the pull-up bar. **Don't engage** — let the shoulders unpack and the spine decompress.
30s each side on the mat. Draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
45s each side. Front leg + back leg at 90°. Sink the hips toward the floor — hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Knees wide, arms extended forward. Parasympathetic shift before leaving the gym.

sets.notes: 5 minutes of recovery work, non-negotiable closing block.

tips: **🔥/🛑 intensity tags this week — decide before the set.** 🔥 (near-failure last set OK): lateral raise, cable lateral raise, cable tri ext, straight-arm pulldown. 🛑 (the cue is the cap): push press, incline DB, dips, Kinesis fly. Farmer carry: grip caps it. Form lever → load → near-failure last set only on 🔥, by pushing the set you have.

**Incline DB spotlight — 50 is the working pair; build the reps toward a clean 12 across before the next nudge.** Pack-down is the stop sign. The W19 failure-set 17 was a headroom check, not the plan.
**Kinesis fly spotlight — step forward to deepen the stretch** (ROM is the progression, not the stack). Slow 3s eccentric, fixed elbow.
**Push press holds 45 on the FULL 2 min rest** (W19 confirmed the rest was the unlock). Optional 47.5 if you pull it.
**Bottoms-up press in the warmup** — 18lb, 8/side, forward + T-plane, T-plane light. Rotator-cuff prep.
**Lateral raise holds 15** — floor's risen ('also easy' W19); 🔥 a near-failure last set is fair game.
**Mini-dip warmup stays on the dip station** — warms + 'cracks' the shoulder/front-pec spot.
**Run push press first when the rack's free** — fresh shoulders.
**Pack DOWN, not up** — every press + the carry carries the cue.
**Cable block per-equipment numbers** — column 30/70/120; rope pulley 10/35/50; Kinesis 5-6. Pick what's free, log it.
**Farmer carry: 50lb, chase hold-time** — grip is the edge, no straps.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, permanent every gym day.**
**Day is at capacity — no adds.** Rest: 2 min push press + incline + dips, 90s lateral raise + Kinesis fly + farmer carry, 75s cable block.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state push week — gains come from rest discipline and sharper execution at established loads, not heavier bells. The spotlights drill the incline DB press (building the reps at the confirmed 50) and the Kinesis fly (deepening the loaded stretch via ROM, not load). New this week: the 🔥/🛑 tags make the intensity intent explicit — near-failure is a tool for the safe isolations, while the shoulder-loaded presses stay governed by the pack-down cue. Both spotlights feed the same still-improving shoulder ('weakness, not pain' now). Building decades, not weeks.

referenceText:
REDDIT RECOMMENDED ROUTINE (RRR)
— r/bodyweightfitness Wiki —

GOALS
This routine covers strength, hypertrophy/muscle gain (with proper diet), and fat loss (with proper diet). It's a general-purpose full-body program.

EQUIPMENT NEEDED
• A pull-up bar (monkey bars, doorframe bar, rings, etc.)
• A place to do rows (low bar, rings, sturdy table, or even a knotted bedsheet in a door) — this is non-negotiable
• Parallel bars for dips (kitchen counter corners, two sturdy chairs, etc.) — alternatives exist if you truly can't find any

HOW PROGRESSIONS WORK
• Each exercise has a chain of variations from easy to hard (e.g., wall push-up → incline → knee → full → diamond → pseudo-planche)
• Pick the variation where you can do 3 sets of 5 reps with good form
• Each session, try to add 1 rep per set until you reach 3 sets of 8 reps
• Once you hit 3×8 with good form, move to the next harder variation at 3×5
• You only perform ONE exercise from each progression per session — drop the easier one
• For isometric holds (support hold, tuck front lever, etc.): hold 10-30 seconds per set, advance when you hit 3×30s

WARMUP (5-10 min)
  Reps     Exercise                          Notes
  5-10     Yuri's Shoulder Band Warmup        Alternative: stick/towel dislocates
  5-10     Squat Sky Reaches                  Can be done assisted
  10+      GMB Wrist Prep                     Do as many reps as you want
  30s      Deadbugs                           Core activation
  10       Arch Hangs                         Add after you reach negative pull-ups
  30s      Support Hold                       Add after you reach negative dips
  10       Easier Squat Progression            Add after you reach Bulgarian split squats
  10       Easier Hinge Progression            Add after you reach banded Nordic curls

STRENGTH WORK STRUCTURE (40-60 min)
Done as supersets — alternate between the two exercises in each pair.

  Pair 1: Pull-ups & Squats
    3×5-8 Pull-up progression ↔ 3×5-8 Squat progression

  Pair 2: Dips & Hinges
    3×5-8 Dip progression ↔ 3×5-8 Hinge progression

  Pair 3: Rows & Push-ups
    3×5-8 Row progression ↔ 3×5-8 Push-up progression

  Core Triplet
    3×8-12 Anti-Extension ↔ 3×8-12 Anti-Rotation ↔ 3×8-12 Extension (60s rest between each)

HOW PAIRING WORKS
Do a set of exercise A, rest 90s, do a set of exercise B, rest 90s, repeat 3 times. This gives each muscle ~3 min total recovery between its own sets while keeping the workout efficient. For the core triplet, use 60s rest between each of the 3 exercises.

Example:
  Pull-ups → rest 90s → Squats → rest 90s →
  Pull-ups → rest 90s → Squats → rest 90s →
  Pull-ups → rest 90s → Squats → rest 90s →
  move to next pair

REST TIME
90s between exercises is the baseline. If you're dropping reps (e.g., 8 on set 1 but only 5-6 on set 2), extend rest up to 3 minutes. Quality reps matter more than speed.

TEMPO
All exercises use 10X0 tempo: 1 second on the way down, no pause at bottom, explode up (intent matters even if the actual movement is slow), no pause at top.

REP STRATEGY
Stay 1 rep short of failure. If your max is 8 reps, do 7-7-7 instead of 8-6-5. Going to failure on early sets kills your volume on later sets, which reduces total work and slows progress.

BARBELL INTEGRATION (Optional)
If you have access to a barbell and squat rack, you can swap in barbell work for the lower body progressions after mastering the basics:
• Replace squat progression with barbell squats: 3×5
• Workouts 1 & 3 of the week: replace hinge progression with Romanian deadlifts (weighted): 3×8
• Workout 2 of the week: replace hinge progression with deadlifts: 3×5
• Result: squatting 3x/week, Romanian deadlifting 2x/week, deadlifting 1x/week
• Warm up with progressively heavier sets before your work sets

IF THE ROUTINE IS TOO MUCH
• Reduce sets to 1-2 instead of 3 (preferred modification for beginners)
• Increase rep range to 5-12 or 5-15 before progressing to the next exercise
• Reduce from 3x/week to 2x/week
• Split into upper/lower across different days (e.g., MWFSat)
• Start with just 3 exercises: squat progression + push-ups + rows

TIMELINE FOR RESULTS
• Performance improvements: 2-3 workouts in
• Visible to yourself: 4-6 weeks (with proper diet)
• Visible to others: 12+ weeks (with proper diet)

WHEN TO MOVE ON
Move to an intermediate routine when you plateau for weeks despite good diet, sleep, and stress management. Or when you exhaust all progressions. The r/bodyweightfitness community recommends developing your own intermediate routine based on the programming principles you'll learn along the way.

name: What is Heavy Duty Training?
description: An educational introduction to Mike Mentzer's Heavy Duty system. Learn the principles before starting the program. This explains WHY you train less but harder.

exercises.name: The Man Behind Heavy Duty
exercises.notes: Mike Mentzer (1951-2001) was a champion bodybuilder and philosopher of training. He won the 1978 Mr. Universe with a perfect score. After competing, he developed Heavy Duty - a training system based on scientific principles and logic, not gym bro science.

exercises.name: Train HARDER, Not Longer
exercises.notes: The stimulus for muscle growth is INTENSITY - how hard you train, not how much. One set taken to true muscular failure stimulates growth just as well as 3-5 sets. More sets just add fatigue without additional benefit.

exercises.name: What 'Failure' Really Means
exercises.notes: FAILURE means you cannot complete another rep with proper form, no matter how hard you try. Not 'this is getting hard' - true failure. When you reach this point, you've triggered the adaptive response. Anything beyond is unnecessary.

sets.name: Principle 3: Recovery is Where Growth Happens

exercises.name: You Don't Grow in the Gym
exercises.notes: Training damages muscle. RECOVERY is when you grow. Most people overtrain - they return to the gym before fully recovering, making zero progress. Heavy Duty prescribes 4-7+ days between training the same muscle. Sounds crazy? Try it.

exercises.name: Tire the Target Muscle First
exercises.notes: Problem: On bench press, your triceps often fail before your chest. Solution: Pre-exhaust. Do an isolation exercise (pec fly) immediately before the compound (bench). Your chest is pre-fatigued, so it fails first during the press.

exercises.name: The Only Way to Know It's Working
exercises.notes: If you're getting stronger (more weight or more reps), you're growing. If not, something's wrong - usually overtraining. Log every workout. Add weight when you hit the top of your rep range. Small increments add up to big gains.

exercises.name: Slow and Controlled
exercises.notes: 4 seconds lifting (concentric), 2 second squeeze at contraction, 4 seconds lowering (eccentric). No bouncing, no momentum. This ensures the muscle does ALL the work and maximizes time under tension. If you can't control it, it's too heavy.

exercises.name: How Often to Train
exercises.notes: BEGINNER: Full body 2x/week (e.g., Mon/Thu). INTERMEDIATE: 2-way split, each 1x/week. Day 1: Chest/Back. Day 2: Legs/Shoulders/Arms. ADVANCED: Consolidation routine 1x every 5-7 days. Yes, really. More rest = more growth.

name: KB B-Stance Flow (@Asgooch)
description: Unilateral kettlebell flow: B-stance swing → swing clean → B-stance squat → split stance snatch → OH lunge. 5 reps each side, 5 rounds. Don't put the bell down. Video: https://x.com/Asgooch/status/2026011472489324584

sets.name: B-Stance Flow

exercises.notes: B-stance: one foot back, heel up. Swing between legs, explosive hip drive. Bell swings up to about chest height.
→ On the next swing, CATCH it directly into rack position at your shoulder. Don't dead stop — ride the momentum into the clean.
→ Bell is in rack. Stay in B-stance (back foot heel still up). Squat down and stand back up. Bell stays at shoulder.
→ From rack, punch the bell straight overhead in one motion. Lock out arm, stand tall. Split stance snatch — you're still in B-stance when it goes up.
→ Bell locked out overhead, step forward into a lunge. Stand straight up from the lunge with arm STILL locked overhead. That's 1 rep of the full flow.

sets.notes: 5 reps each side × 5 rounds. Don't put the bell down between moves — one continuous chain. Each rep flows: swing → catch into rack → squat → punch overhead → lunge → stand up with arm locked.

All same arm, don't put the bell down until you switch sides.
The swing clean is catching a full swing into rack — control the momentum.

name: Dead Cluster Flow — Dead Cluster → Snatch → Iron Cross → Outside Pendulum → Tactical Clean → Reverse Lunge → Offset Rack Squat
description: A full-body single-bell kettlebell flow from a Madeleine Conti reel (her '2nd most saved & shared kettlebell flow of 2025') — the ballistic, overhead cousin to the Leggy Flow (kb-leggy-flow). Where the Leggy Flow stays at the rack and works the legs laterally, this one goes overhead: a dead cluster from the floor, a snatch, an iron-cross lateral hold, an outside pendulum swing, then a tactical clean into a reverse lunge and an offset rack squat. Run the whole sequence on one side, then the other. Overhead-heavy — go LIGHT and mind the right shoulder on the snatch, cluster press, and iron cross.
flowNotes: **This is a continuous FLOW, not separate stations.** Move through the whole chain on ONE side — dead cluster → snatch → iron cross → outside pendulum → inside tactical clean → reverse lunge → offset rack squat — letting each move feed the next, then repeat on the other side. Single LIGHT-to-MEDIUM bell; quality and continuity over load. Unlike the Leggy Flow, this one is **overhead-heavy** (dead cluster press, snatch, iron cross) — keep the load conservative and mind the right shoulder: pack the shoulder down on every overhead beat, and regress or skip the iron cross if it flares. The cleans, snatch, and pendulum come from the legs and hips, not the arm. 3 rounds each side.

flowSequence.notes: Dead clean off the floor → front squat → drive up into a press to overhead, then lower to the rack and set the bell down dead for the next rep. Legs clean it, legs squat it, legs drive the press — no grinding the press from the shoulder.

One continuous snatch — hinge and hike the bell back, snap the hips to send it up in a tight arc, punch the hand through so the bell lands SOFTLY on the forearm overhead. Hips drive it, not the arm; the smooth catch protects the shoulder and wrist.

Straight-arm raise the bell out to the side to shoulder height — a 'T' / crucifix hold. Shoulder packed DOWN (not shrugged), arm parallel to the floor, brief hold. Big straight-arm shoulder load — go light, back off if the right shoulder complains.

Single-arm swing on an outside, pendulum arc — out and around the working hip, driven by the legs. Brace the core so the torso doesn't twist toward the bell; let it float at the top and pendulum back.
Smooth, controlled clean threading the bell to the rack — the 'inside' path, no momentum yank, no forearm bang. Sets up the lunge and squat that follow.
Bell stays racked. Step the trailing leg straight back, both knees to ~90°, torso tall, drive through the front heel to stand. The offset rack load makes the core fight the pull to the loaded side.
Bell racked on the one side, squat — chest tall, racked elbow up, resist the pull toward the loaded side, full depth, drive up through the whole foot. Closes the flow before switching sides.

tips: This is a FLOW — the seven moves connect seamlessly, no pausing between them. Smooth, controlled transitions are the point.
Single LIGHT-to-MEDIUM bell — movement quality and continuity over load. The cleans, snatch, and pendulum are powered by the legs and hips, not the arm.
Run the full sequence on one side, then the other. 3 rounds each side is a solid dose; for a conditioning version, run 2-3 rounds/side as one set, rest 1 min, repeat for 4-5 sets.

**Overhead-heavy, unlike the Leggy Flow** — the dead cluster press, snatch, and iron cross all load the shoulder overhead / on a long lever. Pack the shoulder DOWN on every overhead beat, keep the load conservative, and regress or skip the iron cross if the right shoulder flares.
Great for full-body power, overhead stability, grip, lateral-plane conditioning, and coordination.

name: Figure-8 → Tactical Clean Complex (@kettleclubfam / kettleclubfam program)
description:
A single-bell hand-switching complex that pairs the figure-8 pass with a tactical clean. The figure-8 passes the bell between the legs and exits into a clean to rack — the pass IS the clean entry. Then a regular tactical clean back through hike and up to rack on the other side. Hand switches happen at the figure-8 pass-through. Source format: 4 sets of descending time / ascending weight pyramid (2:00 @ 12kg → 1:30 @ 16kg → 1:00 @ 20kg → 0:30 @ 24kg), rest 1:00 between sets.

**Pattern per side:**
- START: Hike position (bell between legs, hinged)
- Figure-8 → Tactical Clean (figure-8 between legs, exit-pass becomes the clean to rack)
- Tactical Clean (lower controlled, hike, re-clean to rack)
- END: Hike position
- Switch sides

The pass-through is where you switch hands; the clean is where you build skill at hand catches under load. Bell-baddie vibes.

dayOverview.theme: A figure-8 + tactical clean complex with built-in hand switches. The pass IS the clean entry — the figure-8 exits into a rack catch. Ascending-weight pyramid lets you find your skill ceiling within one session.
watchpoints: **The figure-8 exits INTO the clean — the bell doesn't return to a hand mid-pass.** Pass between legs, hand catches behind, pull becomes the clean to rack. Practice slowly before adding load.
**Tactical clean = controlled, no momentum hack.** The 'tactical' part is deliberate threading/rotation of the wrist into rack. No flopping, no banging the forearm.
**Hand catches under load are the skill.** That's why the source author programs ascending weight — heavier bell forces cleaner catch mechanics.
**Hike position is the home base.** Every transition resets through hike. If you lose the bell, get back to hike before re-starting.
**Ascending weight = descending time** on purpose. Heavier bells get less work time; lighter bells get longer flow time. Don't try to keep 12kg pace at 24kg.

exercises.notes: Light bell, warm the shoulders.
Light bell, get the pass-through pattern grooved before adding the clean.
Light bell, low wide stance. Just the pass — no clean exit yet. Get the hand-switch comfortable.
Hip hinge warm-up. Light bell.

**2 minutes of the complex** at 26lb (12kg) — or whatever your **MEDIUM bell** is per the source author's relative scale.

**Pattern (one compound move, repeated alternating sides):**
- START hike position (bell between legs, hinged)
- **Figure-8 pass exits INTO Tactical Clean to rack** on one side
- Lower bell back through hike
- Next figure-8 pass switches sides → clean to rack on the other side
- Continue alternating

**Pace yourself** — 2:00 is long. Find a sustainable rhythm. The first set is the technique set.

**90 seconds at 35lb (16kg)** — or your **MEDIUM-HEAVY bell**.
Same compound move. Heavier bell = catch mechanics matter more. Slow down before form breaks.

**60 seconds at 44lb (20kg)** — or your **HEAVY bell**.
This is where the catch under load gets real. Bell-baddie territory.

**30 seconds at 53lb (24kg)** — or your **HEAVIEST bell**.

**Note:** Arrilaga max is 50lb — 24kg is right at the ceiling. If 24kg isn't available, hold 20kg (44lb) and add 15-30s of work time to feel the load. The point of set 4 is the heaviest bell you have access to + the cleanest catches you can make at that weight.

Finish strong. Hand catches stay tight.
Light bell, decompress the shoulders.
60s each side. Hike position fries the hip flexors and glutes — pigeon resets them.
60s. Wide-stance work tightens the adductors.

tips: **The figure-8 exits INTO the clean** — that's the whole skill. Pass between legs, hand catches behind, the catch becomes the clean to rack. No 'land and re-grip.'
**Tactical clean = controlled, no momentum hack.** Threading motion into rack, not a yank.
**Ascending weight + descending time** is the source author's intentional pattern. Don't keep 12kg pace at 24kg.
**Hand catches under load** are where the skill builds. That's why the heavy sets are short.
**Hike position is home base.** Every transition resets through hike — if you lose the bell, go back to hike before re-starting.
**Light warmup first** — get the pass-through and clean grooved separately before chaining them.
**Source bell weights** (12/16/20/24kg = 26/35/44/53lb) — pick what you have access to. Arrilaga max is 50lb, so 24kg may not be available — hold 20kg longer if so.
**Cooldown matters** — hike position + figure-8 wide stance = adductor + hip flexor tightness. Pigeon + butterfly resets.
Source: @kettleclubfam (kettleclubfam program).
formPhilosophy: Skill-first KB flow with ascending load. The complex isolates the figure-8-to-clean transition — the moment when a passing pattern becomes a strength catch. Pyramid lets you find the skill ceiling within a single session: long-and-light to lock the pattern, short-and-heavy to test it under load.

sets.name: Full-Body KB Circuit

exercises.notes: Pass around the body once → squat → next pass. Torso tall and still during the pass; full depth on the squat. Alternate pass direction.
Step back to a reverse lunge → drive the back knee forward and up to a tall, balanced stand → repeat. Drive through the front heel; stay tall.
Hips drive the bell, punch the hand THROUGH at the top for a soft catch — no bang on the wrist. Right shoulder watch on the catch; sub high pulls if it crackles.
Press with the shoulder packed DOWN, lock it out, then march alternate knees keeping the bell stacked overhead. Obliques fight to keep the torso square under the offset load.

name: GymVibe 9-Minute KB AMRAP — Ballistic Row / Thruster / Reverse Lunge + Knee Drive
description: A brutal single-bell AMRAP complex from @gymvibe_: ballistic row, thruster (the source calls it a 'goblet cluster'), and reverse lunge + knee drive, run back-to-back with no rest for as many rounds as possible in 9 minutes. A strength/conditioning workout-set, NOT a flow. The source runs it at one weight (24kg/53lb); here it's a 30 → 40 → 50lb load ladder over the three thirds so you build into the top weight instead of opening on your max.

sets.name: 9-Minute AMRAP (Load Ladder: 30 → 40 → 50lb)

exercises.notes: **Ballistic row — explosive, not a slow controlled row.** Hinge at the hips, back flat, and drive the bell to the hip with power, then control it back. 8 per side. Brace the core, no torso rotation.

**Goblet squat → press in one motion (the source's 'goblet cluster').** Bell at the chest/goblet, squat to at least parallel, then drive up and use the leg momentum to press it overhead. Lock out tall, ribs down, then back into the next squat. Right-shoulder watch on the overhead — pack it down; if it won't lock out clean, this is the move to lighten first.
Step back to a reverse lunge → drive the back knee forward and up to a tall, balanced stand → repeat. Drive through the FRONT heel, stay tall. 8 per side.

sets.notes: **AMRAP — as many rounds of the three moves as possible in 9 minutes, NO rest between moves or rounds.** Single bell. **Load ladder over the three thirds:** 0:00-3:00 @ 30lb → 3:00-6:00 @ 40lb → 6:00-9:00 @ 50lb (swap the bell up at the 3- and 6-minute marks). Builds into the top weight instead of opening on your max. The thruster's overhead press is the limiter — if 50 won't press clean by the last third, hold 40 and chase rounds instead. Count total rounds + where you were when the bell got heavy.

tips: **It's a workout-set / AMRAP, not a flow** — power and breathing rate are the point, not smooth transitions.
**Load ladder 30 → 40 → 50lb** over the three 3-minute thirds — groove the pattern light, climb to the top bell. 50 is the Arrillaga ceiling; don't open there on a 9-min grinder.
**The thruster press is the limiter and the shoulder risk** — pack the shoulder down on the lockout; lighten the bell before the press gets ugly.
**Single bell throughout each third** — pick what's free, swap up at 3:00 and 6:00.
Good fit for a Tuesday strength/conditioning slot; NOT a Thursday move (too brutal the day before Friday legs).

description: A leggy single-bell kettlebell flow from a Madeleine Conti reel — the lower-body cousin of the Bent Press Flow (kb-flow-dead-clean-press). Same dead-clean entry and tactical-clean exit, but the middle is all lunge / lateral-squat work instead of front squat + bent press. Dead clean from the floor, curtsy lunge in the rack, lateral lunge swinging the bell back, clean up into a lateral squat, lateral lunge again, then step the feet together for a tactical clean. flowNotes: **This is a continuous FLOW, not separate stations.** Move through the whole chain on ONE side — dead clean → curtsy lunge → lateral lunge → lateral squat clean → lateral lunge → tactical clean — letting each move feed the next, then repeat on the other side. Single MEDIUM bell (~25-35lb); quality and continuity over load. The cleans come from the legs and hips, not the arm. 3 rounds each side.

flowSequence.notes: Dead stop on the floor, explosive pull to the rack — soft knees to catch, zero impact.
Bell stays racked. Step the trailing leg back and across, knee toward the floor, torso tall, front knee tracks the toes.
Swing the bell DOWN between the legs as you step wide — hips back, trailing leg straight. The swing-back loads the next move.
From the bottom, drive out of the lateral lunge and clean the bell to the rack as you come up into a lateral squat. Leg + hip power makes the clean — the arm just guides. Catch soft.
Swing the bell back down between the legs again — second lateral lunge, controlled.
Smooth, controlled return to the rack — closes the flow before switching sides.

tips: This is a FLOW — the six moves connect seamlessly, no pausing between them. Smooth, controlled transitions are the point.
Single MEDIUM bell — movement quality and continuity over load. The cleans and the lateral squat clean are powered by the legs and hips, not the arm.
Run the full sequence on one side, then the other. 3 rounds each side is a solid dose; for a conditioning version, run 2-3 rounds/side as one set, rest 1 min, repeat for 4-5 sets.
Curtsy lunge stays racked; the lateral lunges swing the bell down between the legs to load the next clean.
